- the following is the report by mrs piia-noora kauppi, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, on the tax treatment of losses in a crossborder context [2007/2144 (ini) ] (a6-0188/2005).
mr president, the different practices in the treatment of tax losses in different countries distort competition in the internal market, are unfair and encourage bad tax practices. we therefore welcome the commission's initiative to propose a minimum level of harmonisation of these rules, hoping that the council can converge on the same. this is an area where better regulation is needed, also to replace the legal uncertainty associated with it. this uncertainty has led to repeated recourse to the court of justice of the european communities and is a factor in increasing uncertainty in economic relations, to the detriment of enterprises and smes. it is indeed of the utmost importance to ensure that different tax practices are compatible with the effective functioning of the internal market. the quality of the report prepared by mrs kauppi has allowed a broad consensus to be reached among the main political groups on the key elements of the report. however, there are aspects of the opinion in its initial version which, being non-essential, could prevent such convergence. in particular, in the view of the socialist group, this procedure is not compatible with the open defence of tax competition practices. such practices encourage artificial movements of companies, capital and people. such movements often leave traces of social, environmental and productive disintegration. on the other hand, fiscal competition in some economies creates serious problems of macroeconomic balance with various consequences, particularly in terms of the quality and quantity of public goods made available by these countries to their citizens. the group of the european socialists believes that, on a matter of such strategic importance, it is in the best interests of the community to present to the commission and the council a position of the european parliament supported by a broad base of support. the european union still has a long way to go in this initiative, particularly in the ccctb, which has been the subject of so much discussion today, in creating a common consolidated tax base for its companies, and we must create the political conditions for this future work. we are not going to be able to achieve convergence on this report. we hope that by the time of the final vote the spirit of compromise between the main political groups will make it possible to put to good use the consensus reached on its essential messages and will not disturb the scope of the final approval, by putting to good use aspects which, although incidental in the present context, divide us politically in an insurmountable way. we must thank the active involvement of several members of the epp group in particular, including your rapporteur, for their spirit of commitment and their spirit of openness, which has enabled us to reach a position which we hope will be consensual on the essential points of this report. thank you very much, mr president.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on tuesday, 15 january 2008.
the following is the report by mr paolo costa, on behalf of the committee on transport and tourism, on the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation amending regulation no 11 on the elimination of discrimination in transport prices and conditions in implementation of article 79 (3) of the treaty establishing the european economic community and regulation (ec) no 852/2004 of the european parliament and of the council on the hygiene of foodstuffs - transport aspects (com (2007) 0090 - c6-0086/2007 - 2007/0037a (cod)).
mr president, in this one-minute speech i would like to highlight the amendments we have tabled with the aim of explicitly taking into account in this directive the constraints imposed on regions suffering from permanent geographical and natural handicaps, such as the outermost regions, in particular in accordance with the provisions of article 299 (2) of the treaty. we believe that the directive should explicitly recognise the importance of airports for the socioeconomic development of these regions and for territorial cohesion and that appropriate exceptions should therefore be laid down in the directive. the proposal that the rules laid down in the directive should not apply to airports in these regions unless they guarantee the fulfilment of universal public service obligations, for which we hope to have your support, is therefore a proposal.
travel within and to europe is increasing, but it is becoming more and more expensive to travel in and to our continent. the factors that are causing this increase in prices, such as the increase in oil prices, security costs and the reduction of co2 emissions, are persistent and very likely to continue. in this context, we must aim to stimulate a genuinely competitive airport market, which can only be viable where there is transparency and predictability. these are, i believe, the main virtues of this proposal for a directive, to the drafting of which our colleague mr stockmann has made a major contribution. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment against pollution from industrial sources. the commission has also proposed that the commission should be able to adopt a proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the protection of employees in the event of the insolvency of their employer. the commission notes that the airport services agreement with ryanair was signed on 28 june 2012 and that the agreement was signed on 27 june 2012. the establishment of an independent national regulatory body, which will only intervene in the event of a final disagreement on a decision on airport charges, also contributes to the smooth functioning of the market. finally, mr president, i would like to conclude by saying that the definition of criteria for transparency and rigour in the use of fees for prefinancing new airport infrastructure projects is at the same time in the public interest of airport development and new airport infrastructure and also in the interests of passengers, that is to say, consumers, whose interests must be given our primary attention.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i thank and congratulate mr ulrich stockmann for his openness and ability to promote compromise between the various interests involved in the preparation of this very good report, particularly on the outermost regions. i support the lines of the commission proposal and i support this report because it guarantees the non-discrimination of airport charges, except where it is compatible and necessary in the light of the treaty, in particular with regard to the provisions relating to the outermost regions, and there must be a mandatory procedure for consultation between managing bodies and users. that any discrimination in fees will be transparent and based on clear criteria, taking into account the principle of territorial cohesion in the long term. our proposal is that future changes will be possible for objective and transparent reasons of general interest, in particular as regards universal access. that member states ensure, and i quote, 'that airports charge the same fare for the same service, and that airport users may be granted discounts on the fare based on the quality of a service used, provided that all airport users can benefit from that discount on public, transparent and objective conditions, may also grant discounts to users opening new routes in accordance with competition law... in this minute of intervention i would like to stress that we believe that the first priority of the european union in relation to children should be to assess the consequences of its policies for the failure to fulfil or the fulfilment of children's rights, in particular with regard to the rapid and significant reduction of child poverty by giving all children equal opportunities. in this sense, and for example, i ask: what are the consequences of the european union's monetary policy and its objective of price stability, or rather wage moderation, for the failure to respect the rights of the child? what are the consequences of the european union's so-called flexicurity, the liberalisation of the labour market, the facilitation of dismissals, the precariousness of employment relationships, the increase in working time and the flexibility of working hours for the failure to respect the rights of children? what are the consequences of the current european union policies promoting the liberalisation and privatisation of public services including health and education for the failure to respect children's rights? here are some examples of what would be the most appropriate, necessary and urgent european union mainstreaming of children's rights.

community legislation prohibiting all forms of violence, whether physical, psychological or sexual. i have already referred to the 2003 unicef figures, which show that in some community countries, in writing. - although it contains some aspects which improve the commission's proposal, the report is nevertheless imbued with and an integral part of the process of liberalising air transport in the eu. the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the transparency of airport charges. however, we disagree with any policy which seeks to liberalise and privatise a strategic public service such as air transport, in this case promoting 'a truly competitive airport market' or integrating principles such as user-pays and profitability into a service which should be public. in fact, the so-called 'regulatory role' of the public sector is even being removed by the creation of 'independent regulatory bodies'. the privatisation experiments in the sector have not generated any added value in the services provided, they have encouraged the destruction of jobs and the degradation of workers' rights and, in some cases, technical and operational problems. we regret the rejection of our proposals to include in the directive the recognition of the constraints faced by regions suffering from permanent geographical and natural handicaps, such as the outermost regions, and to establish appropriate exceptions for the fulfilment of universal public service obligations.
in writing. − the rotterdam convention on the prior information and consent procedure for certain hazardous chemicals and pesticides in international trade was adopted in september 1998 and entered into force on 24 february 2004. regulation (ec) no 304/2003 on the export and import of dangerous chemicals gives effect to the rotterdam convention. the commission considered it necessary to bring an action against the council and the european parliament before the court of justice for not agreeing to the change in the legal basis (environment instead of common commercial policy). in its judgment of 10 january 2006, the court of justice annulled the regulation because it was to have a dual legal basis: article 133 and article 175 (1) of the treaty and ruled that the effects of that regulation would be maintained until the adoption of a new regulation based on the appropriate legal bases. the european commission has put forward a new proposal for a regulation based on the above-mentioned dual legal basis. in today's first reading vote, the european parliament approved a number of amendments to the commission proposal which will now be negotiated with the council. that is why we voted in favour.
in writing. − the european automotive industry, which accounts for around 3% of eu gdp and 7% of industrial output in the union, is one of the most important economic sectors producing around one third of world output. it is also one of the eu's main export sectors, with r & d investment equivalent to 4% of its turnover. the sector is one of the largest employers, with over 2 million direct jobs and 10 million indirect jobs, and is a key factor in europe's economic, social and cultural life. but the sector faces serious challenges. rapid technological progress, coupled with fierce international competition, is driving rapid change. in addition, this sector is subject to significant social expectations, particularly in terms of the environment and road safety. this close interaction between industry, the environment, energy and transport results in one of the most regulated areas in the eu, covered by some 80 directives and 115 unece regulations. however, not all the proposals in this report deserve our support. there is too much emphasis on defending the internal market and competition and too little attention to social and labour aspects and the different levels of development in the member states.
in writing. − the future competitiveness of the european automotive sector is of the utmost importance and therefore the eu's efforts should continue to follow a long-term logic, organised around investments in research and development, improving the functioning of the internal market through the necessary legislation and simplifying administrative procedures, thus making them less costly and faster. the report's guidelines point to an integrated environmental approach, combining new engine technologies, the use of cleaner fuels and additional efforts in the field of traffic management, driving behaviour and infrastructure, to further reduce greenhouse gas emissions. i consider these aspects to be fundamental and the financing of the necessary investments should focus on public-private partnerships as a new instrument for industrial research and technological development. finally, there is the international dimension, which requires urgent measures to improve access to markets, particularly asian markets, through multilateral negotiations and bilateral trade agreements. i therefore voted in favour of the report on the cars21 initiative.
in writing. - unfortunately, the amendments tabled by our group, including some positions opposed to those which were finally adopted, were rejected. this was the case with the opinion on the decision of the court of justice of the european communities in the marks & spencer case, which constitutes an excessive interference with the right of member states to avoid weakening their tax systems. in cross-border situations, tax competence should be distributed equitably between the member states concerned, avoiding double compensation of losses and risks of tax evasion. it also considers that there is a risk that, by allowing cross-border loss compensation, companies may tend to ensure that their profits are taxed in countries with low rates rather than in those with high rates. the possibility of compensating for cross-border losses can therefore only be justified in the case of genuinely interconnected parts of the same undertaking or, in other words, when those parts are economically and organisationally integrated. above all, the conditions for adequate and equitable taxation, which prevents tax evasion, which also ensures the functioning of public services and a fairer distribution of income, must be safeguarded.
in writing. - the report adopted by the committee on employment takes up important aspects of the fight for better living and working conditions, with greater protection of health and safety, but unfortunately, on the proposal of the ppe, several proposals were amended and paragraph 59 was rejected, which underlined that permanent employment is an important factor for health and safety at work. hence our final vote of abstention. parliament was concerned that the number of occupational accidents and diseases was not decreasing uniformly, given that certain categories of workers (e.g. migrants, precarious workers, women, young and elderly workers) and certain member states had rates of occupational accidents and diseases far above the eu average, and called on the commission to give priority in its strategy to activities and/or sectors involving particular risks. however, it is positive that the paragraph has been adopted which considers that excessive working hours and insufficient rest periods are a key factor in the increase in the levels of accidents and illnesses at work and calls for a proper balance between work and family life.
in writing. the slovenian presidency will continue to follow closely the agenda of the german presidency, giving priority to the ratification of the treaty of lisbon, as was clear in the debate, and as is expressly stated in its programme. we know that the political elites in the european union want the treaty to be ratified by all the member states before the 2009 elections. that is why they are pressing hard for no referendums, except in ireland, where they are constitutionally binding, making clear their understanding of democracy and bringing citizens closer together: only when they are not at risk of citizens speaking out against their views and interests. then, what they call the "second cycle of the lisbon strategy" appears as a high priority, to deepen liberalizations and attacks on public services, social and labour rights. we are also concerned that the developments in kosovo will be another threat to peace and development in europe with a possible unilateral declaration of independence. however, the serious social problems of unemployment, precarious work, poverty and the worsening of social and territorial inequalities remain unresolved. we will continue to fight for a break with these neoliberal policies and for another europe of social justice, peace and social progress.
in writing. the slovenian presidency of the council marks the beginning of the third act in the farce orchestrated by the forces promoting federalist, neoliberal and militarist integration in europe, namely the eu - with germany in the lead - to impose a previously rejected treaty by avoiding national referendums. they say that there is no justification for holding referendums: - because there is a 'broad consensus' in each country on the proposed treaty, particularly in national parliaments. but one of the main lessons of the referendums in france and the netherlands was that they brought to light the profound contradiction between the popular will and the so-called 'parliamentary majorities'. - because ratification by parliaments is as legitimate and democratic as ratification by referendum. but how can we understand the claim that holding a referendum in portugal would increase the risks of the treaty not coming into force? what they fear is that the outcome of a referendum will be different from what they want, so they don't hold them. - because the proposed treaty is different from the one previously rejected and there is a 'substantial change'. they don't say which one, though. but are not its promoters themselves claiming that the substance is maintained? the statements of giscard d'estaing are read. it's fear that moves them.
in writing. − the european commission considers that, in order to meet the management needs of the common agricultural policy, it is important to have information on land use and the state of land and crops. it therefore presented remote sensing as a research method to obtain easier access to the information contained in the classic systems of agricultural statistics and forecasts. in this proposal it took account of a pilot project on remote sensing techniques under council decision 1445/2000/ec, which has since been launched. the commission considers that this project has enabled the agro-meteorological system for forecasting crop yields and monitoring the state of the land and crops (mars) to reach an advanced stage of development. the commission is now proposing to continue these remote sensing applications in agriculture for the period 2008-2013 in the field of agricultural market monitoring. the project would be implemented from 1 january 2008 for a period of six years. remote sensing applications would thus be a tool at the commission's disposal for the implementation and monitoring of the common agricultural policy, although with information that could be useful to the member states. the question is how it will be used and for whom. that is why we abstained.
in writing. - while agreeing in general terms with the european commission's proposal, i am voting in favour of the graefe zu baringdorf report, since it introduces some pertinent considerations. i understand, for example, the rapporteur's concern about the impossibility of comparing data between different member states because of the different frequency of analyses. i also approve the proposal to create an inventory and consolidate the spatial data infrastructure and its websites, as well as to improve the website of the agriculture unit to make the data public.
in writing. - this vote refers to the second reading of the proposal initially put forward by the european commission in 2002. the aim of these commitments is to reach agreement with the council on a text which aims to repeal the current directive 87/102/eec and to introduce a common legal framework for consumer credit agreements. the aim is to facilitate the opening up of national markets and to promote the granting of credit for crossborder consumption, in the name of strengthening competition and 'improving' the internal market. among other things, it defines the formula for calculating the annual percentage rate of charge (aprc), the conditions for early repayment and the information to be provided to consumers in respect of credit agreements. we voted in favour of the proposals which sought to improve consumer protection, which is particularly important for portugal in a context where household indebtedness is constantly increasing, exceeding 124% of disposable income, and where the scandalous profits of the main financial groups are being recorded. we voted against all the proposals which aim to facilitate the opening up of financial markets and facilitate crossborder credit, which aims to remove barriers to entry for the major financial groups and not to protect consumers.
in writing. − a common legal framework for consumer credit should establish clear, simple and concise rules in order to provide the european added value in terms of strengthening the internal market. i would therefore like to congratulate this parliament today on the positive agreement reached under this legislation. i consider it of the greatest importance to open up national markets to the consumer credit sector, thereby strengthening competition, with very positive consequences for those who use it. with this new proposal the eu clearly favours competition between lenders and introduces the necessary transparency in the dissemination of pre-contractual and contractual information on credit supply, which i consider to be essential for consumer protection, and also allows for a foreseeable lowering of interest rates by increasing the existing supply, especially in smaller markets. the credit ceilings set by the agreement are also a very positive element for the portuguese market. i am convinced that the new framework will provide more credit opportunities and that it is now necessary to ensure adequate protection and solvency of consumers by preventing excessive exposure to over-indebtedness in the context of a sound social policy. the advantages are to be enjoyed and not to be covered up by problems with other problems.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the roberta angelilli report 'towards an eu strategy on the rights of the child' because it is important to draw attention to the fact that many instruments adopted at eu level affect, directly or indirectly, the rights of the child. i therefore consider it essential to create a legislative framework which will make it possible to recognise the rights of the child and codify them from a legal point of view. in this context, this report makes an important contribution to ensuring respect for the rights of the child, in that it advocates community legislation prohibiting all forms of violence against children and stresses the importance of areas such as education, health, adoption, the fight against poverty and discrimination. it should also be noted that the new lisbon treaty provides a legal basis for the rights of the child, which are now included in the objectives of the european union.
in writing. - this report, with almost 200 articles, includes aspects we support and others we disagree with. our vote must be understood on the basis of this assumption. however, we cannot help but point out that the report fails to identify the causes of the situations it sometimes diagnoses. the report does not criticise the eu's neoliberal policies - whitewashing those responsible - which are the cause of the poverty of millions of people, including children. policies which are at the root of the profound and unacceptable social inequalities which are the result of exploitation and capitalist concentration. policies which promote wage restraint, with the loss of value of workers' wages; facilitating dismissals and the precariousness of employment ties; increasing working time and the flexibility of working hours; or the liberalization and privatization of public services. policies which have profound and negative consequences for the incomes and living conditions of workers, their families and, therefore, their children. respect for and full enjoyment of the rights of the child requires, among other things, a fair distribution of wealth, jobs with rights, decent wages, the reduction of working time, the development of strong public systems of social security, health and universal and free education.
in writing. - in the context of the debate on the construction of a european strategy on the rights of the child, i consider it a priority to emphasise the concept of 'children's interest', not as an opposition to the idea of rights, but as a complementary concept and also as a guiding principle of such a strategy. threats to children's rights are, both throughout the world and across europe, of different nature and degree. while in some places the priority is to address poverty and its causes or the use of child soldiers and sexual exploitation, in other cases it is a matter of ensuring the right of access to health care, protection against sexual abuse, trafficking in children or the right to be adopted in good time and under transparent rules, and the value of the role of the family. in some cases, however, the criterion should be the 'best interests of the child'. this is the standard, the criterion, by which the usefulness, necessity and goodness of any decision, legislation or intervention should be judged. i therefore believe that the most important thing in formulating this strategy is to commit ourselves to this idea, to which the lists of rights, which are not always reasonable, feasible or appropriate, must be subordinated.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the doris pack report on 'adult education: it is never too late to learn' because i believe that adult education, through the acquisition of essential skills, is crucial to achieving the lisbon strategy's objectives of more economic growth, more competitiveness and more social inclusion. on the other hand, and in addition, i also agree with the view that lifelong learning is fundamental to responding to the current challenges of economic and social change, the rapid transition to a knowledge-based society and demographic changes resulting from an ageing population.
in writing. - it is important to pay more attention to adult education. the adult education agenda needs to be given a new impetus as their participation in education and training is not sufficient to reach the benchmark target of 12.5% participation in adult education by 2010. but the quality of adult education needs to be ensured, with particular attention to the various dimensions of quality in learning, notably the development of educators, quality assurance mechanisms and teaching methods and materials. as the report states, adult education is an essential component of lifelong learning and is a very complex field. adults need to link learning with their knowledge, experience and cultural background. finally, it is important to emphasise gender equality in lifelong learning programmes so that both men and women can benefit equally from the opportunities offered by lifelong learning, and to call for the use of all available instruments to ensure equality between men and women in preparing adult education policy measures in collaboration with the european institute for gender equality.
mr frattini, ladies and gentlemen, since 1998 the european parliament has rejected all the initiatives put to it when it was consulted on detailed questions concerning europol. it did so for reasons of consistency, while europol continued to operate in an intergovernmental context without being subject to democratic and judicial control. this initiative is the answer to what we have been asking for all along in this house and is intended to make europol a union agency, financed from the community budget, and to enable us to strengthen our democratic control role. although this proposal is the subject of a great deal of controversy in the council, i do not think we should accept any further postponement. the european parliament has an obligation to show its support for the commission's initiative to transform europol into a union agency. the current legal framework of europol, an international convention, makes it difficult to update or change its powers, and takes years. the increase in new security threats, such as terrorism, which pose new challenges to europol, requires a new approach. the importance of this decision is that it should not only put europol on an equal footing with eurojust and the european police college but also make it more effective by extending its mandate to crime not strictly related to organised crime and by giving greater flexibility to its mechanisms. at the same time, greater transparency and democratic and judicial control must be ensured. i therefore support the excellent report by mr díaz de mera and the important amendments he has tabled, particularly on data protection. i would like to express my respect and solidarity with mr díaz de mera for the excellent report he has produced and for the person he is, especially when some members have tried to unfairly diminish his work by importing national struggles which have already been fully answered by the spanish supreme court of justice.

the rapporteur. - i should like to begin by thanking the members and staff of the committee on women's rights and gender equality and the rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on industry, research and energy for the support and the important contributions they have given, particularly through the proposals they have put forward for this report and which have made it possible for it to be voted on unanimously. it was a work that took place over several months, which also included a parliamentary hearing with important contributions from members of the two parliamentary committees and external guests, especially social organisations. with this report we aim to give greater visibility to the role of women in industry, where on average more than 14% of employed women in the european union work. in some countries this percentage is over 25%, as in bulgaria and the czech republic, and in others it is around 20%, as in portugal, greece and hungary. we know that in some industrial sectors women make up the majority of workers, as in textiles, clothing and footwear, in food, cork, cabling, electrical and electronic equipment, while their participation in high-technology areas is still low. this requires some differentiated approaches, but with a common objective of promoting women working in these areas, ensuring non-discriminatory practices in access to employment and recruitment, respect for equal pay, the creation of career opportunities, vocational training, good working conditions, better pay and the appreciation of motherhood and fatherhood as fundamental social values. the need to ensure employment with rights for women working in industry and to continue to facilitate their access to work in this important production sector also implies greater attention to the situation of the various industries in the european union, the challenges they face and the appropriate responses that need to be found, including in international trade and in monitoring the import situation of more sensitive products such as textiles. special attention is also paid to the restructuring and relocation of multinational companies, which particularly affect women's employment and increase their unemployment, especially in regions where there are no employment alternatives. combating the persisting wage discrimination affecting women workers, including indirect discrimination, requires further development of a methodology for job analysis that guarantees equal pay for men and women, that values people and professions and, at the same time, dignifies work as a structural element for increasing the productivity, competitiveness and quality of enterprises and for improving the lives of workers. it is therefore important to encourage initiatives that help to develop positive actions and human resources policies in companies that promote equality between men and women, also by promoting awareness-raising and training practices that allow the promotion, transfer and incorporation of successful practices. i would like to highlight some projects supported by the equal programme, such as those i had the opportunity to meet in portugal, which should also deserve the full attention of the european commission to ensure its continuity and expansion. as the report stresses, collective bargaining and contracting are of fundamental importance in combating discrimination against women, particularly in the areas of access to employment, wages, health and safety at work, career progression and vocational training. but the member states and the commission have special responsibilities and an important role to play in promoting equality and combating all discrimination, in ensuring employment with rights and in combating job insecurity which particularly affects women. it therefore calls on them to act, whether by setting high standards for the protection of health at work which take account of the gender dimension and in particular maternity, whether by the organisation and timing of work, which respect family life, whether by the creation of effective monitoring mechanisms, the enforcement of labour rights and freedom of association, or also by ensuring universal access to good public social security and affordable social services, in particular day care, childcare and support for the elderly.
mr president, the beijing platform for action states that without the active participation of women and the incorporation of their perspectives at all levels of decision-making, the objectives of equality, development and peace cannot be achieved. moreover, to achieve the objectives of the lisbon strategy, greater participation of women in the labour market is necessary. with women accounting for 59% of graduates, it is not understood that most of the new jobs for women are part-time, sometimes insecure and precarious, poorly paid and with little prospect of career progression. this report by mrs figueiredo, which i congratulate, contains two proposals which i would like to stress: the first is the promotion of women's entrepreneurship, but considering that 61% of women take into account family circumstances when considering starting a business, compared to only 49% of men, measures are needed to facilitate the reconciliation of professional, family and personal life. the other proposal concerns long working hours. it is important that the commission should promote a study on the negative consequences of long stays at the workplace, consequences at the family, personal and social level, such as children being left alone for long hours, which often leads to school failure and criminality. the member states should also be encouraged to monitor more closely companies which force their employees to work overtime and should be subject to very heavy penalties.
the rapporteur. - madam president, i would first of all like to thank the members and the commissioner for their speeches and for the contribution they have made to this debate. but of course i am also calling here - as some have already done - for more practical interventions, that is, for this change in our proposals to be felt on the ground, in the life of companies, in the life of working women, in the life of families, because it is not acceptable - and several people have said this here - that after 30 years of a directive providing for equal rights in the area of pay we still have this brutal difference in average wages between men and women working in industry of 30% which is double the general average wage difference in the european union. we cannot therefore allow this situation to continue for another 30 years, and that is where this appeal to the commission and the member states ends, so that concrete measures are taken, concrete measures which could be legislative, concrete measures which could be more control, but also concrete measures which are more promoting equal rights and equal opportunities, more promoting this reality which must be put into practice in education and training, but also more fighting against stereotypes - which has been emphasized here - but also the problem of the organization of working hours and working time and of effective jobs must respond better to these women's rights, but also to the right to motherhood and fatherhood as fundamental social values of the european union.

in writing. − i clearly supported the creation (in february 2007) of the fundamental rights agency because i believe that this agency can make a significant contribution to increasing the coherence and cohesion of eu policy on fundamental rights. it was officially established on 1 march 2007, but is still awaiting the basic elements for becoming operational, namely the appointment of its director and the adoption of a multiannual framework. this initiative aims to establish a multiannual framework which should guide the agency's work over the next five years, defining the thematic areas in which it should act. i therefore support the enormous effort that the rapporteur - mr cashman - has made to facilitate the negotiations and i hope, as he does, that this will encourage the commission and the council to conclude as soon as possible the discussion on this multiannual framework and, in parallel, the process of selecting candidates for the post of director. the european citizens will not understand any more delays that prevent this fundamental rights agency from becoming fully operational.
in writing. - in addition to the aspects we have criticised and have already had the opportunity to highlight, as the eu fundamental rights agency becomes operational and over time, it becomes clear what is actually intended by it. the debate on the definition of objectives and priorities for its 'multiannual framework' 2007-12 has revealed the narrowness of its thematic areas: racism, xenophobia and intolerance; discrimination on grounds of sex, racial or ethnic origin, religion or belief, disability or sexual orientation or of persons belonging to minorities; compensation for victims, crime prevention and related aspects relevant to the security of citizens; protection of children, including children's rights; immigration and integration of migrants; asylum; visas and border control; participation in the democratic functioning of the union; human rights issues related to the information society; and access to an efficient and independent judiciary. the ep added extreme poverty and social exclusion, but for example, social rights, including workers' rights, were not considered a priority at a time when fundamental social rights are being called into question by eu policies.
in writing. - the proposal for a treaty has not yet been ratified, nor has the proposal to adopt by qualified majority the regulations on the structure, operations, field of action and tasks of europol, as the eu institutions are busy transforming the european police office into a european agency. in addition to our fundamental criticism of this process, we are concerned about:- the possibility that the processing of 'special categories of data relating to ethnic or racial origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical convictions, party or trade union membership, sexual orientation or health' will not be excluded; - the failure to adopt safeguards for the protection of personal data processed in the context of police and judicial cooperation at eu level and in relations with third countries, in particular the usa (e.g. data on air passengers); - failure to guarantee access by a citizen to data concerning him or her or even to inform him whether his or her personal data are being processed by europol; - the lack of clarification on the control by the national parliaments; this would constitute a flagrant violation of the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens.

it was during the portuguese presidency that the council agreed to open the postal services market fully at eu level from 31 december 2010, applying the competition rules to what should be a public service, it is said, with a view to creating an internal market for postal services. "fine, man", says the prime minister of the portuguese government. however, this decision is a serious blow to the public postal services, in particular by abolishing the areas reserved for them, promoting a dynamic aimed at their dismantling and their subsequent handing over to the transnational corporations and their profitability logic, including at the expense of the public purse, putting the rights of the population and workers in the sector in question. if there were any doubts as to the real meaning of the inclusion of the so-called protocol on services of general interest in the proposed treaty, here is the example of this directive to dispel them, that is, the continuation of the process of dismantling and destroying public services, calling into question the ownership and provision by public entities managed and controlled in a democratic way. that is why we are tabled the proposal to reject this directive.
i congratulate my colleagues ferber and simpson on the quality of the report and all the colleagues and parties involved on the openness shown during the negotiating process. this liberalization of the postal services market is still far from achieving a competitive market where the biggest winners will be consumers and businesses, and i therefore argued that the path followed by the commission may not sufficiently guarantee the universality of the service. i therefore supported the position of the shadow rapporteur brian simpson on the need to ensure universal service and the existence of a compensation fund, as well as the commitment to open postal provision up to 50 grams by 2010 or in special cases, such as with the new member states with outermost regions by 31 december 2012. i welcome the special provisions in respect of these states, but i would stress that they may not be sufficient and, if they are, will require additional measures. on the employment front, i welcome the addition introduced earlier, with regard to the obligation to report on the overall employment trend in the sector, the working conditions applied by all operators within a member state and any measures. i welcome the common position reached, but i support the amendments tabled by my colleagues savary, el khadraoui and ayala sender, among others, and by my group in this house, because they reinforce the need for a deliberate process of liberalization that strengthens equal access, development and employment for all. for all these reasons, i urge the house to support this report and the council and to support the position of this parliament.
in the resolution we are voting on tomorrow, parliament recognises the political importance of the bali conference. scientific knowledge has given rise to the political will to act, and by 2009 all countries, whether developed, emerging or developing, will commit to differentiated but concrete targets to contribute to combating climate change. unlike some colleagues, i would have liked to see a stronger involvement of some partners, particularly the united states, in bali, as in kyoto. on the positive side, bali has completed the kyoto gaps on issues such as forest management, the need to support adaptation especially in poorer countries, the role of technology and the extension of climate responsibilities to economies not traditionally considered developed. the role of european leadership has become clear and parliament, in this resolution, expresses its wish that the conditions be created for europe to be able to go even further in its commitments. the following programme of work is demanding and parliament is prepared to take it on. in this connection, i personally welcome the commission's package of decisions taken on 23 december. the shift from political will to instruments of action gives the european union credibility. much will need to be looked at in detail, but the quantification of renewable energy targets, the clarification of sustainability criteria for biofuels and the review of climate-related financial instruments are welcome, for example. i personally welcome the transition of the ets from a national to a sectoral basis, but i believe it is urgent that its compatibility with europe's competitiveness be improved before 2009. the evolution of the emissions trading system to the international level, based on agreements between the world's largest producers for the main sectors, may be a way forward.

the rapporteur. - the face of old europe has changed. today the european union, with 27 member states and almost 500 million inhabitants, faces complex and exciting challenges, which require us to take an ever wider view of the world and to be very attentive to issues such as the maintenance of peace, security, stability, freedom and the exercise of democracy. it demands, as victor hugo wisely perpetuated, that we know what part of the future can be introduced into the present, as the secret to the art of good government. this is the dimension and the great challenge of this report - the challenge of the safety of people and goods in the union - and it is very much present in the daily lives of europeans. i am talking about security, today and tomorrow, every day, on the streets, at work, at leisure and at home, on land, at sea, in the air. it is the security of our common space which, without being imposed, guarantees and reinforces freedom in a balanced coexistence. freedom is a prius, a fundamental value of the union, security is instrumental in the service of well-being, stability and guaranteeing freedom. freedom as a value and security as an instrument are essential to the european project. the austrian initiative, taken up by the portuguese presidency and which led to the council decision, provides for improved cooperation between special intervention units of the european union in crisis situations. it is a good and necessary initiative. this initiative is complementary to prüm, since this treaty provides for cooperation only in the event of natural disasters or serious accidents. my report proposes 11 amendments to the proposal for a decision which, moreover, establishes a minimum general framework for cooperation in cases of man-made crises, aircraft diversions, terrorist attacks, etc., that is, in man-made crisis situations which constitute a serious and direct physical threat to persons, property, infrastructure or institutions. in the proposal, cooperation in the training, preparation and action of special intervention units is always a possibility and it is up to the member state whether or not to request cooperation and to indicate the type of assistance sought. it should be stressed that the effectiveness and readiness of interventions will always depend on the degree of preparation, coordination, coordination and the existence of uniform methods in the modus operandi of the intervention units, so i propose, on the one hand, the possibility of joint training and exercises, and, on the other hand, that such training and exercises may be financed from the union budget, in accordance with articles 30, 32 and 34 of the treaty on european union. it should also be noted that, in our view, the rules on civil and criminal liability applicable in the case of joint operations should be the same as those of the prüm decisions. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this council decision is very important. it is a common solution to common problems and threats facing all member states. it is a solution that values the indispensable cooperation in preparing for and responding to crises caused by the human hand, always unforeseen but always possible. finally, i would like to thank you for the institutional cooperation and technical assistance you have given me and to highlight the amendments tabled by mr díaz de mera, mr demetriou and mr iotova, which have improved and enriched my draft report.
the rapporteur. - first of all, i would like to thank mr fratini and the other members of my committee for the references to my work, to the report and to the other members of the committee who have justified their support for the report and for the initiative of austria and the decision to continue the council and the portuguese presidency. i would like to stress one aspect which i think is very important. in this respect, security - and i repeat, security is an instrument, not a value - is an instrument in the service of freedom and is an instrument in the service of the effective and concrete exercise of the fundamental rights of the citizens of the european union. and another aspect which i think is no less important is that this decision will not favour any intervention, as has been said here, this decision will promote a fundamental aspect in the construction of the european union, which is cooperation between the member states on the one hand, and on the other hand it will also promote cooperation in the field of training, joint exercises and therefore prevention. it is only when member states ask each other to do so that there can be a possibility of acting in the face of concrete crisis situations that arise, and this assessment will of course have to be made by the respective member states. my proposal for budget support from the union budget is also intended, in my view, primarily to stimulate and encourage cooperation in this area, in addition, of course, to some financial support for the member states which need it. finally, i would like to say that it is important that it be implemented, that it be implemented and that it be done quickly, because security does not ask for a day or an hour and every day there can be crisis situations which undermine our security and therefore our freedom in a european union state and which undermine the confidence of all 500 million citizens of the european union.

in writing. − the initiative aims to give cyprus and the two countries that joined the eu in 2007 - romania and bulgaria - the possibility of introducing a simplified regime for checking people at the external borders based on a unilateral equivalence of visas and residence permits. such recognition shall be limited to transit through the territory of those 3 member states and for a period not exceeding 5 days. i clearly support this simplified system, since third country nationals who hold a visa issued by another member state and who benefit from this system have already been subject to a rigorous verification process in that member state and have not been considered a threat to public policy or a risk in terms of illegal immigration. these rules were first introduced in 2006 into the community visa acquis for the unilateral recognition of visas and residence permits, with the aim of simplifying the transit of certain categories of persons while avoiding any unnecessary administrative burden on consular posts. the nine countries that joined the eu in 2004 and became fully integrated into the schengen area on 21 december 2007 see the mutual recognition of these documents as compulsory at the end of the transitional period.
in writing. - as in the report on switzerland and liechtenstein, we think it is important to stress that, in general, these agreements should be part of a more general framework which also aims at promoting the rights of migrant workers and their protection against unacceptable situations of over-exploitation, by promoting the effective exercise of their rights and their integration, for example by guaranteeing the right to family reunification, by applying the international convention for the protection of the rights of all migrant workers and members of their families - it should be stressed that it has not yet been ratified by any eu member state - drawn up under the auspices of the un, an instrument of international law which aims to guarantee the protection of the human rights of migrant workers, in particular the inalienable right to live in a family. in other words, facilitating the movement of citizens between different countries should not be used as an instrument to facilitate situations of exploitation of a temporary, low-cost and easily 'disposable' labour force, of increasing levels of exploitation and pressure on wages, of promoting precariousness, of deregulating labour relations, fuelling a backward dynamic in terms of social rights and conditions for all workers, but on the contrary, to combat such realities.
in writing. - as we have stressed, measures and agreements facilitating the movement of citizens from different countries should be based on principles of balance and mutual benefit for the various parties involved. let us recall the previous agreements between the ec and switzerland on the free movement of persons, which were of particular interest to portugal, given that there are more than 100,000 portuguese working in that country, including many thousands of seasonal workers. agreements which should help to resolve many of the limitations and problems faced by portuguese workers in switzerland, for example as regards changing jobs or professions, family reunification, moving cantons or social protection for workers and their families. in this sense, and in general, these agreements should be part of a wider framework which also aims to promote the rights of migrant workers and to protect them against unacceptable situations of over-exploitation. the facilitation of the movement of citizens between different countries should not be used as an instrument to facilitate situations of exploitation of temporary, low-cost and easily 'disposable' labour, the weakening of labour relations, in particular by fuelling a backward dynamic in workers' social rights and conditions.

in writing. the notion that r & d and innovation are a fundamental part of competitiveness is not new, but remains current. whatever differences there may be on the need to direct efforts towards innovation or more academic research, the fact is that europe needs to improve its investment in knowledge and the practical application of that knowledge. but this need is not limited to financial investment. several successive reports give account of the many causes of the backwardness that europe has and maintains vis-à-vis other parts of the world. from american universities to indian research, the competition around us is immense and growing. on the other hand, the attractiveness of the european schools is reduced, as these reports also prove, which insistently refer, among other things, to the weak overall and per capita funding and the lack of autonomy of our universities as inhibiting factors for better performance. for all these reasons, any approach which treats this matter as an economic and strategic urgency should be applauded. and if it is true that time is running against us, it is no less true that it is better to waste time making the right choices than to decide rashly and ineffectively.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the outcome of the bali conference on climate change (cop 13 and cop/mop 3) because, in view of the urgency of slowing down the increasing global warming process, i consider the agreement reached in bali to be an important step towards a new protocol being agreed and adopted in copenhagen in 2009 with renewed targets for the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions. i believe that the portuguese presidency of the european union played a decisive role at the bali conference, actively contributing to the progress of the negotiations and succeeding in reaching a very positive agreement. it would be desirable, however, that the bali action plan should refer to quantified targets for co2 emission reductions.
in writing. - this resolution in general merely repeats general ideas and is insufficient in several areas. that is why we abstained. of course, because if the objective is to reduce co2 emissions mainly from the combustion of fossil fuels, the question arises of measuring these emissions. it is known that this measurement is very complex and manipulable, since fossil fuels, after extraction, are transported, processed, their derivatives distributed and used in many ways, in thousands of endpoints. as several experts in this field point out, to reduce emissions and meet targets, it was more effective and simpler to monitor an instrument approved on the basis of a protocol on the international extraction and marketing of fossil fuels. this would make it easier to set rates or targets for reducing primary fossil fuel production and corresponding exports/imports, thus setting country emission ceilings. but it would also be necessary to negotiate commitments from the richer countries to unlock funds to support developing countries so that they can meet the economic and social costs of the necessary measures. i regret that they have rejected the group's proposals in this direction.

mr commissioner, mr president, in a minute i can only congratulate commissioner mandelson on his decision not to go ahead with the review of trade defence instruments. imagine that in a system of tumultuous rivers there is a system of dams. the floodgates are run by common rules. is it acceptable that one of the dams should be altered without anyone else doing so, just because some believe that the water this winter will not reach their homes? unilaterally changing the rules of the trade defence instruments would be to weaken the dam to avoid managing the locks. this is not what europe needs, and the commission was right to hear the very clear messages that were given to it in this parliament by the trade unions, european industry and most of the member states. the freedom of trade cannot be achieved by violating the rules governing it. on the contrary, these rules must be modernised and incorporate universal values such as the defence of decent work, the protection of the environment and the climate or public health. it is in this sense, and not in any other, that europe must use its political prestige and its commercial strength in bilateral agreements and vis-à-vis the world's major producers. only with reciprocity and modern, universal rules can trade contribute to improving the living conditions of citizens outside europe, of the world in general, but also the living and survival conditions of european workers and entrepreneurs who still want to keep producing, living and exporting from europe. that is what is expected of the commissioner who represents europe on the world stage. i would like to congratulate you, commissioner.

in writing. - this regulation replaces regulation (eec) no 2913/92 which established the community customs code. the reasons given are the amendments which have been made to it in the meantime. the community customs code (ccc) was established by regulation no 2913/92. it was already a lengthy and technically complex document regulating customs matters in the community. each specific subject within the cac was discussed by the experts in the respective field and the cac issues were addressed in the respective committee. in a world where trade is dominated by large transnational companies, this draft code would have to reflect and serve the interests of these same transnational companies by reducing the time of movement of goods and simplifying customs procedures. it is another question whether this simplification has also led to measures to combat customs fraud. simplification seems to have been favoured over the fight against fraud. it is no coincidence that community texts and/or their translations often speak of 'facilitation' rather than of 'simplification'. it's like they're talking out of their mouths.
in writing. - regardless of whether there is any point in which we should be concerned, we consider that, in general terms, the report raises a number of issues of the utmost importance and relevance. following the european transparency initiative launched by the commission in november 2005, the report reaffirms the need to establish and fully operate mechanisms to make known, for example, the final beneficiaries of the different structural funds by making this information publicly available in an organised manner. the report suggests that different beneficiaries may receive eu funds under different community programmes or sectors of activity, and acknowledges that it could be instructive to have the possibility of identifying all amounts paid to a particular beneficiary across sectors - invaluable information, for example, in the case of relocations of companies, to be provided by workers... the report also deals with other important issues, such as the declaration of financial interests of public office holders in the eu institutions, suggesting the establishment of standards, or the composition of the so-called expert groups (formal or informal) that the commission decides to set up to assist it in its initiatives, including legislative initiatives, suggesting that its composition be known.
in writing. − those who manage public funds are expected and required to be the most rational in their management, the most rigorous in presenting the results of their activities and to be completely transparent. taxpayers - because they are the ultimate funders of all public money - have a right (which they should exercise) to want to know who spends and how they spend the funds made available to the community's interests. for this reason, this report, supported by a communication from the european commission which presents a set of proposals which deserve our agreement in the majority, has received my vote in favour. i would add that i believe that the principles and rules applicable to community funds, in particular those managed directly by the european institutions, should also apply mutatis mutandis to other public funds, in particular those managed by the member states.
in writing. − the fight against fraud and the misuse of public funds, in this case community funds, must be a priority in each member state. to this end, it is essential that each state be provided with the necessary human and material resources to enable it to fulfil its role properly. it should be stressed that, while reaffirming the responsibility of the states to protect the public interest - as the report does - policies are simultaneously promoted which devalue and deprive the states of functions which should be theirs, in particular through the dismantling of public administration services, the permanent disqualification and dismissal of their workers and the use of private entities to perform some of these functions. in our view, the report should also deal with the consequences for the management of public funds of the transfer of public service functions to private companies. it is also stressed that it should be assessed to what extent the excessive complexity and inadequacy of the rules, as well as the delay in the granting of funds, contribute to the irregularities detected. however, the proposals in the report are essentially punitive, in particular by proposing infringement procedures and suspension of interim payments to the member states.
in writing. - although the report contains aspects which we value and consider positive in the context of the worsening world situation, among other aspects, it does not demarcate or denounce the real objectives and consequences of the so-called fight against terrorism, in particular as a factor that promotes and encourages terrorism in itself. the report alludes, albeit mildly, to the fundamental need for a diplomatic and peaceful resolution of conflicts in the world, but fails to point out that the primary factors that encourage terrorism are the spiral of violence fuelled by the militarization of international relations, the attacks on the independence of states and the sovereignty of peoples, state terrorism, the violation of the fundamental freedoms, rights and guarantees of citizens, unbridled capitalist exploitation, the inhuman deepening of inequalities and injustices and the existence of millions of human beings living in desperate situations - as in afghanistan, iraq or palestine. we believe that a serious analysis of terrorism - in all its forms, including state terrorism - will require its political contextualisation, thus exposing its root causes and the policies that are at its origin, such as the so-called fight against terrorism in which the usa and its allies are protagonists. that is why we abstained.
in writing. - one of the greatest dangers in the debate on terrorism and its causes is that we fall into one of two extremes. on the one hand, the understanding that, seeking to understand everything, makes everything acceptable and justifiable; on the other, the refusal to recognize diverse realities that confuse everything and lump everything into the same concepts and standards. both extremes are dangerous as analyses, because, being untrue, they do not allow valid conclusions, misleading police, legislators and citizens. on the other hand, they are a threat to an understanding of reality which is at the same time inclusive and firm with terrorism. that is our challenge: to be able to understand reality as it is, and not as we wish it or fear it; and consequently act on both distant and proximate causes. never forget that terrorism is not acceptable or justifiable under any circumstances. and that it is not the victims (actual or potential) who must understand and justify the crimes of the aggressors. for all these reasons, i voted against this report.
in writing. the european parliament's owninitiative report is a veritable repository of objectives and initiatives for the further liberalisation of world trade - whether in goods, services or capital - led by the eu and its commission, which has almost full power over the common commercial policy with the new treaty proposal, where this is set out as the exclusive competence of the eu. the opening of the markets, the dogma. the end of all and any barriers to trade, in particular with developed and emerging economies, is the way forward. the opening up of markets, if possible in the image of the eu single market, is the objective. in the face of what it considers to be the insufficiently regulatory and binding system of the current wto, it is pushing for the promotion of the european model of governance for trade, either by creating free trade agreements or by insisting on the conclusion of the current round of wto negotiations - for which it calls for the creation of synergies with the eu's main trading partners (such as the us, canada and japan). as an example, the report calls on third countries to remove the restrictions on foreign ownership imposed on european companies. the economic domain is ambition. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. - although the european internal market is vast, the world market, opened up by the mechanisms of globalisation, is even larger and more dynamic. for this reason, access for european companies to this market, particularly to emerging economies with high growth rates, should be a priority for both the public and private sectors. it is true, however, that in the field of private initiative we cannot make choices or, even worse, impose priorities, but in the field of public initiatives there is still a long way to go. on the one hand, we must be aware of the need to open our markets if we want - and we do - to have ever greater access to international markets. on the other hand, it is essential to rely on the ability of european companies to cope with the growing economic efficiency and competitiveness of companies in these countries, which implies the need to rely without hesitation on the competitiveness and innovation of our companies, which can only take place in a free, open and transparent environment.
the reality is that eight years after the adoption of the lisbon strategy, social inequalities have deepened and poverty has worsened, affecting some 78 million people, 25 million of whom are low-wage workers and in precarious employment. most of the jobs created are precarious and parttime work particularly affects women, who continue to be discriminated against in access to employment, training and career progression and at wage level. youth unemployment is twice as high as total unemployment, including many young people with higher education who are unable to find jobs, and even fewer jobs that take account of their training, while some 6 million young people continue to leave school prematurely each year, which also jeopardises their future. these are consequences that were foreseeable in a strategy that deepened its neo-liberal vision with the 2005 revision, which identified as priority measures the liberalisation and privatisation of structural sectors and public services and which insisted on labour flexibility. now the situation of poverty and social injustice may be aggravated by the financial crisis that has started in the united states, with the high price of fossil fuels and some agricultural commodities essential for food. it is therefore urgent to change policies to prevent its consequences in the european union, particularly in the weaker economies, to avoid worsening the social situation. in the resolution we are presenting, we therefore insist on the need to replace the lisbon strategy with a european strategy for solidarity and sustainable development, which opens up new horizons for europe, horizons of full employment and non-discrimination, decent jobs with rights, better wages, economic and social cohesion and adequate public and universal social protection and security, and ultimately ensuring greater social justice.
in 2006, the european union recorded the highest economic growth since 2000. in 2007, the european union outgrew the united states and some new member states approached or even exceeded the double-digit barrier. for those who claim that the revision of the lisbon strategy is neo-liberal and has lost its importance to social issues, the answer is clear: in 2006 employment grew three times faster than the average for the previous five years, and an additional 6.5 million new jobs were created in the last two years, with a further 5 million expected to be created by 2009. you have to go back to the 1980s to find similar values. moreover, in 2006, productivity in europe grew more than the annual average of the previous five years. and for the first time in many years, productivity growth in europe has been higher than in the united states of america. while i cannot claim that these results are the exclusive consequence of the lisbon strategy, it cannot be denied that it has contributed to their achievement. i therefore congratulate the commission on the way it has coordinated the lisbon strategy in very difficult circumstances of implementation. a word about the future: the european economy can continue to grow and more jobs can be created, despite the current situation, if in the coming years the coordination of the economic policies of the member states is improved, if the internal market is deepened, if social dialogue is promoted, if wage increases keep pace with productivity growth, if there is an effective financial surveillance system, if the fifth freedom that of knowledge is strengthened, and, very important to me, if the european union shows clear signs that it wants to defend its interests, which means not being a passive subject of the phenomenon of globalisation, but, on the contrary, showing that it is willing to play a decisive role in controlling it.
mr president-in-office, commissioners, ladies and gentlemen, with the so-called subprime crisis, many of the arguments repeated by the most liberal politicians have fallen flat. after all, markets are not self-regulating, losses do not affect only those who consciously and deliberately participate in sophisticated high-risk games, and europe's good behaviour does not guarantee its immunity to external turbulence. this is just one of many examples which recommend, as the socialist group has been advocating, that europe should define policies and instruments consistent with its objectives and with the role it wants to play in the difficult context of the globalised economy. in 2000 we set a central objective through the revised lisbon strategy. this objective remains valid, but it is not sufficiently achieved. the aim was that in two years' time, in 2010, europe would be the most competitive area in the world, based on a knowledge-based economy creating more social cohesion, more and better jobs. today, the challenges are more pressing and some conclusions are clear: first, the broad economic policy guidelines and the lisbon strategy must be fully aligned; secondly, a balance must be struck between the stability of policy orientations and the ability to respond to rapidly changing environments, including climate, energy, financial market developments, external trade policy or the role of exchange rates; thirdly, the objectives of social and spatial convergence are today one of the greatest failures of the strategy. finally, to ensure external competitiveness and link it to internal cohesion, more effective instruments are needed. the effective coordination of economic policies for growth and employment is just one of them. social, educational, investment, research, science and technology policies must be revised in the light of the new realities. this is the spirit of the contributions presented by the socialist group, which i hope will be welcomed by the commission and the council. we need, above all, citizens to expect the promises of progress to materialise - it is only in this way that it will make sense and that it will nourish your hope and confidence in the future of europe.
the commissioner said that in the last three years it had increased its capacity for growth, improved the functioning of the market, social reforms, public finances and the environmental component. that's a finding, i agree. i recognize that this improvement is mainly due to better dialogue, to better participation by the member states, as we recognized last week at the joint meeting between the european parliament and the parliaments of the member states. the question i would like to ask, commissioner, is this: i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the proposal for a regulation on the european parliament's role in the european union. mr lisbon, at the level of the states, was positive and encouraging. although the responsibility lies with the member states, could the creation of mr lisbon not be encouraged at regional level?

question no 39 by anne e. jensen (h-0051/08) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: airworthiness review by the easa in the autumn of 2007, three accidents with dash8 q400 aircraft occurred in aalborg, vilnius and copenhagen. the provisional reports of the investigating authorities indicate that the accidents of 9 and 12 september were due to construction defects, a conclusion shared by the scandinavian aviation authorities (slv) and the european aviation safety agency (easa). the accident on october 27th was due to a combination of construction defects and detection of defects. the scandinavian aviation authorities have banned the scandinavian aircraft from flying and have set a number of conditions for their continued flying, but easa considers that the design defect in question is of minor importance. can the commission state whether it is not the task of easa to ensure a high level of safety? how is it possible that easa and the scandinavian aviation authorities assess this case so differently when the airline's inspections show that 16 of its 18 dash8 q400 aircraft have the same construction defect as the aircraft that made an emergency landing in copenhagen?
question no 40 by mr jörg leichtfried (h-1062/07) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: transparency of the salaries of company managers there is a steady increase in the salaries of company managers throughout europe. in austria, for example, basic salaries of managers increased by about 3,7% between 2006 and 2007. the increase in the variable components of managers' salaries is still considerably higher. this increase in salaries has led to a growing public interest in the actual remuneration of management activities. particularly because variable earnings are not shown in the annual accounts, shareholders want to know how their money is being used. european citizens are thus clearly demanding greater transparency in the salaries of company managers. is the commission aware of this situation? is there any european legislation to ensure greater transparency in the salaries of company managers or are there already legislative provisions in this area?
