i congratulate the rapporteurs richard corbett and méndez de vigo on their excellent work and the good example of cooperation they have set. the portuguese presidency has had the historic task of transforming a mandate into a treaty, the treaty of lisbon, which the portuguese parliament will ratify next april. the new treaty is not the cure for all the ills of the european union, but it is an asset to democracy. the european parliament gains more powers and so do national parliaments, but participatory democracy is also strengthened - notably through the right of initiative which allows one million citizens to ask the commission to take a legislative initiative in a specific area - and the charter of fundamental rights is now legally binding. the european union is not perfect, but its role in the world is irreplaceable. we need a europe that is more present and more influential in solving global problems such as climate change, food security, energy policy, international terrorism, organised crime, immigration, etc. it is now urgent that each of the 27 member states which signed the treaty of lisbon on 13 december should proceed to ratify it. this is a decisive step towards a europe that is more efficient in decision-making, closer to the citizens, more able to respond to the challenges of globalisation and more effective in external relations. let each one take responsibility for himself, because the world doesn't stop. while europe has prolonged its pause and spent energies in search of a way out of its institutional problems, emerging economies have continued to grow, armed conflicts have widened, climate change has become evident, energy problems have become acute, many people have died from lack of food and medical care. despite the ultra-nationalists and the eurosceptics, europe cannot - and will not - stop.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, lisbon and rome are the starting points for a humanity without frontiers. the dream of global justice and cosmopolitan law runs through the history of the european union. it's the story of the moral will that has taken root in institutions and transformed the old paradigms of politics. it shares the method, the reason, the criterion, the human dignity as the end, the sovereignty of rights instead of the sovereignty of borders, all that made europe the home of the enlightenment. in this march towards large-scale democracy, the lisbon treaty reconciled the european parliament with its parliamentary nature, broke the legislative hegemony of the europe of governments, and brought new leadership figures to the fore for more competition, more politics and less bureaucracy. it is true that the european constitution, with its potential for unity and cohesion, has been delayed, but a post-national europe is already being born. babel will no doubt build its tower.
the idea that i think is essential to stress at this point is the importance and meaning of signals in politics, and we have a duty to send the right signals to the citizens. rather than continuing in this parliament to debate the differences between the constitutional treaty and the treaty of lisbon or how the member states should proceed with its ratification, is it not time to talk about what we will do once the treaty has come into force, as we hope? that is what we told our citizens, that institutional reform was needed to produce more and better results. well, there's the pension. will europe in a year's time be better prepared to deal with globalisation, energy dependence, the demographic crisis, terrorism, financial instability, the shifting nature of jobs? it has to be. is the european parliament more energetic in actively collaborating in the adoption of these reforms? it has to be. that's the right signal to take out of here today, not to do like the chinese proverb, where when the wise man points to the sky, we look at the finger. let us look to our future, mr president, and accept the duty to build it.

they have liberalized and privatised public services, and have multiplied precarious work, which particularly affects women. the extension of the age for access to pensions makes it even more difficult for young people to access employment with rights, coupled with greater difficulties in universal access to public services and adequate housing. all of this tends to lower the birth rate. hence the urgency of changing policies. this is why it is necessary to replace the lisbon strategy with a european strategy for solidarity and sustainable development, which opens up new horizons for europe, with decent jobs with rights, especially for women and young people, shorter working hours without loss of pay, better wages, eliminating discrimination, particularly wage discrimination, which affects women, greater economic and social cohesion, adequate protection and universal public social security, ensuring a better quality of life and greater social justice. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a good example of the need to ensure that the safety of workers is not compromised by the use of asbestos. this is also why we need a bigger budget to increase the financial resources needed for the least developed countries and why it is urgent for all member states to ratify and implement the un convention on the family reunification of migrant workers.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, longer life spans and declining fertility rates mean that the european total dependency ratio will rise from the current 49% to 59% in 2025 and to 77% in 2050. the european union is thus faced with an unprecedented problem, since european cities will have a very high share of the elderly population in the future and will therefore be very different societies from those we know today. this will require major changes in important aspects of public policy. in addition to social security, we can think of health and care services, tax policy, land use planning, immigration, security, culture, tourism, leisure, etc. the financing of the reform system will also have to be re-thought so that it is not predominantly state-based, and yet in this case the revenue is not almost exclusively from wages. the demographic trend, given its magnitude, calls for an intersection of public administration and the social fabric, and the mobilization of all economic, cultural and social actors, who, in a structured way, must analyse and debate the different options for the measures to be taken. that is the merit of this report. once again we are faced with an area where the strengthening of social dialogue is necessary, urgent and even irreplaceable. i would like to say that i support the commission's view that the promotion of birth rates, because of its urgency and its scope, requires the definition of a long-term strategy. only in this way can preventive action be taken and at the same time help the european union to take advantage of the opportunities that also arise from a policy of promoting births.

mr president, commissioner, i would first like to congratulate the rapporteur, mrs françoise castex, on her excellent work. demographic change is a major challenge for europe. a hundred years ago, the population of europe was 15 percent of the world's population. by 2050, it should represent only 5%. in the european union, each woman has on average 1.5 children, which is less than the 2.1 children needed to replenish the population. the situation is serious and will have negative consequences for the economy, social security systems and the very composition of society. this is why measures such as those recently adopted in portugal are necessary, investing over eur 100 million in covering the country with day nurseries and kindergartens, going beyond the targets of the lisbon strategy. the allocation of prenatal allowances to the most deprived pregnant women, family allowances for the children of immigrants, the extension of maternity leave, a 20% increase in family allowances for single-parent families, tax benefits for companies which set up or subsidize day-care centres for their employees, the creation of social maternity allowances, public support for medically assisted procreation - these are good examples for other countries.
member of the commission. − madam president, i wish to begin by congratulating – and perhaps, even more, by thanking – both ms kallenbach and mr guellec on their reports, and also the committee on regional development on its excellent work both on the fourth cohesion report and on the report on territorial cohesion. the commission fully shares your views that european cohesion policy has played a major role in narrowing disparities across the european union and thus fostering european integration, and also getting the union closer to its people. therefore, the commission firmly rejects attempts to renationalise this policy. we also share your view that adequate financial resources for cohesion policy must be guaranteed in the future in order to deal with the anticipated new challenges which will affect all european territories. we have also to keep in mind that, at the same time, cohesion policy will have to continue to cope with regional disparities resulting from the most recent, and forthcoming, enlargements. let me reassure you that, in the context of the ‘lisbonisation’ of our policy, the main priority of european cohesion policy is, and will remain after 2013, the objective of narrowing disparities, as it is enshrined in the reform treaty. the solidarity dimension of the policy is central to this policy and the allocation of resources will certainly follow an inverse relation with the prosperity of countries and regions. this view is also shared by an impressive majority of stakeholders across the union. what is also shared is that european cohesion policy is much more than just a distributive mechanism of resources between member states and regions; this policy is first and foremost a development policy whose objective is to foster the endogenous development of all european regions. the commission also shares your concern about the need for more coherence between european cohesion policy and other community sectoral policies, especially rural development, research or competition. i would add here that the need for coherence between the different development policies also applies to the coordination between european cohesion policy and national polices. i am convinced that this is a key issue for the future of european cohesion, also in its territorial dimension. i fully share your view that the success of the territorial agenda and the leipzig charter depends on two conditions. first, we need to put in practice an integrated approach to the territorial development in order to avoid a piecemeal approach to our territories. a classic example here is thinking in categories of purely rural or urban strategies, which misses the key importance of the true economic regions. on the other hand, the integrated approach means also the need for integrating different sectoral policies both at the eu and member state level, which affect the development of all our territories. the second condition, as you rightly point out, is the need for the commission to monitor and to assess regularly the progress in the implementation of actions agreed under the territorial agenda, and here we need to know more about the effects of these actions in the member states so that the commission can offer them adequate assistance. for example, on the basis of better monitoring, the commission can further progress in the area of defining indicators of territorial cohesion. clearly the commission sees as good news – as does your report – the introduction of the notion of the territorial dimension of cohesion in the lisbon treaty, and now we have to make the most of this new dimension of cohesion policy and the avenues it opens up such as, for example, the new definition of subsidiarity giving more weight to local and regional authorities. that is why the commission included the green paper on territorial cohesion in our legislative and work programme for 2008. even if there is no standard definition of the concept yet, territorial cohesion synthesises the legal objectives of the union to achieve a sustainable balance and harmonious development of its territory and also to provide equity of access to services of general interest. we are all aware today that there are a number of aspects of territorial balance in the union which threaten the harmonious development of the union economy and society in the years to come. they are at eu, national and regional level and also in some specific areas and with regard to outermost regions. i am pleased to confirm that the key recommendations made in ms kallenbach’s report, as regards the definition of the concept of territorial cohesion and the implementation of an integrated approach to territorial development, and also the improvement of the synergies between community policies, are all taken on board in the preparation of our green paper that will be adopted by the college next september. let me also use this opportunity to inform you that we are progressing with the member states in our common understanding of territorial cohesion and its key components. we are currently working on the responses to the questionnaire which we have sent to 25 member states on territorial cohesion, thus clearly making progress possible. we have also established in the commission an inter-service group which is giving us a framework to work in-house on territorial cohesion, and we have already completed the first part of this exercise: the identification of the territorial dimension of key eu policies. we have now embarked on the process, specifically on the process of developing some tools which also match your request. as you probably know, investigating territorial impact assessment of policies and also developing territorial cohesion indicators are among the priorities of the new strengthened espon programme. as regards urban affairs, in march we will have the next urban audit which is currently finalised and the second report on the state of european cities is due for june 2009. urbact ii has now been upgraded to a strategic instrument for networking and for exchanges in urban development. my feeling is that we have, in the case of both reports, a high coherence of your views and of those of the commission, and i now look forward to the debate for a better understanding of your concerns.

gue/ngl. - (fr) in this brief statement on such an important issue as the future of cohesion policy at european union level, we would only underline some of the fundamental principles which we think should guide this debate. firstly, regional policy is an indispensable instrument for promoting the pursuit of economic and social cohesion, a structural policy whose first and main objective, as has already been stated, is to reduce disparities between the levels of development of the various regions and the backwardness of the less-favoured regions, to promote real convergence and to stimulate growth and employment, and it must therefore be an instrument of redistribution and of intended compensation for the increased costs of the single market, economic and monetary union and the liberalisation of international trade for the less developed countries and regions of the european union. secondly, cohesion policy and the financial means associated with it should be used to promote economic, social, environmental and territorial development projects, and should not be subordinated to a policy that has as its priority and dogma competition, deregulation or the so-called adaptability and entrepreneurship that are priorities of the lisbon strategy. in other words, we believe that so-called competitiveness should not be a substitute for convergence in member states and regions which are lagging behind in their socioeconomic development. thirdly, the current community financial resources for cohesion policy are insufficient to meet the needs of real convergence, regional disparities, high levels of unemployment, income inequalities and poverty in the european union, and we therefore reiterate the need for an increase in the community budget, with the central and overriding objective of promoting economic and social cohesion at european union level.

in writing. - this report by the european parliament introduces certain elements which may be positive, although with some contradictions, namely: it equally holds all those involved in the placing of a product on the market, from the manufacturer to the distributor and the importer, but without clarifying how. it also allows the maintenance of national markings which, under the european commission's proposal, would disappear and only the ce mark would be recognised. the compromise now replaces the reference to national markings with other markings. the commission also stresses that the framework is not mandatory but that those who adopt it will have to follow it and introduces a reference to smes, calling for their specificities to be taken into account. however, the objective of the european commission proposal, which is not called into question in the report, is to facilitate the functioning of the single market by removing the obstacles which still remain, but it does not apply to certain sectors of activity, namely foodstuffs, animal feedingstuffs, animal health and welfare, tobacco products, veterinary medicinal products, medicinal products for human use, human blood and tissues and cells of human origin, for which there are already harmonised standards.
in writing. − the european commission's argument in proposing this regulation is that the principle of mutual recognition is hampered by a number of problems (i.e. products marketed in one member state may be prevented from being marketed in another) and considers that the possibility of national technical rules raising unlawful obstacles to the free movement of goods between member states needs to be reduced. it thus lays down the requirements which the authorities must fulfil when they intend to enforce a national technical rule, with the burden of proof being on them. in other words, it imposes conditions with the clear aim of restricting the ability of each state to apply its rules. the european parliament's report adds further obstacles to the action of each state, such as: this regulation aims to strengthen the functioning of the internal market with fair and undistorted competition, improving the free movement of products while ensuring a high level of consumer protection and product safety. in practice, member states are prohibited from restricting the sale on their territory of products when they are manufactured and marketed in another member state, even if they do not fully comply with the rules of the member state of destination.

in writing. − the renewal of europe's populations is a crucial factor for the balance between young and old and for the increase in the active population. the consequences of the current decline in birth rates and the increase in life expectancy will contribute to an increase in dependency in the elderly and the decline in the working population. it is therefore important to take measures to promote demographic change so as to achieve a more productive and advanced europe with a high level of social protection and solidarity between the generations. we must develop policies that encourage the continuous renewal of europe's population and ensure continued economic competitiveness, while preserving the european social model. we cannot ignore another aspect of this issue, which is linked to europe as the destination of important migratory flows, since these populations invariably contribute to increased birth rates. the intersection of demographic and migration issues has potential risks, and we cannot simply rely on these populations for demographic renewal. i would therefore like to emphasize the measures to stimulate the birth rate, accompanied by appropriate policies in the field of education and training and solidarity between the generations, aimed at preventing demographic decline in europe.

the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's environmental policy is not distorted. - i also begin by congratulating the rapporteur and telling him that the envi committee believes that a combination of measures is necessary to ensure a sustainable transport system for future generations. traffic management, better logistics, tax incentives for transport and green fuels, safe, environmentally friendly, efficient and accessible public transport systems, modernisation of railways, non-motorised mobility, etc. are some of these measures, and information and education campaigns for young people are also needed. we support the inclusion of aviation in the european emissions trading scheme and advocate similar legislation for the maritime transport sector, as well as the adoption of ambitious and binding limit values for co2 emissions from cars, making them more fuel efficient. it is therefore desirable that the european union should support research to develop technologies necessary for the creation of sustainable and environmentally friendly transport, such as the development of alternative and renewable fuels such as hydrogen and fuel cells.
the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the report i am presenting to you concerns the fisheries agreement concluded with a small african country which, after more than a decade of armed struggle for independence, has experienced in recent years enormous political instability, punctuated even by periods of civil war. fishing is an important economic resource for this small country and the financial contribution it makes to its budget is very important. but this is not a fisheries agreement to buy fish. this is not the position of the european union in accordance with its partnership philosophy. the european union's policy is inspired by other values and has as its main concerns the sustainability of resources and an effective partnership approach. it is therefore an agreement with mutual benefits: for the european union, of course, because its fleet has access to important fishing areas, but also for guinea-bissau, which, in addition to the financial compensation, will be in a better position to manage more sustainably what is perhaps its greatest economic resource, through support for research, control, surveillance and the improvement of the health conditions of fishery products. it is therefore a balanced and mutually beneficial agreement, and i therefore recommend that parliament approve my report, with the amendment introduced by the committee on development and with my own amendments, which are intended only to strengthen parliament's position in monitoring these matters, and i believe that, despite the statements the commissioner has just made about the apparent unacceptability of these proposals, the fisheries policy can only benefit from a more positive and more permanent position of parliament.
the rapporteur. mr president, i would first of all like to say that i deeply regret the allegedly moralistic attitude which some members are trying to instill in this debate and which reveals nothing more than, in my view, a gross ignorance of what is reasonably at stake. i am fairly familiar with guinea-bissau, its political, economic and social situation and its recent history, and i am well aware of the attack on guinea-bissau's resources by the fishing fleet of the former soviet union in the late 1970s and the predatory, indeed predatory, attitude of some of our competitors in terms of fishing on a global scale. i think that the philosophy which guides the union's fisheries policy is something to be proud of and not ashamed of, and it is a pity that the other fishing powers do not follow our example. the fact that the committee on development voted unanimously in favour of the report and the committee on fisheries overwhelmingly in favour of my report is proof of this. i think that this is the way forward, with political realism, and the way that best serves the interests not only of the european union but also of the people of guinea-bissau. i therefore urge parliament to approve this report because it is a politically balanced report and a partnership agreement which is mutually beneficial for the parties to it.

in writing. − this regulation establishes a 'greater degree of harmonisation' of common rules in the field of civil aviation security at eu level - such as for screening of passengers and cabin baggage, access control or security screening of aircraft - by repealing the 2002 regulation adopted in the wake of the events of 11 september 2001 in the usa. among other things, we criticise the fact that there is no guarantee that the costs of security measures will not be passed on to the users of these services, which are of an eminently public nature. or, indeed, that users will not be overtaxed at the expense of these measures. the commission has also not clarified the elimination of a whole series of security measures which have already been widely criticised, particularly as regards their effectiveness. it should also be noted that, as regards workers, the limitation of access to the 'airside' for safety reasons has been used to restrict workers' freedom of association. the current text does nothing to prevent such abuses or to protect these rights. finally, the regulation clearly opens the door to the presence of armed personnel on flights, a measure which we consider to be wrong, also for safety reasons.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr luís manuel capoulas santos on a proposal for a council regulation on the conclusion of the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community and the republic of guinea-bissau, as i considered that it was a balanced agreement which ensured the sustainability of fisheries and at the same time guaranteed the protection of the interests of both parties involved: the european union and guinea-bissau. i believe that the amendments tabled by the rapporteur make an important contribution to strengthening the european union's fisheries policy, in that they emphasize the importance of strengthening the information and role of the european parliament.
in writing. − established for the period between june 2007 and june 2011, the agreement between the ec and the republic of guinea-bissau provides for the allocation of 37 fishing licences, four of which to portugal. 35% of the ec financial envelope is intended to support initiatives adopted under the fisheries sector policy defined by guinea-bissau. emphasis will be placed on improving the health conditions of fishery products and on measures to monitor, control and monitor fishing activities. this is a particularly important area of action, given that, according to international bodies, the country's fisheries resources have been severely affected by illegal and unregulated fishing, among other reasons. it should also be noted that this agreement provides for the mandatory hiring of local crews, i.e. guinean crews, in accordance with the gross tonnage of the vessels. as in other agreements, it is envisaged that these crew members will be governed by the declaration of the international labour organisation (ilo). article 10 of the agreement also provides for the setting-up of temporary associations between community and guinean operators for the joint exploitation of resources. this is advantageous for community vessels, since they are thus exempt from paying licence fees.
in writing. − the main objective of the new eu-ivory coast partnership agreement is to strengthen cooperation between the parties in order to foster the establishment of a partnership framework for the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and responsible exploitation of fisheries resources in the ivorian fishing zone, with particular attention to supporting the ivorian fisheries policy. the two parties shall decide jointly on the priorities to be set for such support and shall define the objectives, the annual and multiannual programming and the criteria for assessing the results achieved, with a view to ensuring the sustainable and responsible management of the sector. the agreement respects the fundamental principles of the common fisheries policy and grants portugal a fishing licence for five surface longliners. this report therefore deserves the favourable vote of the psd members.
in writing. − this agreement provides for a total of 40 fishing licences to be allocated to vessels from eu countries - 5 of them to portugal - for a period of six years, starting in july 2007. compared with the previous agreement, this represents a significant reduction in fishing opportunities, but the agreement provides that the catch may increase. the parties agreed that the ec financial contribution would be used in its entirety to support initiatives adopted under the sectoral fisheries policy defined by côte d'ivoire. the shipowners benefiting from this agreement are obliged to employ at least 20% of their crew from acp countries. the agreement provides that these crew members will be governed by the international labour organisation (ilo) declaration on fundamental principles and rights at work, which makes freedom of association and the effective recognition of the right of workers to collective bargaining mandatory, as well as the elimination of discrimination in matters of employment and occupation. their wages shall be fixed by mutual agreement between the shipowners and the seamen or their representatives and shall not be lower than the standards applicable in their countries of origin, which may lead to non-compliance with the principle of equal pay for equal work.
in writing. - it is impossible to comment on all the important issues raised by this ep own-initiative report in this explanation of vote, given its complexity and breadth, but it is only to be noted that the document does not address, or addresses incorrectly, aspects which researchers point out as essential in addressing the problems of transport, energy and their impact on the environment. among others:- the failure to mention the already characterised 'peak oil' and its consequences;- the failure to mention the use of methane in road transport (in the form of cng, lng or biomethane);- the mystification of the use of hydrogen as an alternative fuel for road transport;- the uncritical re-orientation of the use of biofuels, with its dramatic consequences already widely demonstrated;- the omission of documents such as the 'target 2020' programme which advocates the replacement by 2020 of about 20% of petrol and diesel consumed in the european transport sector; finally, it should be stressed that, rather than listing the problems, which have already been clearly identified, policies are needed to deal with them effectively, such as questioning the current capitalist globalisation and the role of transport in this context, in particular the increasing geographical separation between production and consumption, increasing transport needs. there's a lot more to it than that.

in writing. − the european commission presented, in its january 2007 energy package, a proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on energy statistics. the european parliament, however, considered that the proposal had a significant number of shortcomings, which it sought to fill with a number of amendments. although we have some reservations about certain amendments, we agree that, as it stands, the statistics produced by the major international organisations such as eurostat are structured on the basis of accounting instruments designed in a period entirely dominated by fossil fuels and which are intended to monitor the operation of the energy sector solely from the point of view of supply. the development over the last thirty years has led to a growing gap between the initial objective of these instruments and their ability to represent energy realities. the risk of distortion in knowledge and assessment of energy realities leading to unfounded decisions thus increases from year to year. the commission proposal is the result of work carried out in 2003, 2004 and early 2005, largely ignoring the documents on energy issues published by the commission in march 2006 (green paper on energy) and january 2007 (energy package).
in writing. - i agree with the european commission's proposal because i believe that detailed, harmonised and updated statistics on trade and use of plant protection products at community level are necessary to properly monitor the risks associated with the use of these products. the proposal to create a legal framework establishing harmonised rules for the collection and dissemination of data on the marketing and use of plant protection products is urgent, as the calculation of risk indicators requires adequate data and, according to experts, existing data on plant protection products lack accessibility, transparency and reliability. although i do not agree with some of the details of the report, such as the inclusion of biocides, i believe that it does not distort the commission's basic ideas, and it also makes some very positive proposals, such as the inclusion of non-agricultural areas in the framework of future legislation and the proper protection of commercial data, which is why i am voting in favour of the staes report.
in writing. - although the report by the committee on agriculture departs from the european commission's proposal, advocating a voluntary 2% increase in member states' milk quotas and ignoring the end of the quota system, the truth is that it also does not take a position against the dismantling of the current quota system or against the liberalisation of the sector after 2015, as the commissioner wants, but which we reject. that is why we abstained. we are afraid that this 2% increase in the member states' quotas, although optional, will allow the large countries and their large producers to increase their production, leading to a decrease in the producer price, creating a situation of dumping, which could serve as a pretext to more easily justify their subsequent dismantling. an increase in the quota should be linked to a community study setting desirable minimum consumption targets by country on the basis of current consumption levels, accompanied by european and national policies to support the increase of production in the deficit countries, promoting a 'regionalized' increase in milk quotas, particularly in the outermost regions and mountain regions, complemented by the creation of a 'premium' to support the organised collection of milk from producers in these regions, guaranteeing them a decent income.
in writing. − in the milk sector, stability and predictability in the long term are crucial for producers and any change to the content of the system which should be in place until 2015 should be given the utmost attention. the amendments now proposed to increase the level of quotas, together with the reduction of fines provided for in the goepel report, mark the beginning of the dismantling of the system well before 2015. despite recent changes in the milk market, both portugal and the eu are producing below their quota, so instead of increasing their quota, we could make adjustments between countries, as 18 out of 27 are below production possibilities. the increase of 2%, voluntary or not, is therefore a first signal to the market that regions with a higher competitive capacity will benefit at the expense of less favoured regions. although the jeggle report improves the commission's proposal, i abstained in order to express my disagreement with what is in practice the beginning of the dismantling of the milk quota system.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' in the definition of the term 'commercial vehicle'. in this context, i would like to emphasize the provision of funds for the maintenance of milk production in regions such as the azores, which is advocated in this report, and i would also like to stress the remarkable commitment and the important contribution of the amendments tabled by mr capoulas santos.
in writing. - this resolution is insufficient in its criticism of the european commission's proposal, although it includes two of the many proposals we have put forward. but its general orientation is negative, particularly when it insists on the unbundling of production aids and urges the commission to ensure that the policy of dissociation is rapidly advanced. experience has shown that the dissociation of direct aid from agricultural production has adverse effects. that is why we are voting against it. but we welcome the rejection of the re-nationalisation of the cap, the call for restructuring measures and the strengthening of key agricultural sectors (such as the dairy sector, the dairy cattle sector and sheep farming) and the approval of our proposals that the european commission should take account, in the world trade organisation negotiations, of the specific features of agricultural production as a food production sector, a structural element of the territorial balances of environmental protection and safeguarding adequate levels of food security. we also welcome the endorsement of our call on the commission and the member states to take the necessary measures to prevent speculative activities, control of the food market and the formation of cartels by the food industries.
in writing. - except for the milk quota issue, i consider the commission proposal very relevant. the goepel report improves it in many respects, but it makes some amendments with which i cannot agree. firstly, i support the idea of a ceiling on aid as proposed by the commission, since, in view of the increasing pressure of public opinion on aid to farmers and following the implementation of the upr, which has made the system clearer and more transparent, certain imbalances have become apparent and it is therefore necessary to find a fair system to limit the level of aid to large farmers. i also believe that the fact that modulation funds are kept in the regions concerned will not help to resolve the major regional differences in european agriculture. finally, as regards milk quotas, i am against a 2% increase in 2008 and against a reduction in fines, because i believe that such measures will eventually lead to the dismantling of the milk quota system before 2015, with disastrous consequences for the most vulnerable regions dependent on milk production and for all their farmers who have invested in this sector and whose expectations have been betrayed. for all these reasons, i abstained.
in writing. - all policies have the obvious duty to respond to a need and to address it effectively. the current reality of agricultural markets, consumption patterns, environmental needs and future trends require a rethinking of the assumptions, concepts and rules of the common agricultural policy and a reform of the common agricultural policy accordingly. the central axis of this reform must take account of a number of key ideas, such as the importance of the viability of the rural world, the need to avoid the disappearance of european agriculture, farmers' incomes and the need to bring young entrepreneurs and creative models of production and management into this market, and also the interests of consumers, who are all of us, and often no one represents them with vigour. despite the immediate disadvantages that widespread increases in agricultural prices may represent for some sectors of society, both in developed and non-developed economies, there is a set of virtues (therefore greater consumption among the populations of rapidly developing countries) and a potential for advantages that must be taken into account in this reform. this is the approach which i hope will be welcomed, both by the institutions of the european union and by the national authorities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mrs christa de klaß on the situation of women in rural areas in the european union, because i believe that rural development policies must take into account the gender dimension, thus contributing to the achievement of the objectives of the lisbon strategy on growth, education, employment and social cohesion. i believe that women have a key role to play in promoting local and social growth, and that proposals to improve the living conditions of women in rural areas, such as the creation of education and training infrastructure at all levels; the promotion of equal access to the labour market; the encouragement of female entrepreneurship; and the development of quality social and health services are essential for sustainable rural development.
in writing. - we welcome the adoption of several amendments which improve the final report, including a proposal we tabled stressing the need to give maximum value to the work of women, including immigrant women who are not part of the family unit of the holding but are workers in agricultural fields and are particularly affected by discrimination in the agricultural world. we therefore voted in favour of the report. however, we regret that other proposals we have put forward have not been adopted on the situation of women in rural areas, which is very much influenced by the situation of agriculture, suffering the consequences of unfair measures in the area of the cap - common agricultural policy, which has led to a growing abandonment of small and mediumsized farms and family farming. we therefore continue to insist on the need for a thorough review of the cap, giving priority to the protection of family farming and small and mediumsized farmers, supporting production and guaranteeing their income.
in writing. - the report deals with a number of important issues and makes some points which we support. we agree, in particular, that we should not start with 'dedicated' biomass but rather use waste from various sources, which makes them more energy-efficient and economically viable, and mitigates or solves serious environmental problems. it is also positive that it states that biogas has a far greater energy potential than liquid biofuels, which has been ignored by the european commission. however, we think it is necessary to go into some questions, in particular the difference between the very important concept of biomethane, which is an upgrade of biogas. a clear distinction must be made between biogas and biomethane. biomethane can and should also be produced from etar, landfill and industrial waste, and of course from livestock waste. switzerland and sweden are already producing biomethane and using natural gas networks for its distribution. in the gothenburg area in southern sweden, there are already some 4500 vehicles running on biomethane alone. in the usa there are numerous producers of biomethane and its distribution is in the form of liquefied biomethane. we therefore insist on the need for the european commission to give full attention and priority to funding for biomethane projects throughout europe.
in writing. the tabajdi report emphasises the potential of using agricultural biogas and suggests the development of a directive on biogas production. i am voting in favour of the tabajdi report because i believe that the use of biogas has two benefits, since it can contribute to the security and sustainability of the eu's energy supply, but also allows farmers to develop new sources of income. the contribution of biogas to the pursuit of the recently launched targets for the contribution of renewable energy by 2020 could be of particular relevance.
the rapporteur. - madam president, as parliament votes on a report on the role of the european union in iraq, it is important to draw attention to some lessons learned from the history of that country. on 16 march next it will be 20 years since the chemical weapons attack on the kurdish town of halabja, one of the deadliest operations in the genocidal anfal campaign waged by saddam hussein's forces against his own people. halabja was not an isolated case. there were many halabja throughout iraq. for decades the regime of saddam hussein, with the passivity and sometimes the connivance of european governments, subjected the iraqi people to a strategy of systematic brutalization whose devastating consequences are still being felt today. that is why i, as rapporteur, wanted the fundamental axiom of this report to be europe's moral and legal responsibility towards the iraqi people. no people have suffered more in recent decades and few countries are more strategically important to the security of europe. in addition to its duties, europe must assume that it has an interest in consolidating a federal, democratic iraq, where the rule of law prevails and where human rights are respected, including women's rights. in 2003, my party, the portuguese socialist party, and i personally opposed the decision to invade iraq, supported by my country's then prime minister, mr durão barroso. i'm holding that position. but this report should not serve to reiterate our known positions on an issue which has divided europe in the past. this parliament is called upon to give its opinion on the present and future contribution of the european union to a secure, prosperous, democratic iraq at peace with its neighbours. it was with this in mind that i made two trips to iraq in january and february in preparation for this report. one to baghdad, nasiriyah and the marshlands region and one to kurdistan in the north of the country. with a budget of $48 billion for 2008, what iraq doesn't lack is money. no budget support or soft loans are needed. what iraq needs and what iraqis are asking for is technical assistance and institutional capacity building so that the state and civil society can function and the country's vast resources can be put to the service of the population, including the millions of internally displaced people and refugees in neighboring countries. this report does not simply encourage greater eu involvement in iraq. we also demand that the union's presence in iraq be guided by transparency, visibility and effectiveness, and parliament welcomes the commission's growing concern to improve the use of european funds in iraq in a very difficult context. in this sense we believe that the commission and the member states can and should be more present on the ground, with personnel and projects, especially in those areas of the country where the security situation allows it, as is the case in the kurdish region. we also want to see regulation of the contracting of military and private security companies. i would stress that in this report the european parliament is calling for the first time for clear rules to be established for the use of these companies by the institutions of the european union. the main message of this report, which is important to convey to the commission, the council, european businesses, non-governmental organisations and public opinion, is as follows: europe has a unique opportunity today to make a positive contribution to the destiny of iraq and, by extension, the region. the interaction with the commission throughout the preparation of this report and the consensus with which the report was received in the committee on foreign affairs of this parliament convince me that europe is ready to take up this challenge. i would like to conclude by personally thanking all the colleagues who have offered amendments and suggestions and in particular the shadow rapporteurs, jana hybášková, baroness nicholson of winterbourne, andré brie and cem özdemir, for their contributions which have greatly enriched this report.
let me say, commissioner, that after all the debate we have had on this subject, i think the united nations deserves my utmost respect. we have to be very careful not to let the people who are responsible for the deaths of our citizens be the ones who are responsible for the deaths of our citizens. that does not mean that we should not know what is going on, we should not know to whom the funds that are being used in iraq are going. and let me also say that the 20 million that the commissioner has just spoken of - and i am sorry i read it two or three months ago - seem to me to be largely insufficient to deal with the plight of refugees and displaced persons. it is a drama of colossal proportions, commissioner, of little use to the oil that will be in iraq. these are people who don't have access to that oil. i would thank you, commissioner, for looking at this matter more closely because, as my colleague béatrice patrie has said, it is urgent to look at this problem.
the rapporteur. - i would like to thank you all for your kind words to me and, in particular, to greet my friend, minister lenarčič, with whom i was in the security council a few years ago, dealing with iraq, the problems caused by saddam hussein's iraq. this report, as i have said, seeks to project the diversity of iraqi reality against the simplistic message of an 'iron and fire' iraq that the television sets send us every day. it should be seen as an action plan, a road map for european union involvement in iraq. i think i can speak for parliament when i say that we want the commission, the council and the member states to use the operational proposals we make as a basis for designing future programmes and projects to support the government and the people of iraq, taking account of the security situation, of course. i came back from iraq impressed by the iraqi enthusiasm for 'more europe'. from president talabani to a primary school teacher in one of the country's most remote rural areas, everyone had a thirst for political recognition and institutional support from the european union. we were bombarded with project proposals in a wide variety of areas: training of staff in the ministry of interior, support for local ngos active in the areas of demining, adult literacy and sexual and reproductive health education, technical and institutional support for the iraqi parliament - finally, just to name a few examples. i think we should measure the success of this report not so much by the number of votes in tomorrow's vote, but rather by the difference it will make to our action on the ground in iraq from now on. our parliamentary delegation for iraq will undoubtedly assume its responsibilities in this process, and i am sure that we will count on the commission, on commissioner ferrero-waldner, whom i welcome, and on her courageous team in baghdad, which is being competently led by the usual ambassador as a key ally in the implementation of this road map.
in writing. this report omits responsibility and complicity in the dissemination of false information that served to justify military intervention in iraq, such as the existence and location of 'weapons of mass destruction' and links of the former regime to international terrorism, and also whitewashes responsibility for the introduction into the country of the iranian revolutionary guards and their iraqi affiliates with the consequent spread of terrorist groups and death squads and genocide that have been and continue to be the primary target of ethnic and religious minorities and the country's elites. the report does not make its relations with, or even the european union's financial support for, the iraqi authorities conditional on their commitment to combating terrorism and genocide, and the persecution and trial of those responsible, outside and inside the security forces, while minimizing the tragedy experienced by millions of iraqi refugees and displaced persons and the attacks on the most basic rights, freedoms and guarantees of iraqis, especially women. the invocation of the crimes of the saddam hussein regime would be acceptable if it were sincere and if it were not made by concealing the present crimes and those responsible for them, which have resulted in hundreds of thousands of deaths and millions of displaced persons.
on behalf of the pse group. other the resolution on the european union code of conduct on arms exports reflects the frustration of this parliament at the impasse in which this important instrument finds itself, as our rapporteur, mrs gacek, has just said, and i welcome that. ten years after its creation, the code remains a source of pride for those who believe that the european union should take the lead in the global debate on arms transfer controls. we welcome the increasing harmonisation of the application of the code and the detail of the annual reports submitted by the member states, and the outreach initiatives undertaken by the council. but all these advances pale in comparison to the most important issue, the need to make the code a legally binding instrument. we know that the transformation of the code of conduct into a common position of the cfsp has been linked to the lifting of the arms embargo on china. parliament rejects the blackmail which has been at the root of this three-year impasse. no one can ignore the fact that the weapons sold by beijing to the sudanese regime are fuelling the conflict in darfur and are also used, for example, to oppress and repress the burmese people at the hands of the illegitimate military regime. this situation frustrates parliament, because we are tired of the practical and principled reasons which should be enough to put an end to the council's hesitations. a european foreign policy without common and binding arms export rules will always be incomplete and ineffective. moreover, one of the most important obstacles to the full harmonisation of the internal market for defence equipment is precisely the multiplicity of export rules in force in the eu. finally, there is the matter of principle: the european union can only present itself as a responsible and consistent international actor in this area and can only lead the way in improving international law if it is seen as a role model. we are counting, of course, on the slovenian presidency, minister lenarcic, but we are also pointing out right now to the next french presidency, which has special responsibilities in maintaining this impasse, that it is time to unblock the problem and to recognise the importance of putting the european union on the vanguard of effective and responsible multilateralism.

mr president, commissioner, this report deals with a highly sensitive area of european economic policy, namely taxation. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's energy policy is not undermined by the current crisis. these taxes are an important source of tax revenue for many member states. on the other hand, the absence of viable alternatives for supplying the commercial freight fleet makes the price of fuels strategic for the competitiveness of many countries. the recognition of the freedom of the member states to fix excise duties is not in question. however, since they directly affect the prices of the goods traded, excessive differences have a direct impact on the proper functioning of the internal market. as has been pointed out here today, there are also transfrontier movements and the environmental impacts caused by these movements. the compromise reached in the committee on economic and monetary affairs is a real compromise and i would like to commend the work of all the shadow rapporteurs, but in particular the lead rapporteur, mr schmidt. i am not going to hide the fact that some people would like the minimum threshold to reflect more clearly the environmental concerns that drive us. i personally doubt, however, that at the present level of oil prices there is a need for a fiscal reinforcement of this kind of message. the approach adopted was to approximate the minimum and maximum tax thresholds, which, in some cases, sacrificed these environmental objectives in favour of reducing fiscal distortions of competition. it was a great effort and we hope that it will be recognised by the commission and the council and that it will allow further progress in taxation within the european union.
mr president, i congratulate my colleague ms uca on this excellent report and i welcome the two-track approach, endorsed by the commission in its communication, focusing on both gender mainstreaming and specific actions to empower women. i deplore, however, that many dci country strategy papers merely refer to gender as a cross-cutting issue, failing to specify concrete activities, targets or financial allocations. this means that, despite the strategic framework, gender efforts in development cooperation could be reduced to rhetoric in the years to come. gender-sensitive performance indicators should be assessed in mid-term and final reviews. parliament will monitor the implementation of the cps, and we hope that the commission will be able to indicate progress in terms of specific gender-related outcomes. finally, i am shocked by several medieval conceptions reflected in some amendments to this report put forward by some colleagues on sexual and reproductive health matters. i will vote against them, evidently.
in writing. - in general terms, the aim of this report is to encourage the integration of the 'new' member states into the eu's external policy, in particular its 'development cooperation policy' and its 'european neighbourhood policy'. the report also considers that the 'new' member states represent an opportunity for the eu to 'strengthen its strategic presence in eastern europe, central asia and the caucasus', regions with which the 'new' member states have priority relations and to which eu 'aid' has been less channelled so far. this means trying to use the privileged relationship of the eastern european countries, which joined the eu in 2004, as an instrument of eu intervention (taking into account the interests of its major powers and its major economic and financial groups, in particular in the field of energy) in the countries of the commonwealth of independent states, the western balkans and the caucasus. that is, to try to use the "experience" of "transition" of these countries to capitalism and to integration into nato and the eu - as a figurehead in these regions. this is what it is all about: a policy that masks the interests of capitalism with "development".
in writing. - the very fact that we are discussing the role of the new member states in the european union's cooperation and development policies, particularly with the african, caribbean and pacific countries, speaks volumes about the success of the enlargement and integration process of the acceding countries in recent years. it is true that the so-called former eastern countries had a long tradition of 'cooperation' with africa, and it is possible that, in completely different terms, the links remain; but what is more important is that these countries, which are still facing the costs of their reforms with great energy, are now able to contribute, with the active consent of their populations, to cooperation and development. this is an exemplary path and can be followed - we hope - by other countries in somewhat similar circumstances elsewhere in the world.
in writing. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's research and development programmes are properly coordinated. this programme aims to improve the quality of life of older people through the use of new information and communication technologies (ict). the participation of the european union in this programme will enhance its capacity to address demographic challenges. the use of icts can contribute to greater autonomy for older people and help them to maintain their health and quality of life.
in writing. - we voted in favour of this report on the european commission's proposal for the community to participate in the programme that several member states of the european union have decided to establish in the field of research and development of new information technologies (ict) to age well and act effectively. this programme is called 'assistance to self-employment at home' and aims to achieve synergies in terms of management and financial resources. portugal is also taking part. the report, now approved by the european parliament, draws attention to and makes concrete proposals to give greater visibility to the role and participation of women in science and research, stresses the participation of smes and equitable access of all member states to cost-effective solutions in order to avoid the worsening of the digital divide, with the consequent creation of a 'two-speed' europe. it is also proposed that the commission carry out a mid-term evaluation by 2010 to assess the quality and efficiency of the implementation of the programme.
in writing. the proposal for a directive aims to reduce the differences in diesel prices between the member states, which distort competition and the environment in road transport. in fact, the price differences between road diesel and petrol 95 are significant. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to finance the necessary measures. portuguese companies suffer from competition from spanish companies, as they benefit from fuel prices which represent around 30% of the costs lower due to lower psi taxation (and also vat). portuguese companies have justified the stagnation of workers' fixed wages with this cost pressure, with serious consequences for workers. the european parliament's proposal is more positive because it eliminates the transitional periods of article 18, which is very important in the current situation, and it is hoped that it will reduce the gap between portugal and spain in 2010, as spain will have to increase its psi from 302 to 330 in the case of diesel. the convergence continues in 2012 and 2015. in the case of petrol, unfortunately, there will be no change along this line.
in writing. - the purpose of this declaration of vote is to underline that once again an opportunity may be lost at european union level - since the mechanism exists - to intervene in defence of small-scale coastal and artisanal fishing by not applying to petrol at least the same taxation conditions as those enjoyed by diesel users for agriculture and fisheries. it should be recalled that petrol is the fuel used by vessels in this important and major segment of the fleet of the different member states, in particular portugal. in its resolution of 28 september 2006 on improving the economic situation in the fisheries sector, the european parliament, considering that fuel price increases are having a particularly negative impact on the fisheries sector - significantly aggravating the existing socio-economic crisis and reducing fishermen's incomes very significantly - and stressing that there is a serious risk of thousands of fishing enterprises disappearing and thousands of jobs being destroyed, approved a set of proposals to support the sector, in particular to enable it to cope with the increase in fuel prices. a year and a half later, apart from the increase in de minimis aid, virtually nothing has been done at eu level.
in writing. the resolution adopted achieves the 'astonishing' feat of not making a single mention of the brutal and illegal aggression and occupation of iraq by the us and its allies. the resolution whitewashes the whole role of the death of hundreds and hundreds of thousands of iraqis, the destruction of an entire country and the deliberate and massive human rights violations of aggression and occupation. the resolution completely omits the first and foremost cause of the very serious problems facing the iraqi people and their country today and therefore the way to solve them, namely the immediate withdrawal of all occupying troops! the resolution also calls for the eu to take a more active role in the fight against terrorism and for the eu to play a more active role in the fight against terrorism. it also called on the neighbouring countries to refrain from any interference in iraq, to respect its independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity and the wish of the iraqi people to build their constitutional and political system through their own efforts. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. - the fact that parliament has decided to debate the future of the european union's role in iraq, rather than insisting on a fruitless debate on past issues, is a positive. the five years that matter to us now are the next five years, not the last five years. the starting point for any debate on this issue today must be to recognise that the situation on the ground has improved greatly - although it is still very serious. what this improvement reveals, first of all, is that there is a viable path towards the goal of building a democratic and secure state. our objective is achievable. but it also follows from the experience of recent years that this objective can only be achieved with greater efforts, whether by increasing safety, investing in the preparation of local authorities or - very importantly - actively contributing to the creation of infrastructure that makes possible the economic viability of the country beyond oil. in the case of the european union, specifically, it is a matter of investing significantly in the economic reconstruction of iraq and in the building of a democracy in the country. a democratic, secure and human rights-respecting iraq is vital for the region and for the world.
in writing. − there is no doubt that an effective eu-wide code of conduct on arms exports is of increased importance in the context of its accelerated militarisation, which is reflected in the proposed treaty, currently in the process of ratification in each member state. the resolution itself, not without some irony, makes it clear that with 'the evolution of the european security and defence policy (esdp), in the framework of which more and more military and civilian missions are being carried out (...) european union personnel may be threatened with weapons previously supplied by member states of the european union'. the eu is increasing its 'military equipment market', encouraging 'several attempts to harmonise national policies on the acquisition of arms and on the intra-community transfer and sale of arms' and 'a willingness to increase arms exports as a means of promoting economic interests'. the slogan is: arms race and militarization of international relations. that is why initiatives and measures aimed at at least making such an escalation possible are positive and necessary. however, as we have said before, the regulation of the arms trade will be all the more relevant if it is accompanied by a process of multilateral and reciprocal disarmament, starting in particular with the dismantling of the huge nuclear arsenals.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mrs marie panayotopoulos-cassiotou on the particular situation of women in prison and the impact of parental detention on social and family life, as there is evidence that european prisons are mainly geared to male inmates, ignoring the specific needs of women. i therefore believe that measures should be taken to improve the situation of women prisoners, particularly in the areas of social and occupational reintegration, health care and hygiene, psychological support and the preservation of family ties.
in writing. − although women make up around 4.5 to 5% of the prison population in the european union, prisons remain fundamentally male-oriented and tend to ignore the specific problems of women who constitute a small, though increasing, percentage of those in prison. the main areas of concern are health care, the situation of mothers with children in prison and vocational and social reintegration. particular attention should be paid to women's health care and hygiene needs, in particular for pregnant women, who require specialised resources and care in terms of nutrition, exercise, clothing, medication and medical care by specialised staff. children who remain with their imprisoned mothers require adequate protection and care and should not suffer any form of discrimination. the imprisonment of women can have particularly serious implications when, before being imprisoned, they were solely responsible for the education of their children. the social integration of women prisoners should be prepared during the period of detention and after release, in cooperation with social services and other relevant organisations, in order to ensure a smooth transition from imprisonment to freedom.
in writing. - we consider this report to have several merits. among them is the call for attention to a burning problem in both eu countries and developing countries, namely the need to ensure access to information in the field of sexual and reproductive health, to ensure their freedom of decision, as well as to create and promote public services for the protection and enforcement of the rights of all and of women in particular. however, we think it is important to stress that the greatest contribution to 'gender equality and women's responsibility in development cooperation' will come not from policies that promote relations of dependency and domination, the liberalisation of markets (see the eu's economic partnership agreements (epas)), the exploitation of workers, social inequalities and injustices and the disregard of human rights, which particularly affect millions and millions of children and women, but from a policy of real cooperation, based on equal rights between states, respect for national sovereignty, the right of each country to define and implement its development model that responds to the needs and aspirations of its people, a policy that truly interprets the word solidarity.
