the debate will continue on the oral question to the commission on the fight against cancer in the enlarged european union, tabled by mr miroslav ouzký on behalf of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety (o-0014/2008 - b6-0015/2008). we have to involve mrs vassiliou in this debate for the first time. i greet you, madam commissioner, i welcome you and i hope that we shall get along very well. the time will come when you will have to speak and then you will begin your work of cooperation and collaboration with the european parliament.
commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i think it is extremely important to support small and mediumsized enterprises and to stimulate their scientific and technological development. a strong technological base in smes is relevant to enhance their contribution to economic growth and development. smes are typically highly initiative-oriented and adaptable, free from stifling bureaucracies and are usually run by entrepreneurs and managers who are deeply committed to their work of creating wealth. this capacity for initiative and adaptability facilitates the launching of new businesses, involving the manufacture and/or sale of new products or the operation of new services adapted to the needs of consumers of other companies. often these new products and services may require a more solid technological base than is already available in many of these small enterprises, and this eurostars joint research and development programme, designed to support smes, may prove to be very important for the effects it may have on the so-called 'real economy'. this will help to improve the skills of small and mediumsized enterprises in various european countries, serving consumers and the european economy. this will also help to create more and better jobs. the report by our colleague mr rübig was very useful in all this.
i am not saying that we should not be concerned about the future of the european union. in this brief speech i shall concentrate on the issue of copyright. in the pre-digital world of books and records, the purchase of the work defined the normal consumer attitude. copiers and tape recorders came to shake the pay of authors, but buying remained the rule. the paradigm shift comes with the digital universe. on the net, the free sharing and circulation of ideas, information and works is freed from its old physical shackles. in this world, payment is a thing of the past. the free movement of works is the natural habitat of culture. we are fighting piracy for profit, but we are completely against the criminalisation of the consumer. some of the constraints and blockages in the digital universe are still necessary because we haven't figured out how to properly remunerate authors in any other way, but their days are numbered.
the rapporteur. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, having proposed a general framework for the cultural issues in the lisbon agenda, i have decided to welcome in my report the various proposals put forward by my colleagues, provided they do not conflict with this perspective. and so, if in some aspects of this report i have points which may be considered redundant in relation to other instruments, however adopted and already in force, they are worth as an insistence on topics deemed of the greatest relevance. the european union has a special duty to safeguard europe's cultural wealth. the european cultural heritage must be preserved, disseminated and shared within and outside the union in all its dimensions and by all means, without prejudice to the wider and more desirable openness to all other cultures, which has always been a hallmark of europe. our cultural heritage, forged in the diversity of its expressions and in the combination of its main matrices, such as greek-latin and judeo-christian antiquity, has historically placed europe at the forefront of all continents. it has proved to be a unique factor of innovation, development and progress that has spread in all directions and remains, even today, a fundamental reference of humanism, of enrichment and spiritual vitalization, of democracy, of tolerance and citizenship. in an increasingly globalised world, this cultural wealth has a core configuration whose specific and distinctive characteristics constitute a true european asset and whose identity role is essential for europe and the union, for its understanding of the world, for ensuring its cohesion, for making its mark and for asserting itself vis-à-vis other peoples. the particular expressions of the historical projection of europe's cultural heritage on other continents must give rise to special actions which highlight the factors which have built civilization, mutual understanding and the constructive approach of the peoples represented by these expressions. we recommend that the council and the commission should value the classical european heritage and the historical contributions of national cultures, over all centuries and in all dimensions, but also take into account the needs of the cultural sector in the future. we therefore suggest that 2011 be designated as the european year of the greek and latin classics, in order to draw the attention of the peoples of the union and the rest of the world to this essential aspect of cultural heritage, which is now threatened by oblivion. for the same reason, we insist that the promotion of european languages in the world and their role in the cultural creation of other continents be given greater importance, in order to facilitate mutual knowledge and understanding and the cultural interaction generated and conveyed by these languages in their non-european aspects. the community programmes currently available in the cultural sector do not, however, allow for a full coverage of the situation relating to the common cultural heritage of europeans. hence the need for specific programmes which stimulate creativity and enable wider and deeper contact with the tangible and intangible goods and values which make up the european cultural heritage, so as to facilitate their interaction in the humanistic understanding of identities and differences and in contemporary cultural production. all programmes in the cultural sector have very positive aspects for cohesion, real convergence, economic growth, sustainable development, innovation, employment and competitiveness, but this should not make us forget that culture and cultural products have a value in themselves. we remind the council of the urgent and pressing need to review the budgetary appropriations to support the actions envisaged in this commission communication and the existing actions. with all this, and the more that cannot be mentioned, i conclude by welcoming the commission's communication and the approval it has received from the council and expressing our agreement with the objectives set out in it.
the rapporteur. - madam president, after so many very cordial speeches, i regret that i have to refer by telegraph to only a few points which i consider essential, but i believe that all of them and much of what is contained in the report which has not been mentioned here contribute to enriching this debate in an extraordinary way. the first point i would like to make is that the introduction of culture in the commission's communication is a political innovation. it was emphasized by mrs trüpel and it is a question of ensuring the presence of culture in other european policies. i think this is fundamental. the second point raised by mr mikko concerns the cultural dimension which must be integrated into european foreign policy, not only of the european union but also of the member states - it is absolutely essential. the third point, raised by mr hieronymi, concerns the well-balanced balance between the economic and the economic value of culture and culture as a value in itself. just two more points. mrs staniszewska spoke of the importance of cultural action at regional and local level, which is also emphasized in the report, but i think it should be emphasized here. you have my full agreement on that. finally, i should also stress that providing access to culture for families and students, from the school and society, and building bridges between cultural heritage and the exact sciences, innovation and technology are fundamental aspects of these concerns. madam president, since i cannot go into more detail than i have just said, i would just like to conclude by saying that culture is an indispensable and inescapable system of values and collective and individual experiences, and that it is with these values and collective and individual experiences that europe must look to the future.
on behalf of the pse group. other i would like to congratulate mrs attwooll on the remarkable effort she has made to make her report as consensual as possible. this is a complex and controversial issue, but one of the utmost importance for all those concerned with the sustainability of resources, but including in this concept the sustainability of the most precious resource of all, the people who make up europe's many fishing communities. the report's balanced approach, which takes account of different perspectives, therefore seems to me to be perfectly appropriate. the result of the vote in the committee on fisheries - 21 votes in favour out of a total of 24 - is a good indication of what i have just said. but as important as not running away from this debate would be making hasty decisions. as an elected member of parliament in a member state where small-scale and multi-species fisheries predominate in southern europe, i am concerned about the introduction of management systems involving the trading of rights, which may result in benefits for the shipowners with more purchasing power to the detriment of the smaller ones. i also fear that the widespread adoption of such a system could have counterproductive effects, and could even lead to higher catches to offset the cost of acquiring the right to fish. i therefore reiterate my support for the overall conclusion of the report, which is that no decision should be taken without studies covering all the member states and the different types of fisheries, without a wider debate taking place to allow all the variables of this question to be weighed.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, i would like to begin by acknowledging the efforts of the rapporteur, mrs attwooll, in producing a balanced report on such a fundamental issue as the sovereignty of the member states in the management of their fisheries resources and the creation of private property rights for access to exploitation of this public good. however, although we value paragraph 11 of the report, it contains a number of considerations with which we disagree, such as the fact that this debate is seen as a preliminary step towards the necessary change in the current management policy or that it includes points which more or less explicitly call for the adoption of management mechanisms based on fishing rights at community level. we believe that it is up to each member state to manage its marine resources, in particular as a means of guaranteeing its food sovereignty, and we therefore reject any phased process which would lead to the future creation of a community management system based on fishing rights, i.e. on the marketing of licences, fishing days or quotas, which would necessarily lead to the private appropriation and concentration of the exploitation of a public good.
i too join my colleagues in congratulating our rapporteur, elspeth attwooll, and i would like to say that in my view the marine natural heritage must be preserved and must be used sustainably by the fishing communities that traditionally interact with it and cannot be seen as a business like any other. in this sense, i do not share the view that sees marine ecosystems and the fishing communities that interact with them as a market, where fishing rights for fish stocks can be freely traded, possibly even on the stock exchange, naturally leading to the industrialisation of the activity and putting at risk the balance of both ecosystems and fishing communities. moreover, it seems to me that the principle of relative stability cannot be called into question in any way and for this reason i think the commission should exercise the utmost caution in this debate.
mr president, i would like to congratulate my colleague, mrs graça moura, on the report that was adopted today and i would like to congratulate her and, above all, draw attention to paragraph 26, which was overwhelmingly approved by 560 votes in favour in the roll-call vote, and which draws attention to the fact that some european languages interact with other continents, with countries all over the world, and that it is important for the european union to know how to specifically promote these languages and the cultural interaction that is generated and conveyed by these languages also with non-european spaces. this is the case for english, spanish and also portuguese and, to a lesser extent, french. i am sure that commissioner orban will be able to draw the consequences of this paragraph, together with the bernat joan i marí report which we voted on two years ago, when defining the guidelines for a european policy on multilingualism. specific support for the dissemination of these languages, which are world european languages, is of unquestionable importance in the globalised world in which we live.
in writing. - we voted in favour of this report on the health policy conditions for the non-commercial movement of pet animals, taking into account health problems and their possible implications for public health. for example, regulation (ec) no 998/2003 of the european parliament and of the council harmonises the rules on the non-commercial movement of pet animals between member states or after their introduction into and re-introduction into the community from third countries. the regulation introduced, inter alia, the passport for cats, dogs and ferrets, when they are moved from one member state to another, which proves that the animal has been subjected to rabies vaccination. however, the regulation provides for temporary derogations which certain member states may apply until 3 july 2008 (articles 6 (1) and 16). article 6 (3) provides for the possibility of extending the transitional period by legislation, on the basis of a report to be submitted to the european parliament and the council by the commission before 1 february 2007, which has not happened. so now there is an agreement to extend the transitional period to allow time for the definition of the new regime to be applied.
in writing. - since the entry into force of the treaty of amsterdam, we have seen a steady development of common european policies on migration and asylum. in this context, it is essential that we can rely on comparable, reliable and objective information and data at national and european level to enable us to better understand migration phenomena, analyse the phenomenon and develop policies or take better informed decisions. however, existing data are scattered and in many cases are not reliable, comparable or even up to date. the thessaloniki european council approved the creation of a european migration network, which began as a pilot project and then as a preparatory action. i therefore support this proposal which seeks to consolidate the existing structure, making it permanent and giving it an appropriate legal basis by defining its objectives, functions, structure and financing arrangements. i agree with the amendments proposed by the rapporteur, in particular the inclusion of asylum in the name of the network and the extension of its mandate. but above all because the council's proposal to give the ep only an observer role, without voting rights, is unacceptable.
in writing. the european parliament adopted today a proposal for a council decision aimed at creating a 'european migration network'. the 'european migration network', which started as a pilot project in 2002, is based on a set of 'contact points' at national level and has as its main objective to provide 'objective, reliable and comparable information' on the immigration and asylum situation in the different member states. the present proposal aims at consolidating the existing structure in the form of a network without creating, at least for the time being, a new agency or a new observatory at eu level. while measures to improve knowledge of the reality of migration (and asylum) in the different eu countries will undoubtedly be positive, we consider it negative that such a measure serves to promote or is part of the 'communitisation' of immigration and asylum policies, which the treaty, now called 'lisbon', aims to promote and ensure. we reject the creation of common immigration and asylum policies at eu level which are security-oriented, restrictive and deeply inhumane, and which take away from the sovereignty of states (and their national parliaments) these essential competences.
in writing. − the bodies referred to in article 185 of council regulation (ec, euratom) no 1605/2002 - the community agencies - have multiplied in recent years (with the creation of more anticipated) and are increasingly assuming a supranational character, performing functions which fall within the competence of each member state. the report makes some improvements to the text proposed by the european commission, including the inclusion in the financial regulation of these bodies of the obligation to make available on each of their internet pages information on the beneficiaries of funds from their budgets, and that this information should be 'easily accessible to third parties, clear and exhaustive'. something that the regulation still in force does not provide for. however, while also requesting more detailed information on the staff, budget and work of the agencies, it accepts the commission's proposal to give these agencies more room for manoeuvre in terms of budgetary transfers, which should be followed up.
in writing. - part of the economic difficulties faced by the fisheries sector are the result of a management system that is not very transparent and not very effective, based, among other things, on the tac and quota system and the management of fishing effort. the commission communication - improving the economic situation of the fisheries sector, addresses the difficulties facing the sector and points to some new approaches to fisheries management. these include management based on 'fishing rights'. this debate is of the utmost importance for the community fisheries sector, as it opens the door to greater biological sustainability for resources and greater market intervention capacity for those responsible for the sector. there is a great diversity of trading systems and fishing rights, not always fully transparent. a serious debate is therefore needed to find ways of managing these rights in a way that ensures transparency, legal certainty and economic efficiency for fishermen. since 'fishing rights' are the backbone of fisheries management in countries with the highest fishing potential (usa, new zealand, norway, etc.), it is appropriate to discuss this possibility in the management of community fisheries. for all these reasons, the psd members supported the attwooll report.
in writing. - commissioner borg's speech was illuminating on the commission's intentions for the future of the common fisheries policy: the modification of its management system by phasing in a community system based on fishing rights. we could almost anticipate their intentions: to extend the application of such a system, at first, to even a part of the fleets in the largest number of member states, and then to create a single market for fishing rights at eu level, possibly through their trading on the stock exchange. the objectives are taken up by the european commission itself: '[...] trigger the large-scale purchase of rights, which will result in concentration in terms of ownership of quotas, geographical distribution of fishing activities and fleet composition. ' and '[...] any mechanism designed to limit the negative effects [...] should be compatible with the single market and community competition rules'. this is a matter of the utmost importance, which goes to the heart of the sovereignty of states and the management and ownership of the exploitation of a natural resource, that is, the assignment to private interests of access rights to the exploitation of a public good. an intention that can only have our most frontal rejection!
in writing. − following the dismissal of 1,549 workers in 2007 at opel portugal in azambuja, alcoa fujikura in the seychelles and johnson controls in portalegre, the portuguese government submitted an application to mobilise this fund (eur 2 425 675) to co-finance actions such as 'vocational training and certification' and wage compensation to 'incentivise' workers to accept lower wages. there is no doubt that in view of the serious consequences for workers, their families and regions of the closure of these units, any measure aimed at reducing them is urgent and necessary, but the lack of resolution of the underlying problem remains: the creation and guarantee of jobs with rights for workers and the ensuring of the socio-economic development of these regions. this is only possible with a genuine investment policy, which takes advantage of the potential of each region and prevents multinationals, after receiving large millions of euros in 'aid', from relocating or closing down in search of greater exploitation. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union's institutions, including the european parliament, the council and the commission.
in writing. − in 2006, i campaigned hard for the creation of the european globalisation adjustment fund. when it was adopted, i made a speech in the plenary where i said that this decision had a political interpretation: for the first time, the three european institutions, the council, the commission and the parliament, recognised the negative aspects of the globalisation process and that workers who were victims of factory closures due to globalisation should be financially supported. i understood that it was a way for the european union to show its presence on the ground to those suffering redundancies as a result of the closure of companies, as happened in portugal, opel, johnson and alcoa fujikara. these are often dramatic situations and the european parliament's decision to make some €2.5 million available to these workers can help to alleviate the distress they are experiencing. when people are restless and fearful, it's hard to accept change. the funds decided today and allocated to these portuguese workers are not a miracle solution, but they are certainly a way of helping these workers to have more confidence in themselves so that, with the support of the european union, they can find reasons to smile again.
in writing. − this report marks the beginning of the debate on the 2009 budgetary procedure as regards the budget of the european parliament and other institutions, not including the european commission, by far the most significant budget. among other points which we could highlight, the guidelines now proposed concerning staff policy should be considered. this is because in recent years there has been a constant pressure to reduce staff costs by opting for precarious forms of recruitment, such as recruitment through the provision of external services, in particular through temporary employment agencies, to the detriment of permanent employment contracts and the rights of these workers. this, of course, deserves our firm rejection. another recurring theme is the need to ensure the diversity and availability of all the eu's official and working languages. during the 2008 budgetary procedure, a small amount was allocated to 'encourage the administration to give priority to providing more effective linguistic support to members during official meetings', but it is not known what measures have actually been taken in this regard, especially in view of the fact that situations where this right is not respected continue to occur, see the eu-acp parliamentary assemblies.

in writing. - i support the content of this report because i consider that the proposals in it are intended to promote research and development in smes, which represent more than 99% of all enterprises in europe and employ more than 60% of the working population. in addition, the number of smes carrying out research and development activities is very small and we must therefore encourage, by all means at our disposal, the encouragement of such initiatives, which will be increasingly decisive in consolidating their competitiveness. the most decisive factor in this respect goes beyond the content of this report. it is therefore important to create multiplier effects which, through modern forms of business management, can lead to processes which, through innovation and efficiency, create value. this value creation should benefit not only the companies where it is developed, but also the whole business fabric, upstream and downstream. the adoption of this report should not make us forget the need to strengthen financial support mechanisms for start-ups, an area where many difficulties are still detected, especially for young people who want to start an entrepreneurial experience. i insist on the reduction of red tape in these processes so as not to discourage smes from committing themselves to research and development.
in writing. - according to information provided by the commission, 40% of the total eu fleet, in terms of tonnage, operates on the high seas or in third country waters. similarly, vessels from other countries also fish in community waters, in particular under the terms of the so-called 'nordic agreements'. it is therefore important that the eu has a clear system for authorising these two types of activities. the legislative proposal and the ep report represent the eu's efforts to 'simplify' the common fisheries policy (cfp) by establishing general rules and conditions for applying for and issuing fishing authorisations, both inside and outside community waters. the commission proposal clarifies the responsibilities of the commission and the member states and specifies the obligations to notify fishing activities. the amendments made by the ep report make the document fairer in some respects. this is exemplified by the increasingly flexible approach to the eligibility criteria of article 7. the psd meps therefore support the morillon report.
in writing. - at present, fishing authorisations to be granted to community vessels or to third country vessels are managed through the various bilateral agreements or with regional fisheries organisations. the proposal for a regulation aims to create a single procedure for the management of all fishing authorisations, highlighting the role of the european commission in granting or suspending these authorisations as opposed to that of the member states. among many important points which merit comment or criticism, we would point out that although this report clarifies certain aspects of the proposed regulation, such as the fact that it considers only serious infringements to be infringements which have actually been confirmed as such under national legislation - which we consider to be positive - it still does not safeguard the sovereignty of each member state as regards the management of fishing activities in its eez, which we disagree with. we therefore tabled an amendment which argued that 'the member states, as interested parties, are active participants in the procedures, including decision-making procedures' relating to the allocation of licences in this context. unfortunately, the amendment was rejected by the majority of this parliament.

in writing. - we voted in favour of this resolution in view of the current situation and the estimates of the international centre for cancer research, which state that one in three europeans will be diagnosed with cancer in their lifetime and one in four will die of the disease. in 2006, there were around 2.3 million new cancer cases and over one million cancer deaths in the european union. cancer is caused by many factors in multiple stages, requiring more prevention that addresses both lifestyle-related causes and causes related to occupational activity and the environment. according to a recent study by trade union organizations, at least 8% of the annual number of cancer deaths are directly caused by exposure to carcinogens in the workplace and this exposure could be avoided by replacing these agents with less harmful substances. it is known that there are shocking differences in the quality of cancer treatment facilities, screening programmes, science-based good practice, radiotherapy services and access to new cancer medicines, which also explains the large discrepancies in the five-year survival rate for most cancers in europe.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the riitta myller report on the mid-term evaluation of the sixth community environment action programme, given the importance of ensuring that the objectives set out therein are met, particularly as regards the thematic strategies, the protection of biodiversity and the application of community legislation, not forgetting issues such as environmental taxation or the problem of subsidies for activities harmful to the environment. more efforts are needed to respond in a timely manner to the environmental problems addressed by the targets set out in the programme.
in writing. − this report is the result of an evaluation commissioned by the european parliament's committee on the environment, public health and food safety to find out to what extent the european union has so far honoured its commitments under the sixth community environment action programme, which was adopted in 2002 and runs until 2012. this evaluation revealed that the implementation of the action programme is very or extremely late in respect of several priority objectives. it concluded that, in the light of the measures taken so far, it did not appear that the programme's priority environmental objectives would be achieved by 2012. the evaluation therefore does not support the european commission's assertion in its own mid-term evaluation that, overall, the eu is up to date with the implementation of the measures set out in the action programme. the evaluation commissioned by parliament will show that the commission's decision to present specific proposals through the thematic strategies has not, in general, produced the expected result. however, although we have voted in favour of the report in general, we disagree with some of its content.
in writing. - we know the importance of cultures and their dissemination in respecting cultural diversity, the rights of artists and the peoples of each of the member states of the european union. the report contains some positive proposals which we welcome, such as the idea of enhancing the mobility of people, products and services in the creative sector, in accordance with the rules and principles of the unesco convention on cultural diversity, and the challenge it makes to the commission to consider the possibility of creating a programme similar to the media programme. it also called on the commission to complete the work on the european digital library initiative, to stimulate and support the music, theatre and publishing sectors in order to facilitate the transnational distribution of works, and, as a preliminary measure, to establish a mechanism under the culture programme to enable the non-audiovisual cultural industries to have access to community funding for the promotion of books, music and vocational training. but we do not follow other proposals which are aimed more at defending purely business interests than at education, culture, the rights of artists and the general public.
in writing. - i welcome the excellent report by my colleague vasco graça moura on a european agenda for culture in a globalised world, which proposes a broad programme for developing a strategy both within the eu and in its relations with third countries. since at least march 2005, graça moura has been stressing that the lisbon strategy will never be able to fully achieve its fundamental objectives if it does not consider culture as one of its essential dimensions. the commission's communication is in line with this and makes culture an important item on the european political agenda. i agree with the rapporteur when he says that 'it is this globalised world which makes it ever more urgent that we affirm and strengthen european identity, without prejudice to the diversity of the cultures of the peoples of europe'. i therefore congratulate the european commission on this communication and call for the creation of the task force on culture, which was announced by president barroso but which is slow to be set up and start its work.
in writing. - there are very contradictory aspects to this report. on the one hand, there is a continuing attempt to hide the reality of europe's evolution. there is no single 'cultural heritage of europe', let alone a reference to 'humanism, tolerance, democracy', etc. the whole of european cultural history, like its history in general, is not only built up of diversity and admirable creative energy and progress, but also of violent antagonistic confrontation, of intolerance, of multiple lines and contexts of cultural domination. the single heritage is a fiction, fed earlier by cultural eurocentrism (europe as the 'vanguard' and other aspects referred to), fed today by the myth, repeated, of a 'european' cultural identity. on the other hand, however, the political intention to assert itself autonomously contains positive elements. this is of course because such an autonomous affirmation is not possible only in the context of any 'european' cultural identity, but in the context of preserving guarantees of resistance to the compressing role of the us-dominated cultural industries (defence of linguistic and cultural diversity; consideration of cultural industries as a 'protected area in relation to trade rules'; recognition that the 'eu trade balance is unfavourable in cultural goods and services'). hence the abstention vote at the end.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the commission green paper entitled 'adaptation to climate change in europe - possible action by the european union', because i share the conviction that adaptation measures are a guarantee against the negative and unavoidable effects of climate change. the early design of adaptation strategies for agriculture, water management, land use planning or public health is part of the desirable attitude in the formulation of environmental policies at community level.
in writing. − it is known that the working group ii contribution to the fourth assessment report of the intergovernmental panel on climate change predicts that almost all european regions will be negatively affected by some of the future consequences of climate change. this could be a new threat to europe's biodiversity and could undermine social development, requiring a truly transversal approach and involving the inclusion of social, economic and environmental aspects in their broadest sense. the resolution points to causes and measures which are sometimes contradictory. it is good to recognise that there are numerous studies and models at regional or local level on the likely impacts of climate change, but many of these studies lack a parallel perspective on the socio-economic dimension and the foreseeable consequences for the affected populations. it is good that the commission is invited to coordinate and support the scientific preparation of a common european database on vulnerabilities, in order to try to understand how cultural and national groups and heritages may be affected and may react to the consequences of climate change in the future. but we disagree on others, like keeping the emissions business going.

mr president, mr barrot, ladies and gentlemen, we are discussing today a second decision which lays down the rules necessary for the implementation of another initiative which has already received the political agreement of the council but has not yet been adopted. i see that initiatives against terrorism and crossborder crime have been taken in succession with a view to strengthening security and surveillance, but i regret that initiatives aimed at greater protection of fundamental rights have not had the same luck. there has continued to be a uniform set of procedural safeguards at union level and there has continued to be an appropriate legal instrument with regard to data protection under the third pillar, as vice-president barrot has just acknowledged in his speech. i therefore ask you, commissioner, to help us explain to the council that this is an unacceptable situation, especially when we take into account that the vast majority of counter-terrorism and police cooperation measures have been taken on the basis of the collection and exchange of personal data. this initiative is another example of that, and it's all the more serious if you think about it, because we're talking about the collection, storage and sharing of dna data, fingerprints and so on. the data protection rules which are laid down in chapter vi of the prüm initiative and which provide for more specific safeguards are not in themselves autonomous and, in order to function properly, require a complete and general framework, which can only be effectively ensured through the third pillar framework decision on data protection. we have very much welcomed the initiative to bring key aspects of prüm cooperation into the union framework. however, we cannot leave the work half-done. it is also essential to ensure that there is a clear, effective and general legal framework for data protection.
on behalf of the ppe-de group. the debate on amendments to the statute of the ombudsman in the committee on constitutional affairs was not easy. it was a long debate, with a lot of controversy, and the question that was essentially asked was whether the extension of the ombudsman's powers increased the rationality of those powers. we started from a clear assumption that the role of each institution in a democratic culture must be well defined and that confusion of roles must always be avoided. clearly defined roles and a rational distribution of roles are the only way to respect the legitimacy, effectiveness and accountability of the institutions. that is why the proposal to grant the ombudsman access to the court of justice has been withdrawn. however, a commitment has been made to secrecy and data protection. it also deals with cooperation with other institutions in the field of fundamental rights. access to the secret is now open, but the ombudsman cannot reveal the secret to third parties. data protection is governed by the data protection rules in force in the european union. on the subject of fundamental rights, it is clear that the ombudsman can collaborate with other institutions in this area, as i think he should. collaboration with the institutions on fundamental rights is the expression of an unwritten principle, since fundamental rights are the foundation and the aim of the european union. but the compromise reached in a debate which is not easy makes clear what i think must be the irrefutable conclusion in this matter: the ombudsman, in his institutional life, should always be clear that when exercising his powers, he must do so in accordance with the principles of necessity, appropriateness and proportionality. because that's the criteria of justice.

in writing. the report is part of the process of transposing the prüm treaty into the community acquis. this treaty is an integral part of the serious security measures which have been implemented under the cover of the so-called 'fight against terrorism' aimed at deepening crossborder cooperation at eu level in the field of 'fighting against terrorism', crossborder crime and immigration. although it contains some amendments which improve on the original proposal, the report does not prevent or denounce the creation of a worrying framework for police cooperation (including the 'establishment of joint rapid intervention teams' allowing police services from one member state to operate on the territory of another), the creation of the 'personal data bank' (including information on dna, or, if 'necessary', on the political opinions of citizens) and the facilitation of access to it by intelligence services, which constitute real violations of the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens in the different member states. the dangers of such a process are even highlighted by the european data protection supervisor himself, who points out that such instruments are being (long since implemented) without adequate safeguards for the protection of citizens' personal data. that is why we voted against it.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the adamos adamou report on organ transplantation and donation: policy action at eu level, as i consider that raising awareness of organ donation and transplantation, maintaining the non-commercial character of donations and combating global organ trafficking are important measures to ensure the quality and safety of donations in europe. given the growing need for organ transplantation, the increase in waiting lists for transplants, and the consequent increase in the number of deaths due to a shortage of donated organs, the promotion of better transplantation policies in the eu is crucial to save more lives and offer a better quality of life to european citizens.
in writing. − the therapeutic use of human organs to replace a defunct organ with one from a donor, if successful, can ensure a full and healthy life for many years for people who would otherwise often need intensive care. although the use of human organs for transplantation has increased in recent decades in eu countries, the number of people in need of a transplant still exceeds the number of organs available for transplantation. official studies indicate that some 40 000 patients are currently on waiting lists in western europe. the mortality rate for patients waiting for a heart, liver, or lung transplant is between 15 and 30 percent. to minimize the risk to the recipient, it's important to test the donors. as mentioned in the report, it is essential to screen donors and verify the presence or absence of a risk of disease transmission, which implies a series of tests. however, there is currently no consensus among member states on these tests. that is why this report is important in encouraging greater cooperation.
in writing. - there is no doubt that the so-called 'volunteering' has a very important social role, as a contribution to finding answers to the problems and needs of citizens, in particular by promoting effective solidarity and mutual assistance. we therefore disagree with the view that 'volunteering' is a 'significant saving for public services'. on the contrary, we believe that their role will be all the more important the more the public services provided and guaranteed by the states to their citizens are strengthened. as mentioned, it is essential to ensure that 'volunteering' will 'complement, not replace, the activity of public services'. 'volunteering' cannot be used as a pretext or a lever to promote the discharge of the state from its social responsibilities by giving it to pseudo-charitable organisations. it is in this context that we are calling for effective and adequate support for non-profit organizations, among many others, the cooperative movement, local authorities and societies, residents' committees, sports, recreational, cultural, youth or child-oriented associations. finally, we would stress that voluntary work also depends on workers having free time, as long as intensive exploitation is not imposed by working hours, low wages or precariousness.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report which stresses the contribution of volunteering to achieving economic and social cohesion in the eu. there are more than 100 million european citizens who are engaged in voluntary activity, which corresponds to an economic contribution of 5% of gdp on average. volunteering facilitates the direct involvement of citizens in local development and plays an important role in the acquisition of skills and in the development of the employability of volunteers, allowing them to acquire a wide range of skills and competences. i support this report which stresses that member states and regional and local authorities must recognise the value of volunteering in promoting economic and social cohesion and must set up strategies to encourage volunteering. the commission should work towards the creation of a system applicable to all community funds, the aim of which is to recognise voluntary activity as a contribution to the co-financing of projects. the commission, the member states and regional and local authorities should promote volunteering at all levels of education so that it is seen as a normal contribution to life in the community.
in writing. − i affirm the social value of volunteering and support its development and appreciation in our societies. i would like to clarify that the reality of volunteering may still be unclear in statistical data, definitions and their use. the clarifications contained in the report seem to me to be important and the measures suggested to clarify the existing data on this type of activity are necessary, as this is an unpaid activity which must therefore be clearly differentiated from the activities of non-governmental organisations. the added value of these voluntary activities is very important for our societies and it is therefore legitimate to recognise and distinguish it. however, we should not take advantage of its altruistic nature to replace the efforts that companies, the authorities responsible or the private sector must make to enhance the opportunities offered at community level. the various community funds are designed to promote the dynamism of the european economy, socioeconomic cohesion and the sustained growth and development of european societies. volunteering is a bonus that we as citizens offer to others, which we should encourage and recognise, but never a bonus that we should take advantage of or use as an excuse to reduce our efforts to offer and create an ever better quality of life in european societies.

in writing. - in recent years, from the treaty of nice to the so-called 'lisbon' treaty proposal, there has been a proliferation of community agencies or other bodies which, based on a wide range of objectives, often serve as a catalyst for strengthening the increasingly supranational character of the institutions and policies of the european union. these agencies and bodies, which were generally set up to 'coordinate' or 'assist' the member states in different fields, have been progressively increasing in number: their number, taking into account the discharge procedure, was 8 in 2000 and more than 20 in 2006! the following examples are not exhaustive: the agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders of the eu member states (frontex), the european railway agency, the european environment agency, the european agency for reconstruction (balkans), the european food safety authority, the european maritime safety agency, the european aviation safety agency, etc. as regards the discharge of these agencies, the court of auditors points out as a general consideration their failure to comply with the rules laid down in the financial regulation, the staff regulations, the award of contracts, among other examples, in the exercise of their activities.

we all know that europe and the world have been suddenly caught by surprise by a problem whose scale and economic and humanitarian consequences require a multifaceted approach and response at european and international level. this is not, of course, an agricultural problem, but it is a problem which cannot be solved without agriculture. we know the different causes, but we are far from knowing the weight of each of them in the present situation: simply increased demand, biofuels, the coincidence of bad harvests in various parts of the world, the consequences of climate change, pure speculation arising from the previous causes? the commission must be mobilized to give us a prompt and accurate answer to these questions. on the other hand, there is the increased importance of the debate we are having on the health check and the wto negotiations have to be deepened and accelerated. as policy makers, this crisis requires us to answer a few questions, of which i would like to highlight: is the liberal model which has been progressively applied to the common agricultural policy effective in dealing with these kinds of problems? how can we produce more without compromising the sustainability of resources, and what alternatives can be found, especially for animal feed? what new intervention mechanisms must we adopt so that public strategic stocks are not simply replaced by private speculative hoarding? are the priorities of the european union's cooperation policies and of international institutions set correctly? to avoid even more sudden surprises or even more serious situations, we must act quickly. the socialists, and in particular those involved in the agricultural sector, are aware of their responsibilities and are ready to take part in this debate and to contribute to finding effective solutions to what may quickly become the most important global problem.
mr president, the increase in demand from emerging economies, the increase in oil prices and climate change are factors which have contributed to the increase in food prices worldwide, but they do not explain everything. the troubled growth of financial markets has contributed to increased speculation, attracted by the returns offered by commodity funds. the evidence is the increase in the price of not only foodstuffs but also nickel, silver and gold. since 2005, food prices have increased by 83 percent, which, combined with the high percentage of income that the poorest spend on food, makes this the single most important factor in increasing poverty and inequality. but even more serious is the fact that we could be on the verge of a planetary tragedy of incalculable proportions, which could lead to starvation and the death of millions of people. this is what the international monetary fund warned when it stated that if food prices remain at current levels, more than 100 million people, mostly in africa, could die. concerted international action is therefore urgently needed to increase aid to those most in need, because we are dealing with millions of cases which are life or death. but it's not enough! the creation of mechanisms to regulate international trade and to supervise financial markets effectively is needed to prevent speculative operations which benefit only a small minority at the expense of hundreds of millions of poor and defenceless people. the european union has an obligation to take the lead in this process at world level, because only in this way can the goal of eradicating poverty and achieving peace in the world cease to be a utopia.
the rise in food prices in the european union and developing countries has a number of causes, but the contribution of the cap and the shift from agriculture to biofuels cannot be ignored. several entities are highlighting this issue. for example, the scientific council of the european environment agency has argued that the eu should suspend the 10% target for biofuels by 2020. even the president of the world bank has pointed out that some countries have nutritional problems and has asked producers of raw materials for biofuels to temporarily abandon their crops. the fao itself has already warned of social uprisings for lack of food. in several countries in africa and asia, there are demonstrations and severe social tensions caused by food shortages. jean ziegler, the un special rapporteur on the right to food, recalled that the mass production of biofuels is a crime against humanity because of its impact on world food prices. it is therefore less likely that the european commission has confirmed that it remains firm in its objective of obtaining by 2020 10% of the fuel used in road transport from biomass or oilseeds.

the recent decisions of the court of justice in the laval-vaxholm case in sweden, the viking line case in finland and now the rüffert case in germany are nothing more than clarification of the real objectives and priorities of this european union. more specifically, the 'priority' of the principle of the 'freedom of establishment' as laid down in articles 43 and 46 of the treaty, which prohibits any 'restrictions on freedom of establishment'. the court of justice considers that the freedom of workers and their representative organisations to defend their rights and interests, in particular the respect of collective agreements, is a 'restriction' as well as an 'unlawfulness' under community law. in this way, social dumping and the attack on collective bargaining and contracting in the eu are legitimised and 'competition' between workers is promoted, by imposing in practice the prevalence of the so-called 'country of origin' principle, i.e. the application of lower wages and protection of rights for workers in contractual relations with employers. these decisions expose the class nature of the eu and who really cares (and drives) its neoliberal policies, refuting the whole discourse around a so-called "social europe", demonstrating how eu policies are dealing with the hard-won rights of workers.
the commission's proposal for a regulation on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster is a good one. europe cannot embark on the exercise of pointing the finger at china out of fear, nor can it align itself with unprincipled competition by avoiding beijing's self-interested methods and criteria. both europe and china have an obligation to contribute to the achievement of the millennium development goals: poverty reduction and conflict resolution in africa. both must assume that only by promoting sustainable development and good governance can their own interests and investments be sustainable and seen as legitimate in africa. in this report we have tried to look at china's presence in africa objectively, recognising both the positive and negative impacts. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is based on the following principles: first, the eu needs to give a coordinated response to the challenges posed by china's supposedly unconditional policy. this response cannot be without regard to european principles. the eu must remain committed to development cooperation policy, especially with regard to human rights conditionality. because without respect for human rights there can be no good governance and without good governance and the rule of law that it implies, there will be no sustainable development in africa or anywhere else in the world. secondly, europe must involve china in the discussion of its african policies, but this cooperation cannot, of course, take place over the heads of africans. this trilateral engagement requires adequate support for the role to be played by african institutions such as the african union, nepad, other regional institutions and national governments and parliaments. europe should therefore increase its support for the strengthening of african civil societies to promote accountability by their governments. in this report we recommend that the eu should not miss opportunities to speak frankly with china, or about china in africa, particularly where this would involve private or public criticism. china wants to be seen as a responsible actor in africa, but often invokes the rhetoric of non-interference to try to justify unacceptable actions, such as the continued complacency towards the sudanese regime's blockade, the deployment of a un-african union hybrid force - long overdue in darfur - or its most recent and outrageous shipment of arms to the mugabe regime on a ship that is being - quite rightly - prevented from disembarking by zimbabwe's neighbouring countries. everything china does in africa actually has a political impact, whether it's positive or negative. on the other hand, china is proving to be a pragmatic, quick-learning power. it is therefore crucial that europe does not fail to make clear to beijing that what is expected of a permanent member of the un security council such as china is indeed to contribute to the promotion of the principles and objectives of the united nations. in this report we propose that the eu encourage china to increase its participation in multilateral donor meetings and to adopt specific internationally accepted criteria and guidelines on aid transparency, extractive industries, good governance, environmental protection, labour rights, etc., in order to ensure that africa is making a real contribution to poverty reduction, the millennium development goals and the promotion of peace and security. but europe must also look in the mirror and learn from its own mistakes and shortcomings in africa. member states need to deliver on official development assistance pledges and small and targeted aid will only help to enhance china's merit in providing rapid financing to africa. europe must improve the effectiveness of its aid and ensure coherence between its various policies, and this means that it must stop ignoring the crimes committed by certain oppressive african regimes, with whom it continues to deal, as usual, in flagrant contradiction to its proclaimed criteria and principles. in conclusion, mr president, i would like to thank the excellent cooperation i have received from the shadow rapporteurs and other colleagues whose amendments have greatly enriched this report. i hope that broad consensus will continue to be reached tomorrow, especially since there are only a few amendments to be voted on. i myself have tabled three amendments: two involve minor corrections and the third is to reaffirm the european parliament's position, calling for the european union code of conduct on arms exports to become legally binding, thus avoiding the current paragraph 62 from repeating the call already contained in paragraph 66.

in writing. − the european global navigation satellite system (gnss), as the first community infrastructure and because of its technological importance in relation to space, can only succeed through a common will. the european gnss is designed to include two programmes: egnos and galileo. the importance of gnss is mainly due to the fact that it provides an alternative and complementary system to the us and russian systems. this objective involves a strategic, economic, industrial, security and many other interests which no member state can implement alone. as the first programme to have community funding and infrastructure, parliament will have, together with the council, increased responsibility for regulating the implementation and operation of the programmes. for the reasons i have outlined and because the completion of this project will represent a historic strategic milestone in the technological launch and autonomy of the eu, gnss and the report mentioned above deserve my full support as a solution for the future.
in writing. - the directive in question was designed to create a uniform status for third-country nationals legally residing in the territory of the union after five years of legal and uninterrupted residence in a member state. the aim of this initiative is to extend the scope of the directive to beneficiaries of international protection, in order to provide them with legal certainty in terms of residence and rights comparable to those of nationals. however, a gap remains as the directive does not provide for mutual recognition and the transfer of international responsibility to another member state, which ultimately prevents them from enjoying a right of free movement and establishment within the eu territory after their status has been recognised. the examination of these transfer requests thus continues to be governed by the 1951 geneva convention and the europe agreement of the council of europe. in this situation, it is equally important to ensure that the second member state concerned respects the principle of non-refoulement, so that the person concerned is not returned to a country where he or she is in danger, however much that person should be returned to the member state which granted him or her such protection. in all other respects i think they should meet the same requirements and be subject to the same requirements as the directive.
in writing. − the evaluation of the budgetary implementation of the 10th european development fund should not be purely accounting. that is not the role of parliament, as the report under vote clearly states. rather than discussing the integration of the edf into the commission's budget or the rules on the use of the remainder of each financial year, what concerns us is the consistency between the use of these resources and the political aims of the european union in relation to the acp countries. what is important here is that the reality we find on the ground today is very different from that which existed when these instruments and their framework were created. in addition to the china factor, which is to be taken into account in many of these countries, the effects of changes in the agricultural and food market, climate change and the new approach of the united states to africa must be considered. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the ana gomes report on china's policy and its effects on africa, as i considered that, in the light of china's growing presence on the african continent, the european union should seek, by adopting a common position on dialogue, to encourage china to guide its political and economic action in africa by criteria which do not conflict with the promotion of peace, human security, the rule of law or sustainable development. i also share the call for the european union itself to persevere in promoting respect for the principles on which it is founded, regardless of the success of its dialogue initiatives.
in writing. - the report in question is a fair account of the current state of chinese policy in africa, detailing investment, financing and policy consequences. unfortunately, in the proposals it is unrealistic, suggesting repeatedly that the eu should encourage china to adopt ideal behaviour in the field of human rights, workers' rights, respect for the environment, and finally to do in its foreign policy what it does not do in its internal policy. in the chapter on what should be done about the (correct) portrayal of chinese policy in africa and its consequences, there is a missing thread of what should be an eu strategy of its own and in partnership with countries such as india, brazil and (unacceptable failure) the united states. the current world situation is far from being able to be framed in the paradigms that have shaped geostrategic thinking in recent decades. the emergence of new economies with very different characteristics, the widespread and globalised increase in consumption, competition in the acquisition of essential goods and raw materials, the threat of social uprisings, the risk of preference for political regimes with muscles - all these new realities would require analysis and, above all, a more strategic and forward-looking proposal. that is why i abstained from voting on this report.

in writing. − the problem of biodiversity loss is one of the greatest challenges facing society today, and is becoming even more worrying with the effects of climate change. concern about the loss of biodiversity due to climate change goes beyond the protection of endangered species. indeed, the reduction of biodiversity makes ecosystems less productive and less effective in the services they provide to human populations. for example, carbon sequestration decreases dramatically in soils depleted of biodiversity, making climate change even more acute. i therefore support this resolution, hoping that the eu will continue to take an ambitious stance within the united nations convention on biological diversity.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by anne ferreira on the green paper on market instruments for environmental and related policy purposes, recognising that the use of such instruments is essential in the pursuit of workable and effective environmental policies. measures that improve the functioning of markets, such as the application of the polluter-pays principle, which allow for the imputation of costs to economic activities that result in environmental damage, are a form of state intervention to be encouraged, with evidence of environmental protection.
in writing. - i support the anne ferreira report because i consider the use of market-based instruments such as taxation, subsidies or emissions trading for environmental purposes to be an important, but not the only, tool for promoting sustainable development. although i agree with the report in general terms, i consider it premature to introduce a single european co2 tax, as i consider it not very practical to have this tax coexist with the european emissions trading system. i also disagree with the idea of replacing existing community provisions for the protection of the environment with market instruments which, by their very nature, are no alternative to regulation.
in writing. − following an initiative by the european commission, this report sets out a set of guidelines by the european parliament for the creation of market-based instruments for environmental and related policy purposes - a perspective which raises our most serious reservations and concerns. the aim is to reduce pollution and protect the environment by applying so-called market measures, implementing the polluter-pays principle, the costs of which will ultimately be borne by final consumers, usually households, who already bear the brunt of paying environmental taxes and duties. the report even mentions the payment of water consumption fees that reflect the costs of using the resource and the environmental costs. it is noted that there are already proposals to replace income-based taxation with a taxation based on the polluter-pays principle, either at the level of individual countries or as the basis for a future eu own resource. in addition to taxation measures, a system of trading in co2 emission allowances is introduced, where large economic interests dominate and financial speculation is encouraged. that's why i'm voting against it.
in writing. − since january 2005, eu listed companies are obliged to use international accounting standards for their consolidated financial statements. these standards are developed by a private organisation (the international accounting standards committee foundation and the international accounting standards board (iascf/iasb)) which relies on private funds (mostly from companies in the same industry) and is not subject to any public scrutiny. this report, although it contains elements which merit our reservations, proposes some measures aimed at overcoming this situation, being cautious about the possibility of applying this type of international accounting standards to small and mediumsized enterprises. however, it must be made clear that palliatives - measures that seek to minimise the consequences of financial speculation and prevent the occurrence of situations that lead to the collapse of the international financial system as a way of perpetuating the increasing liberalization of capital movements - are not the cure for the patient. we must tackle the root of the problem: the progressive financialization of the economy and the increasing financial speculation, with the consequent flight of investment from the productive sphere. we must put the financial systems at the service of the progress of peoples and their countries and not of big capital!

mr president, commissioner, i would like to begin by welcoming the work that the commission has been doing with the social partners to revise the directive on the european works council. but i understand that the distance between the european discourse and the concrete realities of citizens' daily lives has contributed to the increase in the lack of trust between companies and workers. raising the level of trust between the parties has thus become crucial if the european union is to become more competitive and more supportive. the more intensive the social dialogue, the more transparent the decisions taken in the context of adjustment or restructuring processes. by improving the flow of information between employers and workers, we will be contributing to a better understanding of the impact of international phenomena, as well as to a better acceptance by both sides of the search for solutions to restructuring processes. the legal mechanisms relating to the procedures for consultation and participation of workers should therefore be revised and modernised in order to provide a legal framework which promotes the articulation of social dialogue. it is with this logic and this thought that i call on the european trade union confederation to reconsider its position and to sit down at the negotiating table to discuss this proposal for a directive with employers' representatives. if that is not possible, i shall have to regret it, but i must also say that the commission must take up its responsibilities and it would be good if the process of revising this directive were completed during the term of office of this parliament and this commission.

the debate on the european works council brings to the table a number of proposals which go in the right direction: to deepen the idea of participation, cooperation and partnership between the various parts of the enterprise. but there is also in this debate a constant insistence on an anti-economic view which, in pursuit of a generous purpose, often results in a set of proposals which do not promote economic success or guarantee employment. this is the case with measures which try to save jobs even when the firms or the industry concerned are not viable. no one would think of banning the use of digital cameras or advocating a social surcharge on their price. however, the widespread consumption of it has directly caused the loss of thousands of jobs in the industry that produces film for "old" cameras. the broad participation of workers must be based on an idea of employability, of protecting people, of overcoming economic crises, and not on a vision where economic reality is a detail. technological developments and the opening up of markets must be seen as opportunities, and this is the direction in which the business dialogue should be directed.

the real crisis in large areas of northern portugal, resulting from the closure of many small and mediumsized enterprises, the relocation of multinationals and the practice of very low wages, has forced more than 100 000 workers in recent years to move to spain and other countries of the european union, in most cases to work in civil construction. but they have often been victims of precarious situations, in many cases of abandonment, in others of breach of contracts and promises made, of lower wages than the legal ones, of working overtime, and finally of the general breach of obligations by the companies that hire them. we therefore insist on the urgent need for effective monitoring in the countries in this situation and the urgency of taking action against such illegalities. for example, the unions have pointed to the suspension of the license of construction companies that do not respect the rights of workers and the requirement of a monthly report with the full list of workers in their service, including those who are displaced, and the fulfillment of their obligations.

in writing. - considering it important to maintain and improve the agreement with the republic of seychelles, we agree with the view that it is inappropriate to include in the text of the protocol (which lays down fishing opportunities and the financial contribution) considerations on the state of local port infrastructure and the possibility of changing matters (including the objectives of the use of financial contributions) which are the exclusive competence of the seychelles authorities. we also reject the proposal to include measures such as the suspension of licences by the european commission which do not take into account, in particular, the respect and safeguarding of the member states' competences. furthermore, the principle of equal pay for equal work remains not respected, as the agreement only provides that the conditions of remuneration of seychelles crews on board vessels from eu countries which will benefit from the agreement may not be lower than those applicable to seychelles crews performing similar tasks on board vessels from that country.
in writing. - the application of more specific rules, with specific, different and specific measures and exceptions, which are suitably adapted to the economic realities of the ors and more favourable to their productive capacities, deserve our support. this report aims at the application of a special rate of excise duty to beer produced in madeira. this rate, which is lower than the rate fixed at national level, applies where the annual production of the brewery does not exceed 300 000 hectolitres. as the commission points out, the price of locally produced beer, even with the 50% tax advantage, remains 7,5% higher than the retail price of beer produced in mainland portugal and sold on the madeira market. if the advantage is no longer present, local production will not be able to compete. for all these reasons, and taking into account the specificities and requirements of the situation in the outermost regions, we support measures such as this one which aim to guarantee the right to produce according to the region's own potential, which recognize the regional economy and, consequently, guarantee the survival of the local brewing industry in the face of the national and multinational market.
in writing. - the european commission and the european parliament itself should pay greater attention to the cotton sector, which is of major socioeconomic importance for certain regions of the european union, notably greece and spain. the fact is that the introduction of the principle of single payment of production-dissociated aid in the 2003 cap reform led the commission in 2006 to put this principle into practice in the cotton sector. but spain appealed to the european court of justice, stating that this reform had not been preceded by any impact study, which was eventually accepted by the court, which annulled the application of the new cotton scheme. the only difference is that the proposal which the european commission has now put forward is virtually identical to the previous one. and just over a year after the reform of the cmo for cotton was implemented, its disastrous consequences are already apparent: production in the sector was reduced by about 20% in greece and by more than 50% in spain. similarly, the number of agricultural holdings fell by 11% in greece and by 25% in spain. the factories themselves are threatened. that is why we voted against this resolution.
in writing. - at a time when capitalism is facing a deepening crisis and its contradictions are deepening, this resolution and the objectives set for the creation (in the long term) of the so-called 'transatlantic market' represent a real break with the system, pointing to the increasing liberalization of the markets of these two poles of the 'triad' and pillars of nato as a 'way out'. in addition to reaffirming the strategic 'transatlantic' partnership, the resolution is a genuine roadmap for the liberalisation of financial markets and trade relations between the eu and the us, listing the obstacles to greater competition and capitalist concentration, for the benefit of the big financial and economic groups. the resolution, in an (impossible) attempt to disguise the real aims, contradictions and consequences of the creation of the so-called 'transatlantic market', does not fail to express presumed social or environmental concerns. however, these appear to arise only as a function of and as variables of capitalist competition, particularly at the wto level. although it mildly confronts the brutal reality of 'capitalist globalisation', the resolution glosses over its profound consequences for workers and people, for small and medium-sized enterprises, not only in the eu and the us but also internationally.
