in writing. − the lack of information on deep-sea fisheries, as well as data on landings, fishing effort and their implications for the stocks of each species, is a need that needs to be addressed urgently. this is all the more so since this information is essential for the preparation of scientific studies and opinions, which in turn make a decisive contribution to the establishment of appropriate fisheries management measures. we therefore consider it important that this should be one of the priorities of member states' action to improve the collection and availability of reliable data, including the analysis of the reasons for non-application, or less correct application, of the management measures in force, as referred to in the report. the possibility raised by international bodies that some of these species may be overfished reinforces this need. the objective should be to adopt a precautionary approach, seeking a balance between fishing opportunities and the stability of stocks. we therefore support the amendments tabled. we believe that the measures to be adopted should take account of the specific nature of each species, the fishing zone and the fishing gear used, particularly the more selective ones with the least impact on the seabed.
in writing. - it is well known that the professional lobbying sector - with the aim of influencing the decision-making process of the european union - is developing rapidly and steadily in brussels. at the very least, therefore, it is necessary to set out rules to ensure information about the interests that lobbyists represent, although it is still difficult to ensure transparency and to avoid unethical practices. that is why we voted in favour of the report. but we cannot but regret that the proposals put forward by our group, in particular those which advocated that interest representatives, in addition to the obligation to register, should also be obliged to disclose the expenditure on their activities, in particular by disclosing the same information on interest representation expenditure to members of the european parliament as the members are obliged to disclose in their financial statements, have not been adopted.
in writing. − the changes in our globalised world and the consequences for institutions are undoubtedly reflected in an increasing exposure to the various social actors. we therefore see more and more groups turning to this parliament or the commission with specialist information, which is admittedly important. it is therefore necessary to help ensure that these new interest groups are clearly identified and that the rules for their operation are established and enforced. in the report now voted we find a definition of 'interest representatives' together with measures to assess the implications of a common register between parliament and the commission. the commission has also adopted a communication on the implementation of the european union strategy on the protection of the environment and sustainable development. i believe that these measures are important steps towards ensuring greater clarity and legitimacy in the decision-making process of european policymakers, especially after the vote avoided some amendments which would only serve to distort a correct assessment of this activity in the name of outdated ideological prejudices.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the white paper on sport. lack of physical activity has negative consequences for the health of european citizens, favouring cases of overweight, obesity and many chronic diseases such as cardiovascular disease and diabetes. for this reason, i have advocated the importance of medical advice for women on the potential benefits of physical activity during pregnancy and after childbirth. the importance of non-discriminatory rules for sports competitions should also be stressed, by establishing equal prizes for men and women.
in writing. − the report included proposals we put forward in the parliamentary committee to recommend adequate representation of specific associations for the various categories of sports stakeholders in the decision-making bodies of international and national federations and to advocate preventive measures and health checks for young sportsmen and women, ensuring respect for the rights enshrined in the un convention on the rights of the child. the plenary adopted further proposals that we presented, including recommendations on: the need to provide 'dual-career' training, sport and academic, to young sportsmen, to ensure the reintegration of professional sportsmen into the labour market at the end of their careers; the importance of promoting sport practice, ensuring access to sport for all and equal opportunities, investing in the training of sports teachers and coaches and in more public sports facilities, and the state should take on the burden of security for non-professional competitions organised by non-profit organisations; the value of the achievements of women in sports and the fight against discrimination in prizes; the defence of career opportunities for women in areas related to the world of sport, including in decision-making positions, and calling attention to non-professional sport. but we disagree with the references to the treaty of lisbon.

the report by mr jens holm, on behalf of the committee on international trade, on trade in raw materials and goods (2008/2051 (ini)) (a6-0134/2008) follows.
on behalf of the pse group. i would like to begin by greeting the rapporteur. the difficulties in accessing raw materials today are largely the result of structural change in their respective markets, which is linked to changes in the international economy. the raw material market has traditionally evolved in a cyclical manner, going from periods of shortages to periods of shortages and reaching some points of equilibrium. today we seem to be beginning to face a new situation, namely a situation of structural shortages, which is largely the result of a sudden increase in demand resulting from the fact that several emerging countries are rapidly advancing in industrialization and urbanization processes. it is clear that there must be calls to facilitate access to raw materials, at home and, if possible, within the world trade organisation. but that must not blind us to another vital question: the commission's proposal is that the commission should be able to take the necessary steps to ensure that the community's energy policy is not distorted by the fact that it is not in line with the community's objectives. this forces us, the european union, who are major importers of raw materials, to look at this issue with particular concern and forces us right away, on the one hand, to see the impact this can have worldwide, because it can lead to excessive pressure on the consumption of raw materials with very negative environmental consequences and economic and social organization in developing countries, but it must also force us, the european union, to look within ourselves and to understand our difficulties. this raises two questions that seem fundamental. one has to do with the need for us, in the long term, to promote a revision of our own model of economic development, because it is not compatible with a situation in which there is an over-exploitation of raw materials. secondly, it should also lead us to invest more in applied scientific research in order to ensure greater innovation, in order to recycle raw materials, in order to find new answers to the new problems that this situation of structural shortages is creating for us.

in writing. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's energy policy is not undermined by the use of fossil fuels. this proposal, which establishes the fuel cells and hydrogen joint undertaking, is the result of the work of the european technology platform on fuel cells and hydrogen and aims to contribute to the implementation of the environmental technologies action plan. these are very quiet and highly efficient energy conversion units which could allow for a substantial cumulative reduction of greenhouse gas and other pollutant emissions, as they can run on hydrogen or other fuels such as natural gas, ethanol or methanol. the introduction of hydrogen as a highly flexible energy carrier could contribute positively to energy security and to the stabilisation of energy prices, since hydrogen can be produced from any primary energy source, thus introducing a certain diversity in the transport sector, which is currently dependent on oil. although significant eu public funds have already been channelled into fuel cell and hydrogen research, it is unlikely that these technologies will be commercialized as quickly as would be desirable.
in writing. - the community tobacco fund is intended exclusively to promote information campaigns on the harmful effects of smoking. the proposal submitted by the european commission provides for an amount equal to 5% of the tobacco aid granted for the calendar years 2008 and 2009 to be transferred to this fund. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' in the context of the directive. it is known that, unfortunately, the european commission has been moving forward with the dismantling of production aid, which has contributed to the decline in its production in portugal, although it continues to be imported from the countries that produce it. the commission continues to link this fund to the support scheme for producers of tobacco by-products, arguing that this is the only source of financing envisaged. in accordance with this logic and on the assumption that information campaigns will continue to be useful, the amendments seem to be correct. it also seems appropriate to support the recent request formally submitted to the commission by almost all producer member states for the commission to submit a proposal for a regulation to extend the current tobacco support scheme until 2013, to be addressed in the context of the ongoing discussions on the cap health balance.
in writing. - the current situation shows that, ten years after the first guidelines for the employment policies of the member states, there is less and less employment with rights, which in itself shows that this strategy is not aimed at promoting employment with rights. on the other hand, its constant change, accompanied by the increasingly neoliberal economic orientations of the european union, has contributed to greater precariousness of employment. the rapporteur includes some mitigating measures relating to poverty or social inclusion, but in reality she does not mention the need to break with the current, totally neoliberal macroeconomic and employment policies, where the primacy of competition and flexibility prevail, so that these proposals are merely a smokescreen, not addressing the problems at their source. some other proposals even go so far as to promote flexicurity, or rather deregulation of the labour market, advocating flexible and reliable contractual arrangements based on modern labour law, collective agreements and the organisation of work, and stating that member states should implement their own action plans, based on the common principles of flexicurity adopted by the council. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. − the budgetary procedure has now started with the presentation by the european commission of the proposal for the community budget for 2009. in previous budgetary processes, the budget for the european parliament has absorbed about 20% of the amount entered under heading 5 - administrative expenditure - of the multiannual financial framework. the rapporteur proposes to maintain similar levels for the 2009 budget. such a decision should not make it impossible or impede the provision of financial resources to respond adequately to the identified needs for reinforced staff and for the improvement of interpretation and translation services, while respecting equality and the right to use all official languages in the european parliament and in the activities promoted by it. this has been a recurring problem, as the need to improve services such as interpretation and translation is often pointed out, but the necessary financial resources are not allocated to them, often resorting to rules that have been precisely created to hinder the use of different languages. the criteria adopted in the joint acp-eu parliamentary assemblies are as follows: the report also makes no mention of guaranteeing workers' rights, particularly when the ep has in recent years increasingly resorted to outsourcing services.
in writing. - in this report we look beyond the traditional trade in raw materials and commodities. in the new international context, various factors and components of production can be considered as raw materials, including energy. the price escalation of these products is serious for european industry, which buys them across borders. markets respond to increased demand from more producers, while facing natural and environmental constraints and reacting to financial speculation. it is worrying that this international situation has favoured a price level which is likely to undermine economic growth in europe. if this trend holds, the race for resources will generate a pressure and a shortage that promises to challenge many generations of managers and will surely have implications for the governance of the modern world. the european parliament calls on the commission to raise the issue of access to raw materials markets in the wto. the aim is reciprocity, and this organization is a suitable way. the negotiations on these products should never come down to the regional level, in order to promote integration, development and sustainability. the prevention of large-scale speculation and conflict requires that we be able to get our trading partners who hold these resources to pay fairly for their goods.
in writing. - we do not share the view on trade in raw materials contained in the report. we do not agree with the criticism of third countries for setting up policies and measures introduced 'to create obstacles to free and fair access to raw materials ... which prevent eu (!) companies from accessing raw materials and goods'. the sovereign right of each country to decide on the use of its raw materials or the trade in its goods is inalienable. it is up to the people of each country to decide how to use their resources and the wealth they create. what the report does not say is that the real problem lies in the neoliberal model of the eu. imbued with neo-colonialist ambitions, it seeks to reduce many countries to the status of raw material producers for eu countries, using technology and domination and control of market mechanisms - including financial speculation - to promote economic dependence and exploitation by transnational corporations. what is needed is a radical break with the prevailing economic and social model, eliminating the dominator/dominated or exploiter/exploited relationships, defending national sovereignty, developing the economic potential of each country and the complementarity of its external relations, producing to meet the needs of the people, preserving the planet.
in writing. - there are news which, although good at their origin, do not cease to worry us about their consequences. that is partly what is happening with the rise in the price of raw materials. the good news is that, as various indices show, a growing share of the world's population is accessing levels of consumption that were previously unknown to them. the problem, however, is that some of the consequences, especially the immediate ones, of this growth in consumption - and therefore in demand - may be determining. the laws of economics, even in distorted markets, work, and an increase in demand is matched by an increase in supply, or, as has been the case, by an increase in price. as it has been. the european union must promote a general opening up of markets, to enable more and more producers to benefit from increased demand, and it must encourage increased trade, while at the same time we have a duty to support directly those who are suffering immediately from these new circumstances: those who have no way of coping with an increase in the prices of essential goods. market distortion rarely produces positive effects, especially in the long term. but nothing prevents us, on the contrary, from financing those who have less.
, in writing. the resolution proposed in this report contains recommendations on the balance sheet and future prospects of the strategy for the outermost regions, among which i highlight: the use of indicators other than gdp to measure the level of cohesion achieved; better coordination of cohesion policy and other community policies across the board to increase synergies and better adapt current and future european policies to the realities of the outermost regions; policies and measures in their favour which are not transitional, adapted to their different needs and respond to their permanent constraints; community support for their agriculture and provision of support measures for their respective fisheries sectors; differentiated treatment in the field of transport, including civil aviation in the ets debate; inclusion of the future strategy for the outermost regions in the lisbon strategy; placing the future of the union's policy on the outermost regions in the centre of attention; the need to ensure that the implementation of the eu's policy on the outermost regions is conditional on the implementation of the eu's immigration strategy; the special attention paid to the implementation of the eu's policy on the outermost regions and the need to ensure that the outermost regions are compensated for their specific needs. it deserves my support and that of my political group. i have called for its approval and have voted in favour of the report.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. some argue that this is a resolution on regional policy and not on fisheries. a sheer fallacy. the resolution is the ep's contribution to the future of eu policies for the outermost regions, so it is here that the proposals adopted, in particular those adopted by the ep's committee on fisheries - as was the case with the ep resolution on maritime policy - should be explained. that is why we insist on presenting them again, and in line with the positions we have taken in portugal. we also regret the rejection of our proposal which clearly stated that community measures to support the outermost regions should be permanent. the rapporteur justifies that the aim is that one day these measures will no longer be necessary. the commission has also proposed that the community should be able to provide the erdf with a loan of ecu 1 billion for the construction of a new railway line in the south of the country.
in writing. − the ors have specific features which have been taken into account in european measures to support european development and growth. however, there is still a lot to be done to develop it further and to make even more use of this frontier with other world economic blocs. the transversal and complementary measures for the outermost regions have contributed to an improvement in the economic and social situation of these regions and it remains important to work on reducing the accessibility gap, improving competitiveness and regional integration. however, there are still difficulties on the ground which are not being taken into account. we can think of the question of preserving traditional agriculture, of increasing support for the development of structural sectors or of maintaining differentiated tax systems. the development of the specific strengths of the outermost regions is thus the strategy to ensure the sustainable development of the outermost regions in areas of attraction and cooperation. the introduction of climate change, demographic change and the management of migration flows, agriculture and maritime policy as new priorities is a good measure, to be complemented by the necessary diversification of the outermost regions' economies, with their specific characteristics and the widest possible application of the rules in force, using the most appropriate instruments to solve the specific problems of the outermost regions.
in writing. - a genuine consumer protection policy must be based on a number of principles. firstly, there must be a fair policy for sharing and redistributing income, based on living wages, adequate remuneration for producers, particularly micro and small farmers, industrialists and traders, which encourages local food markets and promotes food security and food sovereignty. secondly, there must be an effective policy to combat speculative commercial and financial activities, consumer information and transparency. the report does not deal with these matters. on the contrary, it defends positions which give more attention to defending the interests of economic and financial groups and the liberalisation of services than to consumers in general, although it occasionally makes some positive proposals, but only in a framework of complete neoliberalism, where consumers are the weakest link in the whole process. for example, the report stresses that greater liberalisation of the services market is necessary, in particular to promote competition and thus to offer better prices to consumers, which we know is contradictory and only serves the interests of companies. that is why we could not vote in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the liz lynne report on progress on equal opportunities and non-discrimination in the eu, given the need to urge the european commission to strictly monitor the transposition of directives 2000/43/ec and 2000/78/ec on equal treatment between persons and the application of national legislation deriving from them. i would stress that women are particularly vulnerable to discrimination at work, especially in relation to their choice of maternity. the right to non-discrimination in any form is a fundamental and basic principle of the european union which, if it is not enforced by effective legal mechanisms, will lose its meaning.
in writing. − the report contains positive aspects, including the insistence on the commission and the member states to end all discrimination on the basis of employment contracts, guaranteeing all workers equal treatment, protection of their health and safety and provisions on working and rest periods, freedom of association and representation, protection against unfair dismissal, collective bargaining and collective actions. it also stresses the importance of access to training and the continuing protection of acquired rights through the coverage of education and training periods, the improvement of access to care and the maintenance of basic social rights such as pension rights, the right to training and the right to unemployment benefit during periods of change in professional situation, between two employment contracts or in the transition from employment to self-employment. the epp therefore tried to amend the report in several respects, notably in the content of the demand for an anti-discrimination directive, but failed to do so and voted against. we rejected the ppe's proposals and supported the rapporteur, although we disagreed with some of the points in the report.
in writing. − the active and committed advocacy of non-discrimination does not mean and should not be confused with the relativisation where everything is equal, everything is equivalent and all choices, options, or circumstances have equal value in the legal order. the promotion of policies that defend larger families, for example, does not in any way infringe the principle of non-discrimination. the same is true of the refusal to give legal framework to all possible forms of human relations, which can be equated with any kind of discrimination. what i defend, what i consider it my duty to defend in the field of non-discrimination is, above all, the defence of a broad concept of individual freedom, and not a collectivist and statist view of freedoms, where only what is promoted by the state is considered non-discriminatory. society can and does have preferences, expressed in public policy. what it cannot and should not do is impose or prevent behaviour which does not conflict with the freedom of others.
in writing. − we believe that a maritime policy based on cooperation between member states (ms), which would add value and boost the sea-related policies and measures defined by each country, could have a positive impact. however, although more backward than in the previous report, the ep reaffirms objectives for an integrated maritime policy with which we cannot agree. it is also imbued with a federalist and geo-strategic vision of the use of each member state's eez; it advocates the rapid integration of intra-community maritime transport into the internal market, i.e. its liberalisation; insists on the initiatives aimed at creating a european coast guard, an area of competence for each member state; advocates the incorporation of shipping into emissions trading, another business; and, paradoxically (or not...) advocates that maritime policy be properly taken into account from 2013 onwards in the community budget (???), i.e. advocates the political/economic domain centralized in the eu, once again, without giving anything in return (even if this was ever acceptable)... the ep resolution certainly contains proposals with which we agree - some of which we have drawn up - but these do not erase the negative content of the resolution. that's why i'm voting against it.
madam president, i welcome and support the ria report in general, particularly where concerns are expressed about the implications of the closure of the ak party. on the other hand, the settlement of the cyprus question now has a fabulous opportunity which must be seized. it is also essential, as it says, that the turkish government pursue reforms while respecting pluralism and diversity in a democratic and secular turkey, and that all citizens are able to develop their cultural identity within the turkish democratic state. of course, progress is also needed in other areas, such as the defence of trade union rights and further progress towards effective gender equality, but the ria report recognises that a number of steps needed for the modernisation of turkish society have already been taken. madam president, turkey's march towards full integration must continue on the terms agreed by the european council and voted on in this parliament. no more, no less than that.
in writing. − it is positive that the closure of mercury mines in the community poses environmental and social problems and that projects and other initiatives should continue to be supported on the basis of available funding instruments in order to enable the affected areas to find viable solutions for the environment, employment and local economic activities. it was also agreed that the applicant for the licence will take the necessary measures, by means of financial or equivalent security, to ensure that the obligations arising from the licence (including post-closure maintenance operations) will be fulfilled and that the closure operations will be carried out. it was also agreed that industrial sectors obtaining mercury from natural gas cleaning or as a by-product of non-ferrous metal extraction and smelting operations should submit the relevant data to the commission and the competent authorities of the member states concerned. the commission should make this information publicly available. we also believe that it is right to encourage the provision of technical assistance to developing countries and countries with economies in transition, including assistance aimed at facilitating the transition to alternative mercury-free technologies and the phasing out of the uses and emissions of mercury and mercury compounds.
in writing. - it is important that the rapporteur has acknowledged that, according to the judgment of the court of justice of 23 october 2007 (c-440/05), criminal legislation and rules of criminal procedure are not a matter for the community and cannot determine the type and degree of criminal sanctions to be applied. amendments were therefore made to the proposal for a directive which the european commission had submitted and which was not acceptable. it is also important that the commission and the council have accepted these amendments. but there is still an insistence that the community legislature should be able to impose on the member states the obligation to impose penalties to ensure that the rules it adopts on environmental protection are fully effective. as the role of the member states in the whole process was not very clear, we opted to abstain in the final vote.
in writing. − the proposal for a regulation is justified by the commission's new political approach to simplifying legislation and better regulation. i agree with the commission's proposal, which succeeds in simplifying procedures by reducing the number of internal inspections, while maintaining the necessary level of rigour of the previous provisions on the collection of structural statistics relating to crop and livestock production, agricultural labour and equipment used. on the other hand, and for the sake of simplification, the proposal merely introduces a new type of inspection and does not lead to any obligation on the part of the member states to change their administrative systems.
in writing. - regardless of criticism of the aspects of the partnership included in this proposal for a regulation, its content should not be analysed without taking into account its 'role' in the context of the further liberalisation of international road haulage and passenger transport promoted by the european commission and the institutions of the european union with a power of co-decision, the european parliament and the council. the central idea is emphasised by the european commission itself in its proposal: 'the directive 96/26/ec on access to the occupation of road haulage operator and the four regulations on access to the transport market, together with the deregulation of international road transport prices a few years earlier, have shaped the internal road transport market'. in other words, 'common requirements for access to the profession' were established, while 'the market opening established by the regulations encouraged greater competition'. as we have pointed out with regard to the proposal for a regulation laying down common rules for access to the international road haulage market, the present proposal aims to further liberalize international road transport by seeking to promote greater competition between the different operators in a sector where it already exists, with numerous and heavy costs for its workers.
in writing. - the report by mrs ţicău is part of a package of measures, together with two other reports, to regulate road transport activity. this activity is of the utmost importance in the european economic area, making possible the open and competitive market of which we are proud today. the new proposal would require companies to hire a certified transport manager who would be responsible for managing the transport company's traffic, while maintaining the conditions already established for access to the profession - suitability, financial capacity and professional capacity. the aim of this recast is to ensure that the existing legislation is made more intelligible and more demanding in terms of safety and effectiveness for the practice of this activity. i therefore welcome the work done by the rapporteur in the area of safety accountability and guarantees of seriousness in this economic activity, and also the measures relating to professional competence, which involve rigorous training and the mutual recognition of diplomas and licences.
in writing. - this is a further step (and a new instrument) towards further liberalizing international road haulage by promoting greater competition between the different operators in a sector where competition is already rife, with numerous and heavy costs for its workers. among other things, the aim is now to find a way of facilitating the inclusion of cabotage operations by road - that is, the carrying out of up to three consecutive international transport operations, provided they are carried out within seven days - in the market, which is already liberalized, which will have profound consequences for the financial balance and the survival of operators at national level. such a decision will also have negative consequences for road haulage workers. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work is a step in the right direction. and, if we take into account the recent decisions of the european court of justice, even the reference to directive 96/71/ec on the posting of workers will not defend the labour rights of many workers in this sector.
in writing. - this proposal forms part of a package of measures in the field of road transport. the proposal adds coherence to community legislation on the international carriage of goods by road by merging two existing regulations, with the aim of ensuring greater effectiveness in the application of the rules and clarifying and facilitating the application of the concept of cabotage. it also implements measures to simplify and standardise the community driving licence and driver's licence, thus reducing administrative costs and delays, in particular in the case of checks along the way. member states will also be able to strengthen their reporting systems, which will make it easier to learn about infringements committed by a road transport undertaking in the member state in which it is established. i believe that this text is of the utmost importance for the development of this activity on the european market, giving it the necessary speed and the requirements and structure appropriate to an open, regulated and fair market.
in writing. - there are positive aspects in this report which we value, in particular the proposals on the importance of mobile satellite services covering areas outside the main urban centres of the member states and providing the best possible services in order to bridge the digital divide, or on the advocacy that the initial service coverage area of the proposed mobile satellite services be fixed at a sufficient level by increasing the coverage capacity of such systems. but we must not forget the context in which these proposals appear - liberalisation and the advancement of the internal telecommunications market. we cannot therefore vote in favour of this report. we also disagree with the member states' willingness to waive their national rights to allocate spectrum because of the fact that mobile satellite services have a large beam area, which makes it difficult to avoid interference beyond national borders, although the commission's decision of february 2007 recognises that member states should retain the right to allow the operation of additional terrestrial components on their territories.
in writing. - in general, the report aims to simplify and reduce community legislation, arguing that it is particularly beneficial for smes. it is true that there may be some positive aspects to this simplification. and we generally support the simplification of measures in the area of company law, provided that it is the abolition of bureaucracy. however, we cannot vote in favour of a report which calls for simplification on the one hand, but also for the creation of new legal frameworks at community level. among the doubts and negative aspects which have prompted our abstention are the following proposals contained in the report: to legislate on possible coordination between the tax administrations of the member states to harmonise the information requested from companies, to revise the statute of the european company in order to ensure a more uniform community legal form, to create a new legal framework for companies, to create a common consolidated corporate tax base on the grounds that it would make the statute of the european company more useful and effective.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the britta thomsen report on women and science because i believe that it is necessary to facilitate access for both genders to scientific careers under equal conditions. factors such as stereotypes associated with the exact sciences, or the obstacles raised by the difficulty of reconciling personal and family life with professional life, bring numerous disadvantages and difficulties for women scientists and researchers, putting many women out of scientific research. the disparities between women and men in terms of presence in academic and scientific leadership positions, salaries earned, or the demands of personal life make it essential to take measures that counteract gender stereotypes in science, encourage women to pursue scientific careers and close the inequalities therein.
in writing. - we know that there are more women than men in higher education, but when it comes to choosing a career in research, the number of women is still outnumbered by that of men. the increase in the number of women in higher education has not led to an equivalent change in the ratio of women to men in certain academic or professional fields, nor has it eliminated the gender pay gap. as the rapporteur points out, women researchers are still in the minority in the public and higher education sectors, and in the european union both sectors have an average of 35% of women. in all countries, these two sectors have a higher percentage of women researchers than the private sector, where the community average is no more than 18%. it should be noted that there are great variations between countries. the lowest numbers of women in private sector research are in germany (11.8%), austria (10.4%) and the netherlands (8.7%), in contrast to countries such as latvia, bulgaria and romania, where the percentage is above 40%. the patterns of distribution of male and female researchers by major scientific fields are also very different. among male researchers in higher education, 54% work in the field of natural sciences and engineering, compared with only 37% of female researchers.
in writing. - ship dismantling continues to have a significant social and ecological impact, both because of the way it is done, which can harm the environment, and because the number of ships under construction has been increasing over the years. hence the importance of continuous innovation and development in the shipbuilding sector in the member states in order to improve shipbuilding and make it less harmful from an environmental point of view. since 2005, imo has been working with the ilo and the united nations environment programme to develop binding international standards for the environmentally sound dismantling of ships. negotiations are currently under way on a draft convention which will have to be adopted by 2009 but will not enter into force until a few years later. under the current draft, the convention will not apply to warships or other state vessels. consensus has not yet been reached on standards that do not fall within the scope of the imo, on the basic standards for ship recycling facilities, on notification requirements (in particular state-to-state notification) and on the type of mechanism to monitor the application of the convention.
in writing. - european concerns about the environment and working conditions in third countries deserve our agreement in principle. the export of conditions of misery, whether environmental, labour or otherwise, can never be part of our vision of trade and world trade. it is important, however, not to defend such an absolute and contemporary view of our reality on certain values that it ignores the whole by focusing on one part only. the adoption of drastic measures which end practices which are in fact social or environmental dumping, but which also involve the destruction of an economic sector in a third country and which thus plunge a deeply vulnerable part of the population into even greater misery, is not in line with what we are advocating. gradual reforms, setting standards as development is promoted is a more efficient and desirable way. we do not prevent misery and human degradation by merely offering as an alternative misery and human degradation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the interim report of the temporary committee on climate change on the scientific evidence on climate change (conclusions and recommendations for decision-making), as i am convinced that the broad consensus within the scientific community on the role of anthropogenic causes in climate change reflects the urgent need for increased action by the political powers, with particular attention to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and a future international climate agreement. the deepening and dissemination of scientific understanding of climate change will enable people to become more aware of the phenomenon, so as to change their lifestyles, and will make decision-making processes more responsible, informed and effective. stimulating research on the economic and social impacts of climate change should be a priority.
in writing. - this is another report which, although it starts from some correct findings on the current situation, does little or nothing to help find the solutions that are needed, is not clear in the measures it advocates, and limits itself to listing vague proposals and justifications, which seems more likely to facilitate the launching of new companies that want to obtain more and more profits from new activities in the areas of the environment and energy, at the expense of climate change. i therefore feel that it would be good to have comparable effort and persistence, and equal concern, for other global problems which are either ignored or merely kept on the list of chronic concerns - elimination of curable diseases, protection of soils and habitats, depletion of finite resources, especially hydrocarbons... the report also calls for the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the eu's environmental policy is properly implemented, and calls for the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the environmental policy is properly implemented. we shall await that report in the future.
in writing. − the scientific facts focused on in this report have been discussed in depth with world experts during the meetings of the interim committee on climate change and cannot therefore be lightly questioned. like the florenz report, i welcome the ipcc 4th report as the most comprehensive study on climate change and agree that it is absolutely necessary to avoid a rise in global temperature of more than 2oc in order to avoid the most catastrophic scenarios, suggesting that the ambitious european targets for reducing ghg emissions should be maintained. as a compendium of the most credible information available today, and cutting through the recurring ideas of a few isolated extremists who continue to question human action as the main cause of global warming, the florenz report is a clear sign that the european parliament will maintain its position of rigour and ambition in the fight against climate change, and i therefore support it.
in writing. - scientific discussions should not be the subject of debates of conviction. and doubting the truth of the majority opinion cannot be interpreted as denial or as a political option. on the other hand, recent episodes such as the debate on the unintended and unforeseen implications of encouraging increased biofuel production show how permanent doubt is the only scientific certainty that we should embrace without hesitation. on the contrary, in the field of the debate on choices in the face of scientific facts, we are clearly in the realm of political choices. if i do not consider myself scientifically competent to give an opinion on the first question, i consider it my duty to do so on the second. what i have been advocating, and insisting on, is that in the face of the foreseeable increase in consumption (in particular energy) by huge masses of the population, due to the positive effects of globalisation, we must look for scientific answers, technological solutions. some changes in the field of behaviour, both individual and collective, are certainly welcome. but it is in science that we will find the essence of the solutions we need.
in writing. - despite the contradictions, it is a fact that turkey is of strategic importance for the eu's ambitions, particularly in the current context of the deepening crisis of the capitalist system. while its final status is not defined - full membership of the eu or of a future mediterranean union - what seems certain is that the eu is seeking to find the solutions that best serve the interests of the major economic and financial groups of the great powers, with particular emphasis on germany. turkey represents a huge market that arouses various appetites. it is a vast country with a huge amount of cheap labour and consumers, who are not even allowed to celebrate may day, as was recently seen in the brutal crackdown by turkish security forces on trade unionists and protesters. it is a vast territory occupying an important geostrategic position between europe, asia and the middle east, playing a central role in the dispute over the control and access to central asian energy resources (as exemplified by the nabucco project) and playing a pivotal role in the us/nato/eu partnership. turkey, a country whose authorities are militarily and illegally occupying part of the territory of an eu member state, cyprus.
in writing. - the progress made in various sectors of society, the economy and politics in recent years is a reminder of how the will to join the european union successfully promotes reforms of the greatest importance in the countries where this possibility exists. this being the case for turkey, and keeping the negotiations open, it is worth stressing the importance of taking advantage of this opportunity to promote the most far-reaching and necessary reforms in turkey, whatever the outcome of the negotiations. the recognition of the report - and the statements of senior eu officials, including the president of the commission - are accompanied by concern about the legal proceedings against the akp. although it is preferable that there should have been no military intervention, it is regrettable that there should have been an attempt to obtain by judicial means what the ballot boxes had denied. on the other hand, the persistent doubt about the real intentions of the akp is also of concern. the defence of religious freedom as we understand it in the european union deserves our agreement. the widespread imposition of a religious view on the whole of society would be unacceptable.
more than 63,000 dead and missing and two and a half million homeless today is the result of the cyclone combined with the cruelty of the junta that misrules and oppresses burma and has prevented international aid to the needy. what a contrast to the openness and readiness in china to aid the survivors of sichuan! the un security council cannot refrain from applying the responsibility to protect to burma, by immediately authorizing access to the country by international humanitarian agencies and ngos to help the abandoned population of the irrawaddy delta, and it cannot refrain from referring the burmese military junta to the international criminal court for prosecution for crimes against humanity. this parliament expects european governments to activate the un security council immediately. it is time for all members of the council, including china, which has been backing the burmese dictatorship, to assume their responsibilities to the sacrificed people of burma.
madam president, commissioner, we all regret the catastrophe that has devastated southern china. over 50,000 people died and 4.8 million were left homeless. we all stand in solidarity with the families affected. the european union did the right thing: it activated the civil protection mechanism and supported the chinese authorities. the international community in general has also given its support. never before has china received so many expressions of solidarity and material support, because this time the chinese authorities did not try to hide the scale of the tragedy. on the contrary, they have provided the necessary information, they have allowed access to the international media, in short, they have acted with transparency and efficiency, unlike what happened to the old burma. climate change is causing an increase in natural disasters. preventing global warming is everyone's responsibility. it is therefore necessary that china also contributes to reducing co2 emissions by supporting the european union's efforts to reach an international agreement by the copenhagen conference in december 2009.
in a recent letter to the london times, nine former british military commanders appealed to the uk government to join those who advocate a ban on cluster bombs. the argument is the same as that which was invoked in the context of anti-personnel mines: however useful a weapon may be in the short term, in a military logic, the fact that it causes indiscriminate long-term effects is sufficient to justify the suspension of its use by responsible armed forces. the same logic applies to depleted uranium munitions. the european organisation of military associations, euromil, is following this matter closely and its position, based on the information it receives from military personnel across europe, is categorical: the depleted uranium munitions must be abandoned as soon as possible. the european parliament has already spoken in favour of a total ban on these weapons and the un general assembly resolution adopted last december, which puts the issue of weapons and munitions containing depleted uranium on the agenda of the 33rd plenary session of the general assembly, has confirmed that the european parliament is right to take a leading position and to ask the council to take a leading position in this further debate on disarmament and humanitarian law. the arguments "against" of the skeptics among us do not work. the most elementary precautionary principle requires the stigmatization of these weapons before even the many circumstantial evidence pointing in the direction of their indiscriminate carcinogenic effect is replaced by irrefutable scientific evidence. what will policy makers say about us a decade from now, when the harmful effects of these weapons are clear and unquestionable, and even today's skeptics, if we have not done anything to remove them from circulation in the meantime? they 'll say the same thing they say now about land mines: how could they wait so long!

the central issue in this debate is the priority to be given to the defence and promotion of existing industries in the various member states, taking into account their specificities, whether they are industries in the textile, clothing and footwear sectors, the automotive industry, the shipbuilding industry, the chemical industry or any other traditional sector or new materials and innovative techniques. this priority requires not only measures to boost innovation and to support micro, small and mediumsized enterprises effectively, but also a strategy for international trade, which takes account of the reality and the industrial ranks existing in our countries, the defence of employment with rights, the promotion of the development of our regions and social inclusion. it is not enough to say that we want an industry that looks to the future. it is urgent to look to the present and to put industries and their social impact at the centre of the decisions that must be taken in terms of macroeconomic, financial and trade policies, whether at community or national level.
a new animal health strategy needs to pay particular attention to disease prevention, animal feeding, border controls and transport. all prevention measures, testing, vaccination and other interventions to prevent further outbreaks of animal diseases are important to avoid serious damage such as that already suffered from bse, foot-and-mouth disease, bluetongue and others, because food safety and also public health are at stake. it is therefore also important that these principles be taken into account in relation to imported animals, as has already been stressed here, and we hope that the new action plan which the commissioner has just mentioned will be put in place as soon as possible and also with the aim of improving the existing mechanisms, deepening technical and human support, ensuring financial support and increasing the budgetary funds provided. this is a question which must be clarified today.
i congratulate mr van hecke on this important report. investing in human and financial capacity and overcoming existing inconsistencies between policies and institutional architecture is key to improving the effectiveness of european aid. the treaty of lisbon opens up an opportunity with the creation of the european external action service. in addition to supporting the future high representative, this service should be equipped to carry forward eu development policy in parallel with the cfsp and esdp. to ensure that aid is effective, we do not need to reinvent the wheel. it is dependent on the fulfillment of promises made. as commissioner michel stressed, member states must increase official development assistance to the levels promised in 2005, without inflating it through debt forgiveness, and must genuinely direct it towards achieving the millennium development goals, especially at a time when the escalation of oil and food prices makes the fight against poverty in the world even more urgent. mr president, more than the effectiveness of aid, what is at stake is the credibility of the european union and its effectiveness as a global actor.
, in writing. in the absence of any opportunity to comment on the variety of important issues listed in this report - both positive and negative - it should be noted that this report does not fail to mention the negative development of so-called eu development aid, even if in a mitigated way. although it does not dismantle the use of development aid, often as a mere palliative, (false) counterpart and condition for the liberalisation of markets or as an instrument of interference - with the known negative objectives and effects, see, for example, the so-called european consensus of the eu on development, the economic partnership agreements that the eu intends to impose or the financial speculation around foodstuffs, which call into question the proclaimed development objectives - the report points, not surprisingly, to the insufficiency of the results of development aid and its significant decrease in the eu - 0.38% in 2007 compared to 0.41% in 2006, far from the 0.7% of gni indicated by the un. the report also warns of the increasing use of development aid for purposes unrelated to development (such as military expenditure) and the fact that it is disbursed, in most cases, according to the priorities and timetables of the donors themselves.
in writing. − due to the delay in adopting the new structural programmes and subsequently the operational programmes submitted by the member states, the 2007 community budget for the european regional development fund (erdf), the european agricultural fund for regional development (eafrd) and the european fisheries fund (eff) was not implemented, with a total of eur 3.525 million. part of this amount has already been transferred to the 2008 budget, but €2.034 billion remains unspent. the draft amending budget proposes, among other things, that part of this unspent amount be transferred to the current budget (eur 772 million) and that the remaining amount be transferred to subsequent years. such delays have a serious impact on the implementation of programmes and, of course, it is micro, small and mediumsized enterprises, small farming and family farming, among other examples, that are most affected by these consequences, especially in view of the worsening financial and socioeconomic crisis as a result of the neoliberal policies. moreover, in the face of rising food prices, fuel prices and the downward revision of economic growth in the various eu countries, such funds should be used to promote public investment for the dynamisation of the economy and the urgent improvement of workers' incomes.
in writing. - the european parliament's report, following the european commission's own communication, forgets the enormous social impact of existing industries and persists in a neoliberal path which may guarantee high profits for large companies but does not guarantee employment with rights and the improvement of the quality of life of the population. while industry in the eu countries contributes more than 80% of private sector r & d expenditure and its innovative products account for some 73% of eu exports, the report does insist on the creation of an open and competitive internal market in services and industry, which is of interest only to the large economic groups, as it may affect micro, small and medium-sized enterprises and a high percentage of employment, which may affect the incomes of workers and many small entrepreneurs, and therefore their activity as consumers. finally, we also disagree with the strengthening of the role of the european union's defence sector, even though this may have implications for the growth of the arms industry. our proposal for social progress and development is accompanied by a perspective of peace, not war.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because of the importance it attaches to issues which i consider essential, in particular the promotion of small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) in the european union. representing more than 90% of the european business fabric, smes have not only an economic role within the union but also a social one, as they make a remarkable contribution to employment and growth. in this context, initiatives such as the european commission's reduction of unnecessary red tape faced by these companies by 25% and the promotion of investment in human resources quality and research are to be welcomed. the eu industrial sector still has great potential for improvement, both in the realisation of research and innovation into business opportunities and in the anticipation of these opportunities for a faster adaptation to market changes. improving the regulatory framework, particularly with regard to the patent system, in order to facilitate access to the internal market and fostering european entrepreneurship are key factors in increasing our industrial competitiveness. in this context, the promotion of regional clusters also seems to me to be very positive. it seems clear to me that a thriving european industry is crucial to the achievement of the lisbon objectives.
in writing. - it is regrettable what happened today in the vote in plenary. the ppe tabled an amendment calling into question the agreement already reached with the council and aimed at improving its functioning, ensuring better conditions for support in the study and analysis of national and local labour markets, in its link with the european parliament, which would now have a strengthened role in its functioning and monitoring. with the approval of the ppe's proposal, albeit by a narrow margin, all the consensus reached was called into question. contrary to what was foreseen, a second reading is therefore necessary, and the report will be discussed again in the committee on employment and social affairs, because we are in a legislative area of codecision. hence our final vote of abstention.

in writing. - global economic growth and biofuels policy have created a paradox. with the world's level of wealth, it is a serious matter that many families struggle to eat. the market is conditioned by an unprecedented concentration of population in urban agglomerations, the abandonment of agriculture for tertiary activities, and the consumption of basic foodstuffs in other complex elements of the food chain, such as livestock. biofuels have introduced a thief into the field and an unexpected guest to the table. competition between energy sources and food orchestrates their prices. we are faced with issues of scarcity, sustainability, safety and ecology. the self-sufficiency policies respond to the disappearance of strategic reserves and war fears. given the announced restrictions on grain sales, the volume of this year's harvest will be crucial. speculation is such that central banks warn of the underlying inflationary risk and india has banned trading in food futures contracts. it is urgent to reverse the situation in favour of farmers who do not yet know what they will reap, especially the smaller ones, victims of perverse and inconsistent agricultural policies. technology and science that once diverged thus find a new opportunity from which we will all benefit.
in writing. - under the pressure of the worsening capitalist crisis worldwide, even with its limitations, the resolution adopted is a denunciation of the consequences of eu policies on agriculture, exposing the real and unacceptable objectives of the cap and the wto agreements. however, the resolution fails to point out those who are really responsible for the very serious situation that exists, and it fails to draw the proper consequences from the diagnosis it makes, by failing to question the policies that are at the root of it, among other examples: it does not affirm food sovereignty as a central issue to ensure the right to food; it does not make the raising of incomes in small-scale farming and family farming a necessary condition for the preservation of agriculture, the countryside and food security; it does not call for the withdrawal of agriculture from the wto, for the end of the treatment of agri-food production as a commodity and for the revision of the blair house agreement; it does not require a break with the cap, the end of the disconnection of production aid, the application of a real cap and modulation in favour of small farming and family farming and a fair redistribution between countries and productions, promoting the full development of the agricultural and livestock production of each country.
in writing. − following the implementation of the us legislative reform on enhanced security requirements under the visa waiver programme, the us decided to propose individual memoranda of understanding to each eu member state in a 'divide and rule' attempt. these agreements are unacceptable not only because they do not respect the community's competence in this area but also because they call into question the principle of sincere cooperation and give rise to unequal treatment between citizens of the various member states in the field of visas. i welcome the fact that the commission has been given a mandate (within the framework of community competence) to negotiate an agreement between the eu and the us, which should guarantee uniform treatment on equal terms for all citizens of the union in terms of visa exemption if they want to enter american territory (as, incidentally, the union already applies to all american citizens who want to enter the union). it is important that these negotiations proceed swiftly and in the spirit of european unity so that by 2009 all member states can participate in the reformed us visa-free regime. i believe, however, that the conditions for this will only be created if the bilateral agreements concluded in the meantime are annulled. i am therefore awaiting the opinion of the legal service of the ep, which i hope will confirm this position.

in writing. - since 2001, the implementation of the aarhus convention, which entered into force on 30 october 2001, has been under discussion. as most of the 35 parties to this convention are member states of the european union, they have special responsibilities in setting up the mechanisms necessary for its implementation. it is equally important to ensure that specific provisions, similar to rights already provided for in the convention, which enhance public participation at regional and global level, are also included in other conventions and treaties dealing with environmental issues. parliament and the council have already adopted three legislative instruments to implement the aarhus convention, but difficulties remain. so although there are some unclear points in the european parliament's resolution, we have generally supported it because we believe it is important to help create universal conditions for access to justice and to proceedings involving environmental matters. we therefore hope that at the third session of the meeting of the parties to the convention, to be held in riga, latvia, from 11 to 13 june 2008, some positive progress will be made in the process.
in writing. - there are aspects of the resolution that are more important than others... some policies, because of their structural importance, condition all the others... an example... by not calling into question the economic partnership agreements (epas), merely by referring to the need not to make development aid conditional on countries accepting greater liberalisation of their markets, all the positive aspects of such aid are being thrown out of the picture. the epas condition the sovereignty of the countries, they impose a model which favours the eu's multinationals, they condition the production of the countries not to the multiple needs of their peoples but, on the contrary, to the requirements of an increasingly liberalised market. i therefore welcome the fact that military expenditure should be excluded from the scope of development aid, that effective resources should be allocated to the development and improvement of public services, that aid should be definitively stopped being diverted to objectives which are not in any way linked to development, but these measures will only be effective if we reject trade liberalisation and the instruments of domination and interference enshrined in the epas. only by overcoming this contradiction can aid be established that is truly based on solidarity and respect for national sovereignty.
i congratulate helmut kuhne on his excellent report and in particular on his insistence on introducing the concept of human security in combination with the principle of the responsibility to protect - a concept which mr solana has also defended here. these should be the twin pillars of a european approach to crisis management missions. on the one hand, a decision to intervene in a country under the esdp must be guided by an interpretation of the un charter that underlines the imperative of the responsibility to protect: the obligation to prevent genocide, war crimes, ethnic cleansing and crimes against humanity. on the other hand, since the union is involved in a crisis which requires the use of military means, it is essential that the application of force be guided by the doctrine of human security. this will require european troops to concentrate their efforts on creating safe spaces for non-combatant civilian populations, far more than on destroying the enemy with military victory in view. these two principles equip europe with a coherent strategy for crisis management at the beginning of the 21st century. the first amendment of the pse therefore reflects the moral, legal and operational demands we face in afghanistan, chad or lebanon and will face in the future. i therefore find it regrettable that this amendment has been rejected by the epp-ed and gue/ngl members. this reactionary alliance insists on turning a blind eye to the primacy of human rights and this is a concept which would only strengthen the legitimacy and popular support for esdp missions.
