the commission's proposal is to be incorporated in the treaty of amsterdam, and the council's proposal is to be incorporated in the treaty of amsterdam. in its communication, the commission explains how it has challenged the need to reconcile port development and management with transparency, competition and, in general, the acquis communautaire, as well as the creation of a genuine internal market for maritime transport in europe, for which it will present a legislative proposal, i.e. the aim is to further integrate port management into the competition rules of the internal market of the european union. the commission obviously has no power to privatise. however, it seeks to create the conditions so that when these are realised, they can be implemented within the european union through the liberalisation of port services, for example, in the case of service concessions in the port sector, and i quote, 'so as not to restrict or limit free competition beyond what is necessary', or in the case of public funding for all commercial ports, and i quote, 'regardless of their turnover'. we therefore believe that the european parliament's report should explicitly reject any further attempt to liberalize port services at european union level in terms of public funding, port concessions, technical and nautical services or cargo handling services. the port sector is a public service of strategic importance for the economic and social development, the environment, defence and sovereignty of each member state and should not be liberalised at the level of the european union.
i would first like to congratulate mrs ries on her work. the link between bad environment and health risks is now evident. there are more pathologies associated with environmental factors and climate change, such as respiratory, allergic and cancer diseases. global warming is causing new pandemics. studies reveal that droughts and floods kill more people than any other natural disaster. the lack of air quality in schools and health facilities is also a source of serious problems. more and more people are getting sick as a result of air pollution in big cities and inside buildings, as a result of water pollution and even groundwater pollution, as a result of contamination of agricultural land by plant protection products, as a result of the lack of treatment of waste water and urban waste. measures must be taken to avert future evils.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, we know that this is a very sensitive area because the protection of soil, a scarce and non-renewable resource, is vital, because agriculture and the conservation of biodiversity depend on it, because it is a platform for human activities, including cities and infrastructure, but also for nature and landscapes, and so its protection is crucial to preserve our heritage, natural resources, the quality of surface and groundwater, health, human life. soil protection is a very dynamic system, with many functions and vital services for human activities and the survival of ecosystems. soil protection is a collective imperative for our common life and for the protection of future generations, which means that it is not subject to the rules of competition. but, as a result, soil is also subject to multiple encroachments, property speculation, degradation and contamination, including in border areas, which calls for greater cooperation between member states and the definition of some common objectives in respect of the principle of subsidiarity and the social function of land. there are a number of policies at community level which have implications for soil and may jeopardise its protection, so we need to go further in the study of the risks and the various perspectives of soil in order to take account of appropriate measures aimed at its preservation, although a very important contribution would certainly be a change in the common agricultural policy to provide more support for family farming and small and mediumsized farmers. it is in this context that it is important to know the council's position and also to follow its development.
mr president, as the minister has said, we are dealing with a very sensitive and complex subject on which it is not easy to reach consensus among the 27 member states and even in this parliament, as has already been seen. as my colleague, mrs inés ayala, has said, soil is a non-renewable resource, which is linked to natural disasters and agricultural production, which is linked to land use, land use planning and nature conservation, in other words to very delicate and very demanding aspects. there are many interests involved and many of my colleagues have asked themselves whether this directive is necessary. others have questioned his flexibility. however, a very strict legal framework is not always the best way to achieve the objectives, taking into account the different realities. this directive, in my view, is important and necessary to maintain the balance of ecosystems.

in writing. - taking into account the concerns expressed in the report about the need for investment in port regions, technological modernisation and environmental protection, we consider that the report highlights that the european commission's objectives for a future port policy include the further liberalisation of this strategic public service in different member states. we therefore regret the rejection of our proposals, which emphasised: - rejection of any further attempt to liberalise port services at eu level by applying the competition rules of the internal market; - calls for action to combat the precariousness and risk of accidents in the sector and to guarantee and enforce the rights of port workers, in particular in the field of employment, fair pay, decent working conditions, social protection, collective agreements, trade union rights and vocational training. the diversity and complementarities of ports in europe and their management under advanced standards of quality and safety, which is a strategic element for economic development, must be safeguarded. the opening up of european port management to transnational companies, as has been demonstrated, will devalue labour relations and collective bargaining and increase the dangers of the port system becoming precarious, thus putting maritime safety at risk. that is why we abstained.
in writing. - while we follow the concerns and proposals in the report, we believe that it does not reflect essential guidelines for national policies for this strategic sector - with social, economic and environmental implications - namely to base this system on a strong public sector and the necessary fight against the systematic violation and non-compliance of workers' rights in segments of this sector. we therefore consider that the report falls short of its objective in not addressing the central issue of working conditions for professionals in this sector. the practice of precarious employment, which encourages non-compliance with working hours, rest periods and collective agreements, is a violation of workers' rights and threatens their own safety (and that of others). it is therefore necessary to stop the destruction of jobs and the precariousness of working relationships by promoting integration into the workforce of companies and the dignification of careers and wages. we also disagree with the insistence on the application of the 'user-payer' and 'polluter-payer' principles, since it is the final consumer who is the most affected by these measures, which only benefit those who have the financial capacity to 'use' or 'pollute', and do not necessarily contribute to a significant improvement in the transport of goods.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the doris pack report on the bologna process and student mobility, as i believe that quality, efficient, innovative and accessible european higher education for all european citizens is crucial if the european union is to remain competitive and successful in the face of the demands of globalisation. in this context, i believe that measures such as the promotion of reciprocity in the flow of students, the continuing training of teachers in the various fields of study and the development of means of financing student mobility are fundamental to ensuring the achievement of the objectives of the bologna process.
in writing. - although the rapporteur expresses particular concern about student mobility within the european union, considering that member states should be supported in their efforts to modernise and innovatively reform their higher education systems, the truth is that the whole report involves this issue in the approach to the bologna process and in what she considers to be absolutely necessary to face the challenges of globalisation, insisting on its deepening. that is why we abstained, because we disagree with this analysis. but we agree that it is time to reflect and debate on the bologna process, in particular to try to determine to what extent the education systems have changed and to what extent these developments and changes have affected the quality of higher education in the various member states. access to high quality education should be an option for all citizens, regardless of their nationality, country or place of birth, and mobility can have very positive effects not only on the individual on mobility, but also on higher education institutions and society as a whole. moreover, its social dimension must not be forgotten, as has happened in the past.
in writing. − the tenth anniversary of the signing of the bologna declaration in 2009 marks the need to redefine the objectives of the process. the serious redefinition of these objectives requires a reflection on the implementation of the bologna process in the member states. it is necessary to consider whether the policies pursued in the name of bologna have, in fact and as intended, led to the consolidation of a european higher education area capable of responding to the challenges of competitiveness at international level. i support this initiative - a concrete contribution to identifying, on the one hand, problems and challenges that have arisen in 10 years of implementation and, on the other hand, issues that must remain a priority. this is the case with student mobility, a cornerstone of a richer and more competitive education and an essential contribution to the development of the concept of european citizenship. it is essential that member states are encouraged to check the impact of this process on the proper qualification and preparation of young people. as our rapporteur points out, the objectives of the process and the central importance of students in all matters concerning their education must not be lost sight of.
in writing. - we voted against this report because, despite some of the remedies proposed and some criticism of the financial crisis, no concrete measures are taken to combat effectively the growing financialisation of the economy, rampant speculation, the proliferation of financial instruments and products to secure ever greater speculative gains, or even the end of tax havens and banking secrecy. as we said in the plenary debate, the consequences are always the same: workers who go out of work, people who have to pay higher interest rates, including here in the european union, especially in the countries with the weakest economies, such as portugal, where the debt ratio is close to 120% of gdp and household debt is around 130% of disposable income. we therefore insist on the priority of supporting job creation with rights, production, poverty eradication, improving the purchasing power of workers and pensioners, supporting quality public services and increasing subsidised credit lines to support micro, small and medium-sized enterprises.
in writing. - the concerns expressed in this report, which are accompanied by a due recognition of the importance of the financial products in question, merits my agreement in their essence. given that we are going through a period of evident financial market turbulence it is important to react with as much firmness as calm and science. much of the economic success of the last few decades in europe, the united states and other fast-growing economies has been due precisely to the agility of financial markets. in the necessary corrections to the existing system, it is important to act on the causes of the crisis, but not to destroy what is virtuous about the system. this is the assumption which the european commission must take into account when urging the european parliament to act.
in writing. − transparency should be a guiding principle for the functioning of markets, including financial markets. it should not, however, be the only element of consideration, otherwise the principle would be made the norm, confusing the desired result (healthy and efficient financial markets) with the proposed means of achieving it (sufficiently regulated and supervised markets). in the context of the current political and economic debate on the financial market, it is important that the commission interprets this recommendation in this way, endeavouring to defend the quality of the european financial market, recalling that it is from the proper and fundamentally free functioning of this market that the greatest economic benefits for society result.
in writing. - we voted in favour of this report because transmissible spongiform encephalopathy (tse), commonly known as mad cow disease, is a serious threat to our health. as is well known, this deadly infectious disease develops through a protein that can be found in infected meat and results in deterioration of the human brain. this epidemic has been reduced by strict european regulation. in this report, the rapporteur complements the work of the previous rapporteur by adding new elements which should be governed by the regulatory procedure with scrutiny. we therefore agree that the commission proposal should be amended to ensure that controls are not reduced. we must be extremely careful to ensure that the regulatory procedure with scrutiny does not slow down the implementation of measures against this disease. we must also avoid creating loopholes in legislation by granting member states exceptions. that is why this report is so important and why i hope that the european commission will take it into account. after the well-known scandals relating to this disease, the public in the member states is demanding the transparency it legitimately deserves.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by roselyne lefrançois on a proposal for a council framework decision amending framework decision 2002/475/jha on the fight against terrorism, because i believe that the instruments for combating terrorism need to be adapted to the new means of information and communication available to terrorists. the revision of the eu framework decision allows for the inclusion in the notion of terrorism of specific preparatory acts, such as recruitment and training for terrorism and public incitement to terrorism, which will be criminalised in all member states. the important amendments proposed by the pse group to guarantee fundamental freedoms of expression and association should also be highlighted.
in writing. − the current international and community legal framework includes a set of instruments which are all the more necessary for combating actual terrorism and the violent and transnational organised crime associated with it. the aim of this proposal is to strengthen the set of security measures which, by exploiting the events of 11 september 2001, have been putting at risk the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens. the present proposal, like the rapporteur, is moving forward with definitions which, because of their ambiguity, do not safeguard respect for fundamental freedoms. as in the framework decision 2002/475/jha on combating terrorism with its definition of 'terrorism' , the possibility of applying security measures and criminalising natural or legal persons who effectively fight, by word or by writing, against state terrorism is once again open. the present proposal does not add any value in the fight against actual terrorism and the transnational crime associated with it, but rather poses real dangers to the security and fundamental freedoms of citizens in the different member states. as we have stressed, more than security measures, it is necessary to address the real causes that fuel terrorism. as we said, we will not trade freedom for security, because we will lose both. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. - the legal clarity of the legal framework for combating terrorism is as necessary as clarity and determination in this regard. in this sense, the commission's concern about the mechanisms, means and methods involved in the recruitment of terrorists, particularly those recruited in european countries, often native to europe, is understandable. in this respect, it is necessary to ensure that the police authorities and the state have the necessary means to act, preferably preventively. non-police and non-judicial measures, but also measures to combat this phenomenon, are equally important. the aim is to ensure that, alongside the judicial system's reaction, there is also an alert, attentive and capable political system to intervene, whether in strengthening integration, in promoting moderate, majority voices or in combating the marginalization associated with illegal immigration. for all these reasons, political power must be alert and active. while it is true that it is impossible to prevent all acts, it is possible to prevent the environment that promotes, incites and encourages terrorism.
in writing. - stressing that this is a procedure for the council to 'consult' the ep, we stress that - having supported amendments tabled by the ep, even if they are more backward than previously adopted positions - we consider that this proposal falls short of what is required in terms of 'protection of personal data processed in the context of police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters'. in addition to other crucial aspects in the negative assessment of this proposal, it should be stressed that it did not exclude, even in a (pseudo) conditional way, 'the processing of personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical convictions or trade union membership, as well as the processing of data relating to health and sexual life', which is unacceptable! as was stressed in the debate, this is a proposal based on a minimum common denominator for a matter as fundamental as the guarantee of the rights, freedoms and guarantees of the citizens of the different member states, which is lower than that contained in other legal instruments, notably the council of europe. the protection of personal data is urgent and essential, and it cannot be ensured by means of a legal instrument whose scope, because it is too broad or defective, allows for its non-compliance or fails to safeguard it. that is why we abstained.
madam president, commissioner, colleagues, mr minister, as shadow rapporteur for the paulo costa report and rapporteur for the flag state report, i would like to say something about the civil liability of passenger carriers and the package as a whole. as regards the paulo costa report, my efforts have focused on strengthening passengers' rights in the event of accidents and incidents, ensuring adequate financial compensation and early support to alleviate the consequences of incidents, whether they occur at sea or in inland waterways, where sea travel often ends, and also on strengthening passenger information requirements. i therefore also agree with the second reading of these proposals. as for the package, ladies and gentlemen, i would say that each of the reports is worth something in itself and certainly brings added value. but i would say that the package as a whole, including the one i was rapporteur for, the flag state obligations package, has added value for maritime safety, and i therefore ask the council, the commission and everyone to do their utmost to get the package approved. i would also like to thank the french presidency for its efforts, following on from the slovenian presidency, to bring this matter forward. i believe that only an integrated package will promote maritime safety. i would like to take this opportunity to congratulate all the rapporteurs. we will come out of this with a response, i would say, "cambada", as they say in portuguese, if we do not look at the package as a whole, because only the package as a whole can prevent erika and prestige from happening in the short term, and only in this way can we effectively ensure maritime safety.

the question period is now over (b6-0462/2008). the following questions were put to the council.
question no 2 by mr manuel medina ortega (h-0616/08) subject: european pact on immigration can the council indicate what consequences the recently agreed pact on immigration may have for the development of the european union's immigration policy?

question no 6 by brian crowley (h-0625/08) subject: the use of the european parliament in the european parliament subject: objectives of the european conference on alzheimer's disease the author of the question welcomes the french presidency's programme which emphasises the promotion of better health care for people suffering from alzheimer's disease and their families. encouraging the exchange and sharing of national experience and cooperation of best practices between member states in the field of health is precisely the eu's objective. greater exchange of information and best practice between member states on all health-related issues will greatly benefit medical professionals and, most importantly, our citizens. in view of the fact that a large european conference on alzheimer's disease is to be held in october, can the commission state what the objectives of the conference are and what the french presidency intends to achieve?

mr president, mr president-in-office of the council, mr vice-president of the european commission, ladies and gentlemen, we have examined two instruments: a regulation and a decision on the migration of sisone4all to sis ii, including the implementation of a global test to assess whether the level of performance of sis ii is equivalent to that of the current system. these proposals result from a change in the migration strategy. four points: first, the initial plan was to migrate 15 member states in a process that should have taken around 8 hours, but this has since been increased to 25 member states, which has made the process much more complex and difficult; second, an interim technical architecture should be created to allow sis 1+ and sis ii to operate in parallel for a limited transitional period. it is a prudent solution which deserves our agreement and which allows us to have a rearguard in case something goes wrong; third, during this transitional period a technical tool, a converter, will be made available which will connect the central system of system i to the central system of sis ii, allowing them to process the same information and ensuring that all member states remain at the same level. finally, the mandate given to the commission in 2001 expires at the end of this year, in 2008. we raised four concerns. firstly, the need for the european commission to continue to have a mandate to develop sis ii until it is operational. we oppose the idea, which has been considered, that the commission's mandate could end with the completion of the work on the c-sis central system. secondly, there should be a clear definition of the responsibilities of the european commission and the member states. third, that all the conditions laid down in paragraph 2 which establishes the legal basis for sis are fulfilled before the data migration takes place. and fourthly, that this migration should be done in a single step, a one-shot, to be processed by all the member states. the proposals which we received on 3 september, the same day as their adoption by coreper, represent major changes compared to the initial proposals. normally, as the texts presented involve substantial changes, parliament should be consulted again. but once again, we are faced with a tight timetable, the commission's mandate expires at the end of 2008 and it is essential that the council approves these proposals by the end of october. parliament once again shows its responsibility, it is not our fault that the procedure is late, the changes introduced in fact answer most of the concerns raised in my draft reports, above all i see that there is a clarification of the responsibilities of the commission and the member states and that the commission will continue to have a mandate for the development of sis ii until it is operational. in conclusion, i would like to congratulate the french presidency on the excellent work it has done to reach a good agreement, which seemed difficult, between the commission and the member states. the european parliament wants to help ensure that there are no further delays and that sis ii can be operational by the new date of 30 september 2009. we are concerned because several technicians have informally said that it is very likely that this date will not be respected again. there are two main points which the european parliament considers to be fundamental and which all the political groups support. firstly, that the european parliament be kept informed every six months of the progress of the project; secondly, that the mandate given to the new commission not be an unlimited mandate, that a rule be included requiring the european parliament to be consulted again if there is a delay of more than one year. we sincerely hope that this time the project will be completed in time and that sis ii will be able to start operations on the date planned.
as underlined by different organisations following the process of the communitisation of justice and home affairs, areas which are at the heart of the sovereignty of states, the so-called migration of the schengen information system to its second version extends the characteristics of this information system and database beyond its original purpose, integrating new types of alerts such as the european arrest warrant, adding new categories of data such as biometrics, extending its access to new entities, developing new features and functionalities with interlinking of alerts and its link to the visa information system. the committee also notes the worrying possibility that records may be kept for a long period of time if necessary, and asks who defines this need, and also lays down the too vague field of possible data sharing with third countries. we believe that this extension of the previous system poses risks to the safeguarding of citizens' rights, freedoms and guarantees, because it adds new elements to a database which will be more shared and accessible. in fact, far beyond the response to enlargement to new countries, the aim is to adapt sis to the dangerous security drift in the context of the growing communitization of internal affairs in the european union, which we reject.
the rapporteur. - mr president, i take the risk of making my final remarks in french to respond to the courtesy of the remarks of minister jouyet and vice-president barrot. so i will now speak in your language to commend you. it was not an easy job to build consensus within the council, but you succeeded. two things are really important to us: the clarity of the division of powers between the european commission and the member states, and the problem of the commission's mandate. the commission's mandate will not be able to end until the sis ii system is fully operational. i also want to thank the council, the commission and all the political groups in the libe committee for the work they have done together in drafting the amendments which we are going to vote on tomorrow. we consider the transparency clause to be very important: citizens have the right to be informed about the schengen system and sis ii. as for the question of the duration of the commission's mandate, an unlimited mandate is not acceptable and we have succeeded in solving that problem. finally, mr president, i would like to explain to those who have expressed a lack of optimism about the system why we like sis ii. we like sis ii because we like freedom of movement in europe. but if we are to have free movement in europe, we must be sure that our external borders are secure. the security of the external borders is a condition of freedom for european citizens and that is why sis ii is needed very quickly.
mr president, this particular case is a clear case in which the concern for the liberalization of international trade must be subordinated to more important objectives, in the present case of an environmental and social nature. the conservation of tropical forests is essential for the ecological balance of the planet and as such we can say without exaggeration that tropical forests are truly a heritage of humanity and that we all have responsibilities in the conservation of tropical forests. the most developed and prosperous countries in particular have responsibilities which they cannot give up. these forests are located in countries which are, for the most part, poor countries, countries which are struggling with enormous difficulties, and all the rhetoric we can produce here is absolutely incapable of working if we are not able to promote development actions directed at these countries. it is absolutely necessary that we support these countries, it is absolutely necessary that the main consumers and the most developed areas in the world, as is clearly the case in the european union, should make efforts to ensure that there are strict mechanisms to monitor how these forests are exploited, but at the same time it is essential that these countries should make efforts to ensure support for the producing countries. these are countries that depend on the rainforest, their economy is largely associated with the forest, rapid deforestation ends up having dramatic consequences from all points of view the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full, and i am glad that the commission has taken this step. we must indeed support, we must have measures that encourage the development, the transformation of the productive structure of these countries, so that they can have a relationship with their forests, with their resources, more suited to their interests and more in line with what are also the most global interests of humanity. and that is a responsibility that the european union has. this deal is going in the right direction: the report does not go far enough, and it has the merit of clearly pointing out these shortcomings, but it does give us some hope for the future.
mr president, the european parliament is represented before the court by its president and, in controversial cases, the president first calls on the full court. this is the case with resources. the new report extends this system to other procedural acts where the president also represents parliament and, in controversial situations, calls on the plenary. but there's something new in the report. the new text introduces the conference of presidents as a decision-making body between the president and the plenary. this solution is not in itself problematic, but it is good to take the opportunity to remind that the european parliament must never lose the classic semantics of parliaments, and must concentrate in the plenary all the final decision-making power. the plenary is sovereign over everything, because it is there that the legitimacy that comes from the ethics of representation is found. it is true that institutions which govern complex and wide-ranging areas, such as the european parliament, often cannot avoid the temptation to bureaucratize their own democratic power. the temptation is often inescapable, but the truth is that we must avoid as much as possible the bureaucratization of democracy, since the effectiveness of good governance can never mean the loss of the space of politics and, much less, the loss of the space of politics for quasi-administrative forms such as committees and, sometimes, conferences. because, to use mirabeau's expression, these are not the true "map of the people".
in this very worrying moment, when the people of our countries in the european union and the world are facing vital challenges, it is unacceptable that the european commission does not put forward proposals that break with the policies that have led to the worsening of the social situation, the increase in unemployment and precarious and low-paid work, the financial, food and energy crisis, which mainly affects the countries with the weakest economies and the most vulnerable sections of the population, the growing militarization of international relations, with all the dangers this poses to world peace. even though it is aware that there is clear opposition and resistance from workers, consumers and users of public services to their privatisation and liberalisation, to unfair reforms in health and social security, to the distribution of income increasingly at the service of economic and financial groups, exacerbating social inequalities, the european commission insists on maintaining and continuing with the same instruments and policies that led to this situation, with particular emphasis on the stability pact and its irrational criteria, the liberal lisbon strategy, the false autonomy of the european central bank, and insists on unspeakable proposals for directives such as the directive on working time. at a time like this, the priority must be to put an end to the process of ratification of the draft treaty of lisbon, to respect democracy, the result of the referendum in ireland, the sovereign decision of its people, which follows the same results in france and the netherlands. it is time for the leaders of the european union to take back the leashes of these votes and of the opposition and resistance of the workers and peoples to neoliberal, militarist and anti-democratic policies. at this stage it is imperative that concrete proposals such as those we have put forward in our group's motion for a resolution be made, including the repeal of the stability pact, the end of privatisation and liberalisation, and a commitment to a monetary policy and a reorientation of the european central bank to give priority to employment with rights, the fight against poverty and social justice, including through a pact for social progress and development. we must give hope to our poor, create jobs with rights for our young people, respect equality for women and equal rights for women.
in writing. - we believe that the schengen area (which does not include all eu countries, let alone all european countries) strengthens the barriers between the countries participating in it and with other countries (in particular, with countries with which portugal has historical links). that said, we cannot ignore the fact that the use of 'freedom of movement' is intended to build an information system and databases that go far beyond this objective, seeking to make it one of the central instruments of support (the 'backbone') to the security offensive (played by the eu) and the progressive communitization of justice and home affairs, areas that are at the heart of the sovereignty of the states. that is, we cannot accept what the presidency of the council of the eu proposes: the system is installed, and its purpose will be defined later. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full.
in writing. − this proposal aims to amend the regulatory framework for electronic communications in order to improve its effectiveness, to make access to the frequencies available in the radio spectrum simpler and more efficient, and to reduce the administrative costs necessary to implement the regulation. in this way, european citizens should be able to benefit from more efficient and less expensive communications services wherever they are in the eu, whether they use mobile phones, broadband internet connections or cable television. the new radio spectrum regime aims to promote investment in new infrastructure and to enable all citizens to access broadband. a properly functioning internal market in communications and a competitive information society economy for the benefit of consumers and businesses can only exist if the telecommunications regulatory framework is applied consistently. to this end, the commission's coordination role should be strengthened, acting in close cooperation with the nras and the new european authority (bert), in order to improve coherence both in national decisions with an impact on the internal market and in the imposition of remedies. i therefore support this report and the main amendments which seek to widen the consumer's choice by strengthening competition.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the catherine trautmann report on electronic communications networks and services because i believe it is essential to improve the legislative framework for electronic communications by providing consumers with more choice, better protection, a cheaper service and better quality. together with the creation of a new european telecoms regulatory body, this new legislative framework will better protect consumers' private data, increase competition, provide more choice for consumers and make contractual terms clearer. it should also be noted that the package will facilitate access to telecommunications services for people with disabilities.
in writing. - we know that, like other natural resources, spectrum is a public good. so this is an area that should be kept in public management to ensure that it serves the public interest. only in this way would it be possible to provide public goods which are indispensable for the realisation of an information society for all. hence our basic disagreement with the resolution and the vote against the final text. experience has shown that so-called combined (political and market) approaches always end up serving the interests of economic groups more than the interests of the population. the same applies to the allocation of the spectrum freed up by the digital transition, where the priority should be social, cultural and economic value (better public service, wireless broadband to underserved areas, growth and employment, etc.) rather than the increase of public revenues. spectrum management is the exclusive responsibility of each national state, but there are some aspects of the resolution which deserve our agreement, given that spectrum knows no borders and that efficient use of spectrum in the member states and coordination at eu level are useful, particularly in the development of services and in the negotiation of international agreements. but we disagree that the same approach should be used as in trade policy.
in writing. − the liberalisation of telecommunications, which began in 2001, has unleashed european markets, which are now more competitive, innovative and highly profitable. european consumers have undoubtedly been the main beneficiaries of this development, with more and better services, forms and content becoming increasingly accessible. it was a technological, economic and socio-cultural (re) evolution. despite this frankly positive balance, we cannot rest on our laurels. there are still bottlenecks to the creation of a genuine integrated market, mainly due to disparities in the implementation of european regulation by each national regulatory authority (nra). i therefore support the creation of bert, the european telecommunications regulatory body, as an updated and strengthened version of the council of european regulators for electronic communications networks and services (erg), which is responsible for the most consistent application of the regulation and which has the effective participation of nras with valuable daily experience in the field. the establishment of bert promotes a consistent eu-wide regulatory approach to the remedial actions taken by nras, with full independence from governments and industry. bert will also perform functions in the field of consumer awareness. the eu has already had cause for satisfaction in this respect when it recalls its intervention to bring down the price of roaming substantially.
in writing. − the aim of this proposal is to promote coordinated action at eu level to ensure effective use of the digital dividend. the transition from analogue to digital terrestrial television by the end of 2012, when the increased efficiency of digital terrestrial television spectrum is expected to allow for a considerable release of spectrum, should create a unique opportunity for the eu to open up new possibilities for market growth, expansion of quality and choice of services to consumers. it is hoped that this will enable the ems to unlock their digital dividends as quickly as possible, so that european citizens can benefit from a whole new set of innovative and competitive services. member states should determine the use of the digital dividend and ensure that all types of electronic communications services are offered in the available radio frequency bands in accordance with their national radio frequency plan and the international telecommunication union regulations. however, it is essential that there is a coordinated community approach in order to avoid harmful interference between member states and between member states and third countries. it should also allow for the maximisation of the benefits of the use of that spectrum, ensuring optimal use from a social and economic point of view.
in writing. - it is symptomatic that the european parliament has not been able to adopt any resolution on the priorities of the european commission's programme. it is true that we are approaching the elections to the european parliament, and this is already influencing the decisions, especially those who want to whitewash their behaviour and their responsibilities in the policies that have led to the worsening of the social situation, the increase in unemployment and precarious and low-paid work, the financial, food and energy crisis that mainly affects the countries with the weakest economies and the most vulnerable sections of the population, the growing militarization of international relations, with all the dangers this poses to world peace. but at the same time they do not want to accept the need for a break with the policies that gave rise to it. they prefer that the european commission continue with the same instruments and policies that led to this situation, albeit with some pink and green touches to fuel illusions. we therefore insist on the proposals contained in our group's resolution, including the repeal of the stability pact, the end of privatisation and liberalisation, priority for employment with rights, the solution of the problem of poverty and social justice.
in writing. − 2009 will be marked by commission activity conditional on the timing of the european elections and, consequently, on the least possible opportunity for action, in particular by one of the institutions. this is not, however, an obstacle to a realistic business plan. the world requires a paradigm shift, an understanding that reality has far outgrown many of the theoretical debates about economic and social models, about the multiple polarities in international relations (both at the level of hard power and economic powers or the relations of trade forces). we must hope that the commission will respond to this new reality with a long-term vision that is flexible and adaptable in its implementation; at the same time we want an agenda for 2009 that helps to make clear to the voters in each member state the importance and the benefits of union policies for our economies and societies. this demonstration, which is much more a result of the quality of policies than of communication issues, must be the focus of our activity and, consequently, of the activity of the european commission. unfortunately, the resolution put to the vote did not reflect this approach, and i voted against it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's joint resolution on the preparation of the eu-india summit because i believe it is essential to adapt the strategic partnership with india, adopted in 2004, to the new challenges facing the eu and india, such as the food crisis, the energy crisis and climate change. i would stress that the resolution encourages india to continue its efforts to achieve the millennium development goals, particularly in the area of gender equality. it is also important that the resolution reminds india of the values of the european union, calling on the indian government to abolish the death penalty.
in writing. - in addition to the possible assessment of many other issues raised by this resolution, we consider it essential to underline that we are unquestioning advocates of deepening real and effective relations of cooperation and friendship between the countries that make up the eu and india. that is, a relationship based on responding to the needs of different peoples, which is mutually beneficial and contributes to mutual development, respecting the principle of non-interference and respect for national sovereignty. on the basis of these principles and assumptions, we naturally cannot agree with many of the proposals in this resolution, particularly as regards the establishment of a so-called 'free trade' agreement, which aims to include, among other things, an 'agreement on services', 'competition', 'public procurement' and 'the abolition of the current restrictions on direct investment' between the eu and india. this proposal (and its objective) seeks to respond to the expansionist aspirations of the major economic and financial groups - which have not been realised at the level of the wto negotiations aimed at liberalizing world trade - whose urgent need is to increase the accumulation and centralisation of capital. a move which is contrary to the needs of the workers and peoples of india and the various countries of the eu.
in writing. - sometimes it is necessary to remember that india is the largest democracy in the world in terms of population. this, coupled with its economic vitality and its growing role in international relations - first and foremost in that region - suggests that we rethink our relationship with this important partner. it would, of course, be a mistake to ignore the fragility of indian democracy, its economic structure or its social organization. so it should be considered that in our relationship with this country these aspects should be at the top of the agenda. however, this agenda must be broader and, above all, more in line with new realities and circumstances. strengthening political ties and getting closer to this giant must be seen as strategic. we must also be attentive and ready to strengthen india's role in the concert of nations, particularly in terms of institutional architecture and framework. if it is common to say that the 21st century will be the century of the pacific - a question which should receive the greatest attention in europe - it is worth adding the indic to this prophecy. and adapt our strategies accordingly.
what conclusions can we draw from the present crisis? it is the result of the choice not to monitor adequately the activity of the financial markets. competent regulation does not kill the market, on the contrary, it is indispensable to its survival. there are actors responsible for the losses, but today it is the citizens who pay the bill for their excesses and the failures of public oversight. the warning was given long ago. the rasmussen report, which this parliament adopted yesterday by a very large majority, makes precise proposals on the risks of excessive leverage, the lack of transparency, conflicts of interest, but it is the result of the work of the socialist group which was started years before the crisis of 2007 began. the own-initiative report by ieke van den burg and dăianu is in the same vein. the european union is a major partner in the international context, and i congratulate commissioner almunia on the announcements he has brought here today; but does commissioner mccreevy share them? the paralysis which the commission has had in these matters is not justifiable. parliament does its job. the other institutions should also act in a similar way.

in writing. we have recently experienced an escalation in fuel prices that was unheard of, largely as a result of speculation by companies that posted very high profits, the result of speculative appreciation of oil stocks bought at lower prices. this outrageous rise has worsened the living conditions of the general population, especially the economically weaker sections, and has had a devastating effect on economic activity in the various sectors: transport and other services, industry, agriculture and fisheries. however, despite the significant fall in crude oil prices, high price practices continue in several countries, which are a burden on consumers. this should lead to the creation by each member state of a tax exclusively on extraordinary and speculative profits, so that they are returned to the coffers of the states and thus help to support the sectors and populations most affected by the situation. but the big changes should be structural, stopping the liberalisation of the energy sector, bearing in mind that this is a strategic sector for development, so it must be a nationalised sector, in order to ensure public policies that serve the national interests and the general population.
mr president, this is a very important debate and i should like to start by welcoming the commission's initiative and mr foglietta's report. anorexia has been talked about more than obesity, even though obesity is becoming a real global epidemic. more than 50% of europeans are overweight and about 6% of healthcare expenditure is related to obesity these figures have already been mentioned here. childhood obesity continues to rise, with 22 million european children suffering from overweight. the fight against obesity must be a political priority for the european union. i therefore agree with the general measures proposed: consumer information, restriction of television advertising, nutritional and health claims on food labelling. people need to be made aware that obesity is a leading cause of death and is associated with many chronic diseases, such as diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disorders, bone and joint problems, respiratory diseases and cancer. we need to act and fast. the solution is known: more exercise and more careful eating. the exact opposite of what most people do. sandwiches and sodas, sweets and snacks should not be eaten every day, and a sedentary lifestyle is not good for your health. exercise can be walking at least half an hour a day, it does not require much effort, nor does it cost money, but it works. it's important for adults and it's fundamental for children. many parents are not even aware of the harm they are doing to their children by letting them spend their free time in front of the television or the computer, eating what they should not, without any kind of monitoring or control. the fight against obesity requires a concerted effort, involving schools, families and the productive, health and social sectors - each with its own responsibility. the role of the family in changing habits is decisive. it is the responsibility of the school to ensure that the quality and nutritional content of school meals is monitored, by prohibiting the sale of fatty, overly salty or sugary products in bars and vending machines, and at the same time to facilitate and promote physical activity among pupils.
mr president, it is important to have a global and integrated view of nutrition, overweight and obesity, since there are multiple factors involved where the issues of food poverty, malnutrition and lack of information on healthy eating are of particular importance. the issue of ensuring healthy food is therefore of particular importance and public policies should ensure that everyone has access to healthy food, which requires the provision of a range of measures to ensure the quality and proximity of agricultural production of quality foodstuffs, including milk, fruit and vegetables, and their distribution to people with limited economic resources. on the other hand, a different common agricultural policy, based on the defence of family farming and the creation of local markets for fruit, vegetables and other basic foodstuffs, the production of which is duly supported, can guarantee healthy food at affordable prices to the general population. there are proposals to provide some support for the distribution of fruit and vegetables in schools, it is essential to increase the amount the european commission proposes for this programme so as to ensure that it is distributed daily and free of charge to all school-age children and not just one day a week, as is the case now. but just as importantly, a whole range of public health policies and programmes must be put in place to make nutrition a priority, including health information and education campaigns, the promotion of healthy diets and lifestyles, including physical education and sport, ensuring that they are available to the general population, with particular emphasis on children and young people, particularly in schools.

in writing. − the serious public health problem of obesity and overweight should be tackled as a priority from the earliest stages of life this report calls on member states, local authorities and school authorities to monitor and improve the quality and nutritional standards of school meals. nutritional information on foods is important, in particular the distinction between natural trans fatty acids, present in meat and dairy products, and those produced during industrial (artificial) processing. indiscriminate labelling of trans fats will only confuse the consumer, create a negative image for healthy dairy products and have undesirable effects on consumption, harming public health (e.g. reduction of intake of important nutrients such as calcium and protein). european indicators (e.g. waist measurement) are useful in monitoring the degree of risk of the population for various obesity-related diseases. understanding how abdominal obesity is distributed allows planning more effective actions to reduce this problem. i agree with the existence of colour codes for food labelling because, more than clear and easily understandable labelling, european citizens need interpretative elements to make healthy choices.
in writing. − overweight and diet-related diseases are a serious public health problem, and the fight against obesity should be a priority from the earliest stages of life. the foglietta report is very relevant in calling on member states, local authorities and school authorities to monitor and improve the quality and nutritional standards of school meals. i believe that nutritional information should always be given on foods, in particular the indication of artificial trans fats, since these are the ones that have the most negative effects on health. failure to distinguish between artificial and natural trans fats would mislead consumers and would only contribute to a negative image of certain animal foods containing natural trans fats, such as meat and dairy products. i also voted in favour of the development of european indicators such as waist measurement and others indicating risk factors associated with obesity because i believe that these may be used in the future to assess the risk situation of the population and the success of the measures implemented.

on behalf of the pse group. on behalf of my group, i would like to thank the rapporteur for the work he has done. this is an important report, containing appropriate proposals for the european union to meet the challenge of water scarcity and droughts. the problem is not new, but it has been growing and widening. the 2003 drought affected more than 100 million people and a third of the union's territory and cost the european economy €8.7 billion. water scarcity is no longer limited to the countries of southern europe, but is also felt in central and northern europe, as mentioned here, and the situation is likely to worsen as a result of climate change. the european union must take urgent action to tackle these two problems: excessive water consumption and water waste. according to data from the european environment agency, there is a huge potential for water saving in europe. about 40% of the water used could be saved. on the other hand, europe continues to waste at least 20% of its water due to inefficiencies. in view of this, the amendments which i tabled and which the committee on the environment approved, on the reuse of waste water and desalination, are fully justified. and because leaks in pipelines cause a lot of waste, i proposed that the member states use the structural funds to upgrade and renew existing infrastructure and technologies. you can't develop a water-saving culture without the citizens. public awareness and education campaigns are therefore needed. water is a public good, but it's scarce. to make it affordable and accessible to all, everyone must play their part in reducing consumption and waste. before i conclude, i would like to ask the council and the commission when the mechanisms for supporting the solidarity fund will be made more flexible. since drought is an anomalous natural phenomenon with severe and lasting repercussions on living conditions and socioeconomic stability in the affected regions, it is desirable that the fund can support regional situations and that public and private losses are eligible.

in writing. - i support this initiative to extend once again the agreement (of june 2002) on the free movement of persons between switzerland and the eu to include romania and bulgaria. this enlargement will undoubtedly have a positive impact on the promotion of new employment and investment opportunities and on the economic growth of all the countries involved, in particular by increasing the volume of trade between them. special transitional periods of up to 7 years shall be provided for, during which switzerland shall be entitled to maintain quantitative limits for employees and self-employed persons of romanian or bulgarian nationality, in order to gradually facilitate the access of nationals of these countries to the swiss labour market and to increase the entry of these new workers every year, taking into account the needs of the market and the supply of labour available on swiss territory. the same quantitative limits may also be applied by romania and bulgaria in respect of swiss nationals for the same periods. after that period, any quotas may be reintroduced only if the necessary conditions laid down in the safeguard clause, which may only be applied until 2019, are fulfilled.
in writing. − since 2005, the commission has put forward a number of legislative initiatives to regulate and facilitate the exchange of criminal records, putting an end to a time-consuming and basically ineffective system that operated on the basis of the mechanisms provided for by the 1959 council of europe convention. the first improvement was introduced by the 2005 decision on the exchange of information extracted from the criminal record, in particular as regards the shortening of the transmission deadlines. in 2007, the council reached a political agreement on a framework decision to ensure that each member state can respond in the most complete and correct way to requests for criminal records submitted to it concerning its nationals. the present initiative is not intended to change the basic principles of this framework decision, but to complement it. it aims to create a computerised system for the exchange of information on convictions between member states, namely the european criminal records information system (ecris). there are still 27 distinct legal systems with different legal and social sensitivities, but an attempt has been made to find a common ground to enable the system to be applied in practice. in this context, in order to ensure adequate data protection, it is once again clear that there is an urgent need to adopt the framework decision on data protection in the third pillar, which i have repeatedly called for.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the commission states that the central objective is to 'strengthen the european area of security and justice' and that 'information on previous convictions should circulate among judges, prosecutors and police authorities'. as stated, 'the objective presupposes the systematic exchange between the competent authorities of the member states of information extracted from national criminal records in such a way as to ensure the uniform interpretation of that information and the effectiveness of such exchanges'. we believe that, where necessary, the transfer of information extracted from the criminal records of citizens from one member state to another should be carried out on the basis of (bilateral) cooperation between the parties involved. however, among other issues whose scope and implications should be assessed, the report introduces obligations for the member states, as part of the communityisation of justice and home affairs to a level that goes beyond the basis of cooperation between member states, which we point out. we obviously recognise the need for mechanisms for the reciprocal transmission of information on criminal records between different member states, analysing each case and within a framework of cooperation between them.

the new proposal for a directive which we are debating today, madam president, while proclaiming the principle of equal treatment for workers in terms of working conditions, maximum working time and weekly rest periods, allows for a number of exceptions which in practice can call into question these same principles, especially when what is needed is to combat the proliferation of temporary employment agencies and to reduce this to a minimum in order to stop precarious work and prevent workers' rights from being further undermined. we therefore insist, through the introduction of a set of amendments, on ensuring that, for example, the use of temporary agency work should be restricted to exceptional situations, such as times of extraordinary activity and periods of temporary incapacity of the permanent worker; that temporary agency workers should be able to enjoy the labour rights and social protection conferred on other workers, including the rights enshrined in the collective agreements of the sector in which they work; that temporary agency work should not be used to undermine the right to strike; that the same provisions on safety, hygiene and health at work should apply to temporary agency workers as to the workers of the employing undertaking.
madam president, mr minister, mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i am very pleased with this report, which closes a pending matter from 2002. i think that this is a balanced situation which protects temporary workers, makes the labour market more flexible and respects the principle of subsidiarity. this proposal ensures, as a general rule, equal treatment of temporary agency workers from day one, but also offers the possibility for the social partners, if they so wish, to agree otherwise. given the diversity of practices and legislation in this field between the member states, it is encouraging that parliament, the council and the commission have reached agreement. this agreement is reflected in a stable framework for temporary employment agencies, whose role in the european labour market is undeniable. this increased regulatory transparency could facilitate job creation as well as the flexibility of new forms of work. i am well aware that economic developments require greater flexibility in the labour market, but i believe that this flexibility will only be to the advantage of all if it is achieved by respecting the rights of workers in all respects, and in particular those relating to health and safety at the workplace. in my view, the final result of the text of this directive is a good example of this balance. i hope, mr minister, that you will be able to say the same about the working time directive in december. i am grateful to mr harlem désir for his work and to the shadow rapporteur of my political family, mrs elisabeth morin, whom i congratulate on having made a major contribution to this final result.

the rapporteur. - in view of the permanent structural constraints and disadvantages facing the outermost regions, it is necessary to adopt measures which are not subject to transitional criteria or to cyclical or artificial changes in wealth which contribute to promoting their socioeconomic development. fisheries is a strategic sector for these regions, both in terms of supplying fish to their populations and in terms of employment and economic sustainability for their fishing communities. however, despite the improvements made, their fishing fleets are made up of mostly ageing vessels, with an average age of more than 30 or 40 years, particularly in the artisanal fleet. new financial support is needed for the renewal and modernisation of the fishing fleets in these regions, and it is not understood that the european union will make this impossible. continued support for the renewal and modernisation of fishing fleets is considered to be an indispensable condition for improving the safety and working conditions of fishermen and the conditions for the conservation of fish. the committee on fisheries of the european parliament only proposes to extend public aid for the renewal of the fleets of the outermost regions until 2009 and the possibility of registering these vessels until 2011. although we go further than the european commission proposes, we consider that these proposals are still insufficient and do not meet the real needs of fishermen in these regions, particularly small-scale fishermen. we therefore table our amendments to ensure that public aid is granted for the renewal and modernisation of fishing fleets, without any time limit and in accordance with the needs of the sector in these regions. although it is not necessary, it could even be stressed that this is a measure without any additional cost to the community budget and without any impact on the increase in fleet capacity. these are proposals previously adopted by the european parliament itself, which reiterated in 2005 the need for future support for the renewal and modernisation of the fishing fleet in order to make the sector in these regions profitable and competitive, and by the committee on fisheries of this parliament, which this year considered that new support was needed for the renewal and modernisation of the fleets of the outermost regions, since the end of community aid for fleet renewal will make it difficult to overcome their backwardness in relation to the structure of the european continent's fleets, so that, at the crucial moment of the decision, we are simply calling for consistency with parliament's own positions.
on behalf of the pse group. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to remind you of the need to take account of the needs of the fisheries sector in the outermost regions, and to stress the extension of the new deadline for derogating from the general system of entry and exit of fleets in favour of the outermost regions. this extension approved by the commission means that fishing vessels which have benefited from public aid under the derogation can be integrated into the fishing fleet of these regions until 2011 without the entry of new capacity having to be offset by the exit of equivalent capacity. this amendment is the commission's proposal, which was the result of an agreement between the socialist party and the epp-ed with the involvement of members from these two groups from the outermost regions and also the rapporteur, mr pedro guerreiro, although, as we have just heard, he wanted to go further. as the shadow rapporteur for the pse i have been committed to this objective and so i ask members to vote in favour of this report tomorrow and i call on the commission, the commissioner and the council to take account of the legislative resolution of the european parliament which i hope will be adopted tomorrow.
mr president, i believe that the work we have done in the committee on fisheries, involving our rapporteur, the various political groups and the european commission, has been extremely fruitful and that we have reached a conclusion - which i think is very consensual, not entirely, but very consensual - also involving the european commission, that extending the deadline until 2011, with the preparation of a report which can assess the need for extension of this measure, is the most correct way of dealing with this problem. it was an effort for which i would like to congratulate all our colleagues in the epp-ed who agreed this position with us and the european commission. it is now up to us to hope that the council will also be sensitive to what we have decided here and that it will understand the need to give the outermost regions a little more time to fulfil this wish.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, should state aid for the modernisation and renewal of the fishing fleets in the outermost regions be authorised only until the end of 2009 or should it be granted for an indefinite period? the specific characteristics of fishing activities in these regions justify that these aids can be granted beyond 2009 without any damage to the marine environment. state aid for the modernization and renewal of the fleets of the outermost regions for an indefinite period of time does not mean permanent and perpetual aid. they would be immediately discontinued if the studies and the evaluation of the scientific council and the regional advisory councils showed such a need. this is the solution that would best suit the very specific reality of fisheries in the outermost regions. the same reasons which justify an exclusive fishing reserve of up to 100 miles for fishermen in each oct also justify a different treatment in respect of aid for fleet modernisation and renewal. fortunately, the committee on fisheries has found the best solutions to the specific problems of fishing in the outermost regions.
member of the commission. − thank you very much for your comments. i can assure you of my commitment to assisting the fleets of the outermost regions as far as i can and as far as this is possible. however, let me stress that maintaining or even increasing capacity of these fleets is not the solution and can indeed be part of the problem. as i stated in my opening remarks, if there needs to be a measure of restructuring of these fleets, i would urge you to consider the recently adopted fuel package that provides for a number of possibilities that may be beneficial to the fleets of the outermost regions. again, as i said, i can accept the extension of the deadline for entry into the fleet register in view of the backlog problems faced by shipyards, but i cannot accept the further extension for the granting of public aid for construction and for the entry-exit regime beyond what had already been granted under the european fisheries fund, where special consideration was made for the outermost regions, since this will not solve any problems but will only serve to generate more problems. we accept that there is overfishing and we acknowledge that this is due to overcapacity. the commission does not want to contribute to overcapacity in peripheral regions as well, because this will only cause problems for the future. with regard to the possibility of overfishing around the peripheral regions, we have been looking into this and the council has just adopted a regulation on iuu fishing, with the european parliament’s blessing. as from 1 january 2010, no fish that are not certified as having been legally caught can enter the european market. we are also taking the lead in regional fisheries organisations in order to propose sustainable fishing in the oceans wherever we have a voice, and that is in virtually all regional fisheries organisations. we intend to persevere with this effort so that in this way we can guarantee sustainable fishing, not only in our waters but in international waters, which are so crucial for our outermost regions.
the rapporteur. - i would like to thank the speakers for their comments and to remind them that, as stipulated in the treaties themselves, measures to support the outermost regions are possible and desirable. this possibility must be given practical expression. fishing is a strategic sector for these regions. the fisheries sector needs support for its renewal and modernisation, and this is a perfectly natural question. there are community financial resources and, as the debate so far has shown, not a single valid argument has been put forward to continue to prevent public aid for the renewal and modernisation of the fishing fleets in these regions. contrary to what has been claimed, fleet renewal and modernisation does not necessarily lead to overcapacity or increase overcapacity. the question is, then, why are no measures taken to ensure that they are? that is, after the debate we have had, we are more convinced that not only is it necessary to extend the deadline for the entry of vessels which have benefited from public aid for modernisation, as proposed by the european commission and the committee on fisheries, but it is also necessary to ensure that public aid is available for the renewal and modernisation of the fleets in these regions, in particular for the small-scale fleet, without any time limits, as we have consistently advocated once again. we therefore hope that you will support the amendments we have tabled tomorrow. reality demands it, and time will show us the reason.
