in writing. the commission proposes to mobilise the solidarity fund for france. the interinstitutional agreement provides for the mobilisation of this fund within an annual ceiling of eur 1 billion per year. during 2008, eur 260 411 197 was mobilised for the united kingdom (eur 162 387 985), greece (eur 89 769 009) and slovenia (eur 8 254 203). france requested support from the fund following hurricane dean, which struck martinique and guadeloupe in august 2007. the commission proposes to mobilise the solidarity fund for an amount of eur 12 780 000, to be allocated as part of the unused cohesion fund. however, as in the previous cases, there is at least one question that is raised: how is it possible that only now, more than a year after the catastrophes that have hit the people, is eu money being made available? there's definitely something wrong. we recall that we have put forward proposals to speed up the procedures for mobilising this fund and to ensure that regional disasters remain eligible, and to recognise the specific nature of mediterranean natural disasters such as drought and fires in this fund.
in writing. − spain submitted an application for 1589 redundancies, of which 1521 were at delphi automotive systems españa and 68 were at its suppliers, requesting a contribution of eur 10 471 778 to cover part of the cost of the assistance measures, some eur 20.94 million. lithuania submitted an application for 1089 redundancies due to the closure of alytaus tekstile, a textile manufacturing plant, requesting eur 298 994 out of the total costs of around eur 0,06 million. as we have said, the existence of this fund cannot serve as a temporary cushion for the unacceptable socioeconomic costs of relocating companies and their redundancies and for the failure to change the policies that are the cause of exploitation, precariousness and unemployment of workers. what is needed is to prevent and penalize the relocation of companies and to put an end to the policy of liberalizing world trade, instigated by the eu. the granting of public aid should be conditional on long-term commitments in terms of employment and regional development and no aid should be granted which could be used to promote relocations. it is essential to strengthen the role of employee representatives on company boards and in the taking of management decisions of a structural nature.
in writing. - climate change on the planet is due, in addition to its natural development, to a policy of intensified exploitation of natural resources by the industrialized countries, which has accentuated it to a level that confronts humanity with serious problems. responsible action to deal with the consequences of the brutal waste of natural resources requires a break with the capitalist policies that are at its origin. however, the vision that is being set out, with the eu at the head, is that of a joint responsibility of all countries, seeking to impose on the 'developing' countries limitations on the sovereign use of their natural resources, obviously in line with the ambitions of their exploitation by the large transnational corporations. the text adopted by the ep, which contains contradictions and other aspects, completely ignores these central issues, advocating instead a 'security policy to prevent or respond to security risks or conflicts linked to climate', securing and militarising international relations by using 'climate change'. the report also advocates the creation of so-called ecological taxes (as opposed to a tax system based on income), which open the way to the privatisation of public services and private exploitation of such basic resources as water.
in writing. - climate change is a topic worth discussing when it is in the territory of responses. what we must do is reject dogma and unconsciousness. in contrast to a fatalistic discourse which identifies the growth of the world population, the increase in consumption and, inevitably, the improvement of the living conditions of millions of human beings with a potential environmental tragedy, we must bet on the modern scientific capacity and the enormous progress of which we are the beneficiaries to find adequate answers that avoid the risk of containing unwanted effects (as so often happens in hasty decisions made out of the will to act right away but without knowing precisely the reality to which they respond). however, whatever the path taken - or paths, since there must be multiple responses - it is imperative to recognize that there are countries less prepared to react, countries in the development phase which prevent them from having the necessary means and which place them in a situation of enormous fragility. thinking about these countries and their populations, with a view to mitigating the negative impact of climate change and adapting to it, must be a central focus of our policy.
in writing. - obviously, this does not affect our support for the necessary involvement of regional and local authorities or other public authorities, social and economic organisations and the population in the definition of objectives and programmes and in the implementation and monitoring of the use of the community structural funds at the level of each member state, a question we have always raised. however, we cannot accept that other objectives are being pursued under the cover of this legitimate aspiration, such as the merging of the different community funds (european regional development fund, european social fund, cohesion fund and european agricultural fund for rural development) in the 'future cohesion policy after 2013'. this proposal could call into question the central objective of the community budget, namely its redistributive function between the so-called 'cohesion' and the so-called 'rich' countries, in particular by eliminating funds intended only for the former (in addition to calling into question the community financing of 'common policies' such as agriculture and fisheries). we cannot yet agree with its promotion of so-called 'public-private partnerships', which are used to privatise public services that are essential and strategic for the people and the socioeconomic development of each member state.
in writing. - if we want to discuss the need for 'better legislation' before we start a debate on the content of european legislation, we must consider the real need for much of it. it is true that the creation of a common market, the establishment of a uniformity between countries with different histories and traditions, often visible in the details of their legislation, gives rise to a need for harmony which requires possibly more proactive legislative activity. but to say that is not to say that legislation should be introduced first and foremost and that it should be done at european level. without prejudice to the conviction that the eu is often the right platform for action, it must also be said that the principle of subsidiarity is fundamental, too often obliterated in the name of an efficiency that is not real and of a result that is not necessary. if we want the eu to be able to respond to the needs for which a european level of decisionmaking is required, we should, in a coherent and wise way, avoid flooding 'europe' with projects and legislative powers which can be effectively implemented at national level. this concern, which is frequently expressed in the treaties, is unfortunately not very much present in 'brussels', with the inevitable consequences also in terms of bureaucratic temptation.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the evelyne gebhardt report on the law applicable to marriage. given the increased mobility of citizens within the eu and the heterogeneity of the applicable legislation in the different member states, in the event of divorce, i advocate the possibility for spouses, who are of different nationality or reside in different member states, to be able to choose the law applicable to their divorce proceedings. i think, however, that it is essential to promote information for each of the members of the couple so that both know exactly what the legal and social consequences are of the choice of the applicable law.
in writing. - regulation (ec) no 639/2004 on the management of fishing fleets registered in the outermost regions provides for derogations from the entry/exit regime provided for in article 13 of regulation (ec) no 2371/2002 on the conservation and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources under the common fisheries policy. however, the late adoption of the commission legal instrument allowing the member states concerned to grant state aid and the limited capacity of the yards made it impossible to meet the deadline for the entry into the fleet of fishing vessels benefiting from state aid for renewal by 31 december 2008, as laid down in regulation (ec) no 639/2004. the committee on fisheries has advocated in its report the extension of the deadlines for public aid for renewal and for the registration of vessels, both in relation to the regulation currently in force and in relation to the proposal submitted by the european commission, according to which the deadline should be extended by one year only, i.e. until 31 december 2009. the extension of public aid for the renewal of the fleets of the outermost regions until 31 december 2009 and the possibility of registering these vessels until 31 december 2011 is a valuable aid in view of the above constraints. the guerreiro report therefore deserves my vote in favour.
in writing. − support for the renewal and modernisation of fishing fleets in the outermost regions is of the greatest interest given the importance of the fisheries sector in these regions. the report voted on today seeks to extend for another year the period of financing for the renewal and modernisation of the fishing fleet in the outermost regions. in these regions, it is justified to take into account the specific structural, social and economic situation with regard to the management of fishing fleets. this means adapting to their needs the provisions on the management of fleet entry/exit schemes and compulsory capacity withdrawal, as well as the conditions for access to public aid for the modernisation and renewal of fishing vessels. in summary, support for the renewal and modernisation of the fisheries fleets of the ors should be maintained, particularly in relation to the small-scale fleet, since the fleets of these regions are made up of a majority of ageing vessels, some of which are over 30 years old. these measures are essential to improve the conditions for the conservation of fish and the working and safety conditions of fishermen in these regions.

mr president, commissioner, president sarkozy was speaking here this morning about the difference between protectionism and intelligent market interventions. if we add to this the numerous situations in which european industry is burdened with rules and restrictions which, although necessary, make it less competitive, we can easily find reason to commend and vote in favour of the proposal under discussion today. it is well known that the european union has a number of instruments at its disposal to achieve the three-twenties objective it has set itself: one of the most frequent ways is to require european industries to comply with environmental and emission control criteria; another alternative, the one we're discussing here today, suggests that public entities act as market drivers. it makes perfect sense. encouraging large public buyers to stimulate markets and to fuel demand for clean, energy-efficient vehicles, the production of which is perhaps more costly but environmentally friendly, is a legitimate, appropriate and justifiable way of acting in the market. obviously, this intervention cannot be carried out against the interests of the taxpayers. but this interest must measure both the immediate costs and the environmental benefits it brings to the daily lives of citizens. the compromise we are discussing today means that public services are required to calculate not only the purchase price but also the fuel costs, co2 emissions and air pollution over the life cycle of the vehicles when purchasing their road transport fleets and to use these costs as a purchasing criterion. the public authorities thus have the opportunity in the future to be at the centre of the example and the incentive for the automotive sector to develop and invest in the production of environmentally friendly vehicles with ever lower co2 and pollutant emissions. finally, i would like to congratulate mr jørgensen and the rapporteurs whose work has enabled this document to be debated today, in the hope that it will really contribute to a change in habits with positive consequences for a sustainable future for our societies.

many of us in the house use the internet to book our flights and buy our travels. however, i think most of us are not aware of the criteria for determining the value of airport charges which are paid together with the tickets. knowing, however, that not all the fees listed on the ticket are airport fees, i ask you to accompany me in a little reasoning and a little exercise: if a passenger flies from lisbon to brussels, for example, on brussels airlines, the fee on the ticket is 48 euros, if it is on tap, the portuguese airline, it is minus 2 euros. however, on return, this difference disappears and the passenger is offered a surcharge on the fares of eur 15 per journey. what's the reason? however, if our imaginary passenger travels to london on brussels airlines, leaving brussels and using gatwick airport, the fares cost €124 for a round trip, but if he uses heathrow at bmi, he only pays €65 in fares and if he goes to bmi and returns on lufthansa, again via heathrow, he already pays €70 in fares. why these differences? sometimes you pay one amount on the way out and another on the way back. sometimes for the same airport the airlines all charge the same and sometimes they don't, and it even happens that you don't know how much you pay in some cases. the existence of different airport charges is not a bad thing, on the contrary. different services should be charged different rates. what is undesirable is that different services should be charged the same rates and, on the contrary, that apparently identical services should be charged different rates. above all, we want these rates to be comprehensible and to be set according to transparent and clear criteria. that's what we're looking for, after all. to establish fair and transparent competition between the major european airports and thereby contribute not only to the improvement of the internal market but also to the reduction of the costs incurred by passengers when purchasing their ticket. that is why we support this proposal for a directive with hope.

also be noted that the new electronic system for the management and control of transactions is a welcome change which should simplify the operation of the system, both for operators and for the tax authorities, as the commissioner has just mentioned. as regards these more technical aspects - which also include the deadlines for transmitting documents, the rules for the provision of financial guarantees by operators, etc. - the commission's and the rapporteur's proposal deserves applause, consensus and represents serious and useful progress. however, in excise duties, the political content focus on two illustrative issues in this regard. one is the indicative limits on the personal transport of these goods and the other is the rules for the sale of goods via the internet. these matters clearly separate us from the rapporteur. the disparities between the taxation of alcohol and tobacco, and also of fuel, in the member states are very, very large and, consequently, the differences in the prices of sales to the public are also very large. it is sufficient to recall that the price of a pack of tobacco can vary between eur 1 and eur 7 within the union due to the large differences in taxation. as a rule, taxes are due in the country of consumption, with the exception of goods transported within the european union. under the current rules, certain quantitative limits must be respected, otherwise it will be assumed that the products transported have commercial purposes. the commission proposal is aimed at abolishing these quantitative limits, and the rapporteur, mrs lulling, has agreed with this. that was not the view of the committee on economic and monetary affairs. on the contrary, we agreed to lower this threshold, following the initiatives of the shadow rapporteurs, benoît hamon, olle schmidt and myself. liberalisation does indeed allow certain consumers to reduce the cost of purchasing these goods, but it is not sensible for this to be done at the expense of the public finances of the member states, at the expense of public health objectives which the member states have the right to safeguard and, finally, thereby feeding the parallel market, which we all must avoid. so the final agreement reached in the parliamentary committee is to keep the limits at a reasonable level, 400 cigarettes or 45 litres of wine per person. this is assumed to be what is necessary for personal consumption, without affecting travellers who actually purchase these goods to this extent. for the same reasons we oppose amendment no 68 by the epp group, which proposes to tax distance sales, particularly those made via the internet, in the country of the seller and not in the country of the consumer, which is an unjustified reversal of the general principle of taxation. this amendment would also open the door to a large-scale parallel market and should be rejected. finally, and in conclusion, i shall just mention the question of duty-free shops. the internationally recognised principle is that these should only be in ports and airports to allow for optimal control and to prevent any risk of fraud or abuse. we must nevertheless allow adequate time for adaptation and that is why we have proposed, on behalf of the socialist group, a transitional period for member states which still have free shops, allowing them to make a gradual adjustment to the new situation and proposing 1 january 2017, a date which is far away, to allow a gradual approximation to the common rule. so we think this line is the appropriate line. it's a line that has generated consensus. it is not a total consensus, but a majority approval at the level of the economic and monetary committee, and i hope that it will be voted on in this plenary tomorrow.

and rural world of the european union. i have had the opportunity to hear, throughout this time, a great many opinions from organisations representing the agricultural and rural sectors in various member states and to speak with members of parliament and institutional representatives from many, i would say almost all member states and community institutions, starting here, of course, with the european parliament. i have attended various seminars and conferences and have been attentive to all the echoes transmitted by the media in search of the best possible synthesis. i should therefore like to thank all the members who have been enthusiastically involved in this debate, the coordinators of the political groups, and i should like to highlight the role played by mr goepel, not only as coordinator of the epp, but also as rapporteur of the own-initiative report which preceded the reports we are discussing here today. i also thank mr parish for the way he conducted the work of our committee and for the excellent cooperation of the comagri secretariat, which was responsible for the most laborious and technically demanding part of the work. finally, to the commission, in the person of the commissioner, for the availability she and her services have always shown, and to minister barnier for the way in which she has been able to maintain a continuous relationship with parliament even before the formal start of the french presidency of the council. the exercise of enhanced cooperation we are pursuing has been a good example of anticipating the virtualities of codecision, which i hope will come into force with the full ratification of the lisbon treaty as soon as possible. the debate we are having, with all the divergences and convergences that have emerged from it, reflects well the complexity of the heterogeneous european agriculture, but it also reflects in an exemplary way the importance that europe, its institutions and parliament in particular attach to this subject. the fact that the commission has tabled 1170 amendments to the commission's proposals, even taking into account the time available interrupted by the summer holidays, is a sign of the wide participation which this debate has aroused among all members. but the commitments made by four of the most important political groups in parliament, concentrating in six commitments some 400 amendments on the most important issues, also reveal the sense of responsibility and the spirit of commitment and the capacity for compromise of the members. as regards the content of the report, which i consider to be quite balanced and capable of responding to the challenges of the present and of giving good guidelines for the future, i would like to stress that parliament recognises as positive and welcomes and subscribes to many of the commission's proposals. i would stress the confirmation of the need for a common policy as an indispensable condition for a competitive and environmentally sustainable agriculture in europe, the contributions made by the commission to make the cap fairer and more acceptable to society, the commitment to simplification and reduction of bureaucracy, the confirmation of the option of giving farmers greater freedom of choice in defining their production options, the financial strengthening of rural development and the extension of its scope to the so-called new challenges (energy, climate, water, biodiversity), the introduction of the principle of the progressivity of modulation, the extension of the flexibility granted to member states in the management of the cap (article 68), the creation of a system of risks and crises with community co-financing, the good general orientation given to the discussion of the model for the period after 2013 and to a good response by the european union in the context of the wto negotiations, with a view to a fair and reciprocal agreement on international trade in agricultural products. however, the commission's proposals also contain aspects which parliament, and i myself as rapporteur, have considered less positive, and as i have already had occasion to mention in other circumstances, the commission's proposals contain in some respects, for example as regards the instruments for managing the market and the milk sector, an excessively liberal tone which can become dangerous at the very moment when there is enormous instability and volatility on the markets. it also shows a certain social insensitivity, which is clearly evident in the proposal to exclude small farmers. i also think that the commission's proposal is not going in the right direction with regard to social and territorial cohesion, by proposing the end of the mechanism for redistributing the funds of the new modulation, and i also think that the commission has not taken due account of some sectors which are particularly vulnerable to the current market crisis and which are at serious risk of being abandoned with regard to the timetable and the pace proposed for the decommissioning by 2013, such as the sheep sector and what we have agreed to call the small cmos, which, being small, are very large and of very great political, economic and social importance for some regions of europe, where the alternatives are very difficult. the report and the vote in the committee on agriculture, by a large majority, aimed to correct some of these less positive aspects. the five commitments adopted on the key issues of modulation, the percentage and the progressivity of support for small farmers, giving member states greater freedom to set minimum thresholds, the percentage of article 68 and the extension of its scope, the wider scope of the insurance system by extending it to livestock farming, the question of co-financing rural development and the extension of the new challenges were relevant proposals from parliament, alongside many others which also constitute positive contributions, of which i would highlight, for example, the value of the employment factor for the calculation of the allocation of aid and the respect of health and safety conditions at work as regards the conditions for receiving such aid. the committee on agriculture has also taken a very clear position on the most difficult aspect of this dossier, the milk sector. it is a matter of great importance, the approach to which, given the present situation on the markets, requires careful consideration. although i have the greatest respect for all the views, and they are absolutely different in some cases, but both are respectable, i think the position adopted by the committee on agriculture is quite sensible and i would like to see it adopted in the plenary and confirmed by the council with the commission's approval. a prudent increase in production over two years, in addition to the 2% we have decided for 2008, and a definitive decision, anticipated for 2010, on the future of the sector, based on the behaviour of market developments, with a 4% increase over three years, seems to me a very sensible position and perhaps the one that could make the final compromise. i shall end, madam president, just to express my hope that this debate, and the debate that will follow, will help to clarify positions and that we can achieve the consensus that agriculture and farmers expect from us. i hope we all know - parliament, council and commission - that we can rise to this challenge.
we are concerned to be involved in this debate on further changes to the common agricultural policy, which is basically aimed at greater liberalization and subordination to international markets, without taking into account that agriculture is a strategic sector and that food security and food sovereignty should be the key factors in ensuring a quality food for the people of our countries. the social insensitivity with which this reform is being pursued, without taking account of the serious unemployment situation, is also unacceptable and threatens to destroy what remains of family farming, with the cutting of support for small farmers, the announced end of the milk quota system, the renationalisation of the cap costs and the continuing injustices in the allocation of support being particularly serious. we therefore insist on the proposals we have put forward to ensure support for farmers who produce, to combat the instability of productive sectors due to price fluctuations and to prevent the decline of the rural world and the desertification of many regions.
mr president, commissioner fischer boel, minister michel barnier, a medical examination should be used to correct things that are not quite right. there is one aspect of the legislation on agriculture in the outermost regions which is not right, namely the regulation of sugar in the autonomous region of the azores. i would like to ask the commissioner and the minister to look at the amendments i have tabled here and all the members to consider what is at stake, how easy and simple it is to solve a problem. but if it is not resolved, it will mean unemployment and the bankruptcy of a sector with very serious consequences in the autonomous region of the azores. i would urge you once again to give this your full consideration.
the extensive list of speakers and the passionate and convincing way in which they expressed their ideas confirmed once again the extent to which this subject has mobilized the european parliament and the importance which agriculture, farmers and the rural world in europe deserve. the debate was not surprising, because in essence the positions reiterated in the various debates throughout this long process of discussion which has lasted over a year and, in the specific case of my political group, another six months. but it seems to me that it has also been well demonstrated that no alternatives have been put forward to the positions which represent the possible bisectricity for a responsible compromise which can be accepted by the majority. the commission and the council have also reaffirmed their positions, but i have noted with great appreciation the signs of flexibility and openness that have been shown. i therefore trust in your political realism, dear mariann and dear michel, and in your commitment to find a final solution very close to that proposed by parliament on the essential questions. i repeat the symbolic importance of this rapprochement on the eve of the european parliament's assumption of co-decision powers, because i hope that the problem of ratifying the treaty of lisbon will be solved, because europe needs the treaty of lisbon. mr barnier, as i have said many times, we are not yet in the co-decision phase, but we are already in the spirit of co-decision. i therefore wish the difficult negotiations that await us today and tomorrow the greatest possible success and i am sure that we will be able to find a consensual solution that meets the aspirations of european farmers, that meets the aspirations of agriculture, that has its eyes on us, because we are all convinced, and this is the best conclusion of this debate, that a common agricultural policy is needed in europe if european agriculture is to be competitive and environmentally sustainable.
we stress the importance of establishing a genuine system of free daily distribution of fresh fruit and vegetables in season to schools, giving priority to children in pre-school and primary education, given its positive effect on healthy food, public health, combating child poverty and the boost and support it can give to regional products, including those from mountain regions, produced locally by our farmers. this requires much more funding than is provided by the european commission. so, commissioner, you must take account of the proposals that the committee on agriculture and rural development of the european parliament is putting forward here, to which we have also contributed, and congratulate our rapporteur on the work he has done.
i wanted to protest against the statement made by mrs lulling, which is intended to condition the vote of members in this house, and that conditioning is meaningless. the interpretation you are giving is one which we do not share, and it is only in this sense that i would like to ask my colleagues, who know what they are dealing with, who know that we are defending other interests, which are the interests of public health and the interests of citizens and the interests of countries, to vote in favour of the report. in writing. − the document in question does not fundamentally change the content of the regulation adopted in this parliament in november 2008, which regulated the establishment of a public-private partnership for the implementation of a european air traffic management system. the amendments currently being made to the regulation are aimed at recognising sesar as a community body and applying to its officials the status of officials of the european communities. changes were also made to the quantification of the community contribution and its transfer to sesar - a maximum of eur 700 million, 50% of which will be paid from the budgetary allocation of the 7th framework programme for research and technological development and the other half from the trans-european networks programme. the creation of this company sets a dangerous precedent in the use of public money for private purposes. they could have followed the public sector's lead in updating and improving air traffic management systems, including on matters related to their reliability, ensuring the safety of airspace professionals and users. we believe that these objectives will not be better achieved by subjecting them to the interests and pressures of the private sector. for these reasons, we did not support this report.
in writing. - italy submitted an application for redundancies in sardinia (1044 redundancies, 5 companies), piedmont (1537, 202), lombardy (1816, 190) and tuscany (1588, 461) between 2007 and 2008, following the liberalisation of textile and clothing trade. for a total of 5985 redundancies in 858 companies, italy is requesting a contribution of eur 38 158 075. as we have said, the existence of this fund cannot serve as a temporary cushion for the unacceptable socioeconomic costs of trade liberalization, particularly in textiles and clothing, and for the increasing precariousness of workers. with the (possible) expiry on 31.12.2008 of the common system of surveillance for exports of certain categories of textile and clothing products from china, it is necessary to establish mechanisms that limit imports from any country into the eu. in the face of the growing number of companies closing down or relocating their production, the increase in unemployment and the intensification of the exploitation of workers - particularly in portugal - what is needed is an end to the policy of liberalization of world trade (instigated by the eu and the ps government), and the defence of production and employment with rights in the different eu countries.
in writing. - the occasion of the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund at the request of italy is an excellent opportunity to reflect on the reactions that will be needed in the future, when the combined effects of globalisation and the economic crisis will be felt more acutely. the formula of this fund, which follows restricted principles in determining the scope of application, suggests that the european union regards globalisation as a fact and its negative effects as a reality to which we must adapt and not oppose. it's a realistic vision with a potential for effectiveness that i think is significant. understanding the changing world and channeling efforts to respond to it is more appropriate than believing in the possibility of avoiding it indefinitely. or even to believe that this opposition is, in itself, virtuous. adjustment to globalisation is a more appropriate policy option than opposition to globalisation.
in writing. - one of the most important factors in the crisis in the financial system was the excessive ease of supply, the excessive tolerance of indebtedness. it must be concluded, first, that the obligation on banks to ensure the ability/probability of those to whom they lend to comply seems to be a path that should be fruitful, despite the reality of the crisis and its causes. at the same time, the lack of awareness among consumers of the risks associated with the granting of credit - from the very beginning on the question of the fluctuation of reference rates - suggests that some action can and should be taken with them. it is true that the pressure to adopt an economic model based on maximum consumption will hardly be counteracted by such campaigns, but the effort to raise awareness is still necessary and, we hope, useful. in any case, this report should encourage greater transparency and the imposition of clearer rules on the conditions under which credit institutions provide services. as regards education for credit or other types of consumption, it is emphasized that the most important is education in general, which provides citizens with tools for daily decisions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the busk report on the proposal to establish a fruit distribution scheme in schools, because i believe that community support for the free distribution of these products to children is fundamental to promoting healthy eating habits in the european union and, consequently, to improving the health of europeans. the high prevalence of obesity and overweight among the european population, particularly in childhood, is the result of the association between poor eating habits and sedentary lifestyle. it is therefore urgent to take effective measures to combat this epidemic, in particular by promoting healthy eating habits in the first years of life. schools, in conjunction with families, can play a key role in the adoption of a healthy diet.
in writing. − we support this report, to which we have contributed a number of proposals. despite the opposition of the european commission, the report advocates the daily free distribution of fresh fruit in schools to improve the health and quality of life of children, especially those from the most disadvantaged classes. support for this programme takes into account the need to stimulate young people to enjoy fruit and vegetables, which will have a highly positive effect on public health and the fight against child poverty. to be effective, however, it is important that this programme is extended to a wider group of children, and that in future it is extended to other age groups and disadvantaged sectors. it is important that it establishes community preference, that it gives priority to national and local production and that its financing is community-wide in order to contribute to greater social cohesion. this programme could be an example for a genuine policy of solidarity between countries. we hope that this will not become just another propaganda exercise and that it will be possible to reach an agreement at council level so that the funds necessary for its effectiveness at the level of the various countries are made available.
in writing. - the merits of what is at stake in this report are clear. encouraging (and in some cases simply ensuring) the consumption of seasonal fruit among the younger layers of the population has virtuous purposes. whether it's in the immediate, promoting a rich diet, or in terms of creating healthy eating habits. however, two points should be noted. by multiplying the mechanisms for guaranteeing that the fruit offered is of european production, it seems that the motive for this action is not only the diet of young people, but rather the promotion of european agriculture. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the matter. the choice between the distribution of apples or rock pears is left to the discretion of the member states. but there will always be doubts about the need for a community level for such a measure.
in writing. - we voted consistently against this report which undermines the stability pact, which does not take account of the serious economic and social situation, which ignores the worsening social and regional inequalities, which forgets the increase in unemployment and poverty. it is unacceptable that the report insists on the false autonomy of the ecb, instead of defending its democratic control and the modification of its objectives to take account of the need to focus on production, the creation of jobs with rights and the improvement of the purchasing power of the population, in particular workers and pensioners. unfortunately, the proposals put forward by our group, in particular those criticising tax and competition policies, calling attention to the growth of precarious work and low wages and to the consequences of deregulation and liberalisation, were rejected. it is also regrettable that they have rejected our proposal to repeal the stability pact and replace it with a new strategy for solidarity, development and social progress.
in writing. - gender pay discrimination is a problem throughout europe. community legislation on equal pay for men and women, in force since 1975 and revised in 2006, is clearly ineffective. we welcome the rapporteur's request to the commission for a legislative proposal by 31 december 2009 on the basis of the recommendations contained in her report. we welcome the responsible seriousness with which you have presented your recommendations, focusing them on the essential problem, in contrast to some amendments introduced by the socialists which do not contribute to solving this problem - details of political folklore or recommendations which cannot be implemented because they are within the sphere of competence of the member states. in portugal, under the current government, between 2005 and 2006, the gender pay gap increased by 8.9% in equal circumstances. the unemployment benefit paid to women in 2007 was 21.1% less than that paid to men. the amounts paid to women are below the poverty line, also in the social unemployment allowance, and decreased between 2006 and 2007. the psd meps support this report. despite the socialist folklore, we do not confuse the essential with the accessory and we will not let the accessory destroy the essential - the change of an unacceptable discriminatory situation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the bauer report on equal pay for women and men because it is not acceptable that women receive lower wages (the difference in the eu is 15%), even though they have more qualifications (58% of graduates and 41% of doctorates are women). the report sets out measures to review the current legislative framework, including suggesting the introduction of penalties for non-compliance and calling for greater dialogue with the social partners. the principle of equal pay for equal work or equal value is not just a women's struggle, but a society-wide struggle. women are needed in all areas of activity, especially in those traditionally considered to be male. it's been proven that women are good managers. in the current context, and in order to achieve the objectives of the lisbon strategy for growth and jobs, the active participation of women is essential.
in writing. - although the report was adopted with most of the amendments introduced during the debate in the committee on women's rights and gender equality, which had made it a good report, the epp did not give up on weakening its scope in the plenary vote, knowing that a qualified majority of 393 votes was needed. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be given the right to vote in the european parliament elections. but it is still a positive resolution, and we have therefore voted in favour of it. we continue to insist on the need for measures that give value to work, that give priority to employment with rights and a fair distribution of wealth, that help to overcome wage differences and stereotypes linked to tasks and sectors of activity which discriminate against women, that value occupations and activities where women predominate, particularly in trade and services and in industries such as cork, textiles and clothing, footwear, food and other sectors where very low wages are maintained in occupations and categories in which women predominate.

particularly wages, precarious work and unemployment. one of the most effective measures would thus be to increase wage incomes through a fair distribution of income. but of course other measures are immediately necessary. the fact is that the decline in production by car manufacturers has repercussions in many other sectors of activity, including the various component industries and transport itself, which can aggravate the entire economic and social situation. so, just as there were exceptional measures for the financial sector, exceptional measures are required for the automobile sector in order to safeguard employment. it cannot be accepted that the defence of production and employment should not be given the same importance as the financial sector. there must be the solidarity needed to support industry in the european union, especially in the most fragile economies and sectors. in portugal, this situation is worrying, as the sector is very dependent on the strategy of in writing. − this regulation establishes a common framework for the systematic production of community statistics on public health and health and safety at work. at present, statistical information on public health and health and safety at work is mainly collected on a voluntary basis. the adoption of this regulation will formalise the current gentlemen's agreement and ensure the continuity of data collection, as well as its quality and comparability. at first reading in 2007, the european parliament approved 12 amendments to the commission proposal. most of the amendments concerned horizontal issues such as the inclusion of gender and age in the breakdown variables and the use of additional and complementary funding provided by certain community programmes in the two areas covered by the regulation. some amendments were also adopted to the annexes on public health and health and safety at work, in particular as regards the collection of data on protection against possible pandemics and communicable diseases. following the subsequent negotiations with the slovenian presidency, almost all the amendments adopted by the european parliament were incorporated into the common position. the council also made some amendments to the text which, given their generic nature, did not raise any problems.
in writing. − this regulation establishes a common framework for the systematic production of community statistics on public health and health and safety at work. statistics should take the form of a harmonised and common data set and be produced by the european statistical system, the national statistical institutes and other national bodies responsible for the provision of official statistics. to date, statistical information on public health and health and safety at work is mainly collected on a voluntary basis. i agree with the proposed regulation because it aims to consolidate the progress made in regular data collection in the two areas in question by formalising the current informal agreement between member states, ensuring continuity of data collection and establishing a regulatory framework to improve quality standards and comparability through common methodologies. it will certainly provide greater clarity in terms of planning, sustainability and stability of european requirements for public health and safety statistics at work.
in writing. - despite the improvements introduced in this report, to which we have contributed, in particular by the adoption of our proposal to increase the starting base for modulation from eur 5 000 to eur 10 000, with the aim of promoting greater social justice in the distribution of aid to farmers, we regret that others have been rejected, although some have obtained more than 200 votes in favour, as was the case with support for sugar production in the azores. we also regret that the introduction of a simplified aid for farmers receiving amounts of eur 1000 or less was not approved, despite the fact that it received 175 votes in favour. this was a way of combating the social insensitivity of the european commission's proposal by simplifying the process and combating the bureaucracy which was used as a pretext by the european commission to propose that support below eur 250 per year be ended, which could harm some 90,000 portuguese small farmers. so, despite our final vote against the report, we will continue to defend the proposals we have put forward, because we believe that they are the ones that best defend portuguese farmers and our family farming.
in writing. - while i agree with the need to review support schemes for farmers, i believe that the commission's proposals go far beyond what is necessary, seriously undermining farmers' incomes, which are the guarantor of the maintenance of the european rural landscape and of crucial importance in view of our food sovereignty. the capoulas santos report improves the commission proposal in many respects, and the most important is the greater flexibility given to the member states in setting minimum thresholds for receiving aid. i also voted in favour of the threshold of eur 10 000 per year for the application of modulation, which favours many small and mediumsized farmers, and the non-application of the higher rates of modulation to cooperatives or other legal entities composed of several farmers which do not exceed eur 100 000 in isolation, in order to avoid unfair penalisation of farmers. the report is not the ideal one, for example because it does not allow for the redistributive effect of supplementary modulation, so i regard the final result of the vote in plenary as positive and therefore vote in favour of the legislative resolution.
in writing. − the discussion on the cap health review was an excellent opportunity to start an in-depth debate on its reform, which will take place in 2013. to succeed, we must tread a prudent path, placing the emphasis on competitiveness as well as on the environmental, social, rural development and food security dimensions. the agreement between the main political groups, largely due to the efforts of the rapporteur, mr capoulas santos, already points to some solutions and ways forward which the council is now expected to follow. while it is true that this is not a matter for co-decision today, parliament has worked in that spirit and governments should take advantage of that. i voted in favour of the package because it is important that the result achieved in the community's share of insurance premiums and the non-elimination of subsidies of lesser value, which have a great weight in countries like portugal, is achieved. as the balanced solution for modulation in support for rural development stands out. in the case of milk quotas, it is regrettable that a balance has not been achieved which would avoid the foreseeable losses for producers in regions such as the north, the centre of the country and the azores.
in writing. - we regret that our proposals, which advocated another common agricultural policy, based on support for farmers who produce to combat the instability of productive sectors due to price fluctuations, on market regulation mechanisms guaranteeing a decent income to small and mediumsized farmers, to prevent the decline of the rural world and the desertification of many regions, have been rejected. we also regret that our proposal to ensure that the european community finances public insurance in the member states to guarantee a minimum income to farmers in certain circumstances, namely public disasters such as drought, storms, hail, forest fires or animal diseases, has been rejected. we reject the announced end of the milk quota system, the renationalisation of the cap costs and the continuation of unfair aid allocations. the insistence on defending the european commission's proposals, even with some amendments, is not a strong enough basis to demand a different position from the council.
in writing. - although i believe that the amendments to the cap advocated by the commission are necessary, i believe that, as regards milk quotas, the commission's proposal is very damaging to the less competitive european regions which are more dependent on the milk sector. i therefore believe that the dismantling of milk quotas should not have been started with regulation (ec) no 248/2008 and that this dismantling should not have been continued as proposed by the commission and accepted by the rapporteur. the capoulas santos report is less negative in that it points to the preparation of a report in 2010 to analyse the situation on the milk market. i therefore do not vote against this report, but i think it is very positive that the amendments concerning sugar refining in the azores have been adopted, which may allow this activity to continue in a region with no major economic alternatives.
mr president, mr minister, mr vice-president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, unlike the last speaker, i am clearly against a strong europe and therefore support active policies for the admission of economic migrants. the only way to have a balanced immigration policy is to be strong in fighting illegal immigration and to be brave in regulating legal immigration. it is in this context that we have adopted the directive on the blue card. we do not want to limit migration to highly skilled people, however, leaving out all other migrant workers with lower qualifications. in the years ahead, both categories are essential for europe's economic and social development. and we're talking about many millions of people. for this reason, i also support the proposal for a directive to establish a single procedure for the granting of a single residence and work permit. in addition to bringing clear advantages in terms of simplification, reduction of bureaucracy and facilitation of control of their status, it allows the creation of a single, cross-cutting framework of rights which should be recognised for migrant workers legally resident in the territory of the union. with the exception of seasonal and highly skilled workers, who will have sectoral directives, all will be able to enjoy a set of labour rights equivalent to those enjoyed by nationals of the host member state. this equal treatment throughout the community should make it possible to combat any exploitation of labour and to improve the integration of these workers, thus contributing to greater social cohesion. i agree with what ewa klamt points out: the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a good one, but it is not enough to make the directive more effective. i would like to end, mr president, by applauding the efforts of mr klamt and mr gaubert and by saying that i regret that once again it in writing. regarding the 'establishment of conditions for entry and residence of third-country nationals for the purpose of highly qualified employment' in the eu (the so-called 'blue card') and the creation of a 'single application procedure for residence and work authorisation', we consider, among other important aspects, that such initiatives cannot be decontextualised from eu immigration policy. in other words, they only make sense and reveal their full scope if they are integrated into the other pillars of this policy, reaffirmed in the 'european pact on immigration': criminalisation of immigrants, detention centres, 'return' directive; border control, creation of frontex; 're-admission agreements' as a clause in 'cooperation' agreements. the so-called 'blue card', by introducing discrimination against immigrants, seeks to meet the neo-liberal objectives of the 'lisbon strategy' and the labour needs in the eu (established by quotas), reducing the immigrant to a 'labour force', promoting the depredation of the human resources of third countries - in particular their most qualified workers - and implementing dangerous centralised eu systems for the storage and collection of data on immigrants. in other words, the 'blue card' and its 'single procedure' form a pillar of the eu's inhumane immigration policy, which criminalises and expels or exploits and discards immigrants.
the european parliament has already expressed its views on the situation in the former yugoslavia, and i would like to thank the commission for its work in this area. on this same day in 1997, the convention against anti-personnel mines was opened for signature in ottawa. these instruments do not share only the date of signature. both of these conventions are not yet supported, shamefully, by countries representing a large part of humanity, such as the united states, china, india, iran, pakistan, russia and israel. the oslo convention was negotiated in dublin, and 22 of the 107 signatories are members of the european union. we hope that cyprus, poland, romania, latvia and greece will drop their reservations without delay, allowing the european union to stand united in its opposition to these weapons which indiscriminately kill and maim. these weapons are not only immoral, they are increasingly useless from a military standpoint. it is the european defence agency itself that, in its long-term vision for european defence capability and capacity needs, explains that: serious thought needs to be given to the future utility of unguided munitions, as well as cluster bombs, mines and other weapons of indiscriminate effect. the european military forces, and not only european military forces, are increasingly operating in the midst of the civilian population and the objective is less and less to destroy an easily identifiable enemy. therefore, cluster munitions are not only incompatible with humanitarian law, but have also proven to be of limited utility. international law, moral imperatives and the most basic military logic converge on the urgency of putting an end to these weapons. the oslo convention must therefore be ratified by all.

i would like to stress that, in our view, this debate should be entitled 'economic and social policy and its impact on demographic trends' rather than 'demographic trends and economic and social impact'. projections of demographic trends in a country or region should not be dissociated from the policies adopted in that country or region, as these integrate the factors that determine and condition its demographic evolution. for example, 50-year projections are made on the basis of assumptions which should be made explicit, including the economic policies that determine the advanced scenarios. in other words, in the face of the advanced projections, what should be discussed today are the consequences for the demographic evolution of unemployment, the increase in job insecurity, the deregulation of working hours, a monetary policy centred on moderation and the devaluation of wages. what should be discussed today are the consequences of the european union's interest rate policy for thousands and thousands of families who took out loans to buy housing, the consequences of the liberalization and privatisation of public services, the consequences of low reforms and pensions for the autonomy and quality of life of millions of pensioners and pensioners. what should be discussed are policies that promote the centralization and concentration of wealth and the increase in social inequalities. the debate is really about whether or not human rights are being respected, such as the right to food, employment, a decent wage, housing, health, education and leisure.

in writing. − the convention on cluster munitions (ccm), adopted by 107 countries in 2008, will start its ratification process on 3 december and will enter into force after 30 ratifications have been secured. the convention aims to prohibit the use, production, stockpiling and transfer of all categories of weapons containing cluster munitions and requires signatory states to destroy their stockpiles. the european parliament resolution we have signed calls on all signatory states to ratify the jcc as soon as possible and to take national measures to start implementing it before it is ratified. the resolution calls upon all states not to use, invest, store, produce, transfer or export cluster munitions until the entry into force of this convention. it also called on all eu member states to provide assistance to the affected populations and to support the removal and destruction of spent cluster munitions. finally, it called on all eu member states not to take any action that would circumvent or call into question the ccm and its provisions, including through a possible protocol to the convention on the prohibition of certain conventional weapons, which would allow the use of cluster munitions.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, firstly i would like to thank all the contributors for your very constructive, relevant and interesting comments. there are two specific questions that i would like to answer initially and then perhaps i will focus on the treaty of lisbon. mr jouyet has already mentioned the fact – and this is in response to mr von wogau – that the council will adopt the report on five years of the european security strategy. may i add to what mr jouyet said: of course the treaty of lisbon would also help by greatly strengthening and simplifying the institutional structure in this area. this will be an opportunity for the council to look at how to help guarantee the coherence of all our instruments and the balance between hard and soft security. that was in response to mr von wogau. mr bernard wojciechowski asked about the eastern partnership. we can report from today’s commission meeting that we adopted a proposal on the eastern partnership, including a reinforced financing of activities, which covers economic integration, mobility issues, social and economic development policy, cooperation platforms, free trade and student mobility – all of these elements that are in this eastern partnership. i welcome the fact that we have now discussed and adopted such a plan. this debate has shown that this is an important moment for the european union. it has illustrated the whole concept of sustainability. sustainable development means that we cannot put ourselves in debt and then ask future generations to come up with a solution. we cannot send problems with regard to pollution, waste and environmental or climate change to future generations to solve for us. we cannot create social problems for the next generation to sort out for us. the whole definition of sustainable development is the fact that we have to look at ways to satisfy our needs in a way that does not impact on future generations and their wish to satisfy their needs. we have three central and linked issues to resolve in the next month – which have clearly come to the fore: the economic recovery plan, where decisive eu action can have a real impact on europe’s social and economic well-being over the coming year; the climate and energy package, which will put europe on track to lead the world in defining a credible, achievable path to a low-carbon future; and the treaty of lisbon, where we need to set out the way forward to achieving a treaty so that europeans can enjoy the benefits of a more democratic and efficient european union. i fully trust my colleagues commissioner almunia and commissioner dimas to discuss the recovery plan – as so many of you have commented on that – and the climate/energy package in more detail. i understand that will happen later today and tomorrow morning, so i will make just a few more comments about the treaty of lisbon. i think that these two issues are a perfect illustration of why we need the treaty of lisbon. climate change and the economic crisis require a european union that can make the right decisions quickly, efficiently and democratically. if europe is to do the ‘heavy lifting’ to deliver such fundamental change, it needs the right tools to do that job. the commitment of this parliament and of the commission to the treaty of lisbon has always been clear. we wanted a real step forward for europe, more powers for this directly elected parliament. for national parliaments, we wanted a greater say for citizens, streamlined institutions and more clarity on who does what in europe. delaying all of this is of course a disappointment, but it should not distract us from the central objective of seeing the treaty of lisbon in force. that means that we hope to be able to pursue the goal of full ratification and it means winning the case in ireland. i was in ireland myself last month and tried to explain why i think we need the treaty. i also set out to understand why irish voters had reservations. what i heard was very much in tune with the polling evidence that we have seen. on some issues – like taxation and defence issues – voters had concerns with no real basis in the treaty. on others, like the issue of the irish commissioner, they took a worst-case scenario arising from the implementation of the treaty. many felt that information was insufficient or unclear and that a ‘no’ vote was seen as the safest option. the excellent report that we have now received from the irish parliament’s special sub-committee makes a very important contribution to clarifying these concerns and also outlining possible options for resolving them. when asked, i told them that my impression was that there was a lot of goodwill around europe to help to address the concerns of the irish. the commission intends to do what it can to work with the parliament and the irish authorities to improve communication on europe in ireland. we are working on a memorandum of understanding to make sure that we can start doing this immediately, with the government and with the people in ireland. however, i also made it clear that my impression from talking to different member states was that there was no appetite for re-opening an institutional settlement that has taken seven years of long and arduous negotiations to reach a compromise, and that the 25 member states that have now ratified the treaty, many of whom had previously ratified the constitution – and two by referendums, remember – are not going to want to start that process again. with the european parliament in writing. − the republic of korea is the eu's fourth largest non-european trading partner and the eu is the largest foreign investor in the republic of korea. the agreement seeks to ensure 'mutual recognition of competition law between the european community and south korea' as 'the most effective way of dealing with anti-competitive behaviour' and seeks to minimise 'the use of trade defence instruments between the two parties', similar to those already adopted with the united states (1991), canada (1999) and japan (2003). the european parliament, however, stresses that the agreement should be seen 'in the context of the general framework of the existing agreements between the european community and the republic of korea and those currently under negotiation, in particular the negotiations on a potential free trade agreement', and, as the rapporteur points out, 'taking into account the difficulties encountered in other interregional and bilateral trade negotiations'. that is, the european parliament is advocating 'increased market access' with catastrophic consequences for, for example, industry and for employment in shipbuilding and ship repair in portugal, with its almost complete destruction. that is why we are voting against it.

in writing. - in general, we agree with the rapporteur's proposals to improve the european commission's document on the fight against tax fraud linked to intra-community transactions. it is true that vat evasion affects not only the financing of member states' budgets but also the overall balance of the eu's own resources system, in that the reduction in the vat own resource has to be offset by an increase in the own resource based on gross national income. i also think it is not a bad thing that there is an impact assessment report on this directive, paying particular attention to the administrative costs of the new formal obligations for the persons concerned and to the degree of effectiveness of the new obligations in the fight against tax evasion. but we have serious reservations about the relative fairness of the rules and application of the existing system. that is why we abstained on this report.
in writing. - here too, we generally agree with the rapporteur's proposals to improve the european commission's document. this is the case with the proposal which insists on the need for the european commission to fully inform the european parliament of the measures envisaged, in accordance with the agreement between the european parliament and the commission on the rules for implementing council decision 1999/468/ec. i also agree that the member states and the commission should periodically carry out an evaluation of this regulation. however, i do not think the proposal that the commission should draw up a set of indicators to determine the extent to which the member states should cooperate with the commission and the other member states is sufficiently clear, even though the court of auditors has criticised the lack of effective administrative cooperation in the fight against vat evasion. the possible exchange of good practice and the development of analyses cannot justify greater taxation in areas which call into question the principle of subsidiarity. that is why we abstained.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the gurmai report on the situation of women in the balkans because it draws attention to the fact that, despite economic growth, women in this part of europe continue to face numerous forms of discrimination. i believe that the various recommendations in this report, if implemented, will be able to reverse the current situation, provide greater social protection and encourage greater participation by women in these countries. for example, measures to combat the scourge of domestic violence and the wage gap; positive discrimination measures such as the quota system; childcare facilities for children and the elderly to help eliminate restrictions on access to the labour market for these women, etc. i would also like to stress the importance the report attaches to investment in education as a way of drastically reducing stereotypes and helping to prepare future generations for a more just and equitable society.
in writing. − while there are aspects of general political opinion about the region with which we do not entirely agree, we agree on the importance of the role of women and the need to guarantee equal rights and equal opportunities for participation in the labour market, which is an indispensable condition for their economic independence, for the economic growth of countries and for the fight against poverty, to which women are more vulnerable than men. as the report notes, women have been disproportionately affected by cuts in social services and public spending, including health care and child and family care, noting that previously granted non-wage services and perks allowed women to participate in paid employment and consequently reconcile work and family life. but special measures are now needed to prevent the feminization of the lowest-paid sectors, including rural areas, the existence of the 'gender pay gap' and the need to create good quality, affordable and accessible reception facilities for children and the elderly, and the importance of the physical and psychological rehabilitation of women victims of war is emphasised.
in writing. the development of a community plan for the management of sea-crow stocks is the most feasible solution to mitigate the harmful impact of these animals on fisheries resources in some regions of the eu. sea crows, with a daily food intake of between 400 and 600 g of fish, consume more than 300 000 tonnes of fish taken from european waters every year, which is more fish than the fish produced in aquaculture by france, spain, italy, germany, hungary and the czech republic combined. although primary competence in this area lies at the level of member states and their hierarchical structures, strictly local and/or national measures are not proven to be able to reduce the harmful effect of sea crows on european fisheries and fisheries resources in a sustainable manner. a common, legally binding approach, accepted and applied at european level, therefore appears to be the ideal solution to guarantee the primary objectives of this directive, namely 'the favourable conservation status' of the bird species in question, as well as the conservation of a diverse group of fish species. the protection of the legitimate interests of fishermen and fish farmers in the economic exploitation of fishery resources is another factor of no less importance which could be safeguarded by such an approach.
