i should like to take this opportunity of speaking at the beginning of the european parliament's plenary session to express our deepest solidarity with the railway workers who have been the victims of the repression by the management board of caminhos de ferro portugueses cp. in an unacceptable manner, nine railway workers were the subject of disciplinary proceedings for dismissal initiated by the cp management board, as were three other workers at refer, for participating in a strike pick-up in compliance with and ensuring compliance with the law. we express our indignation at this attitude and demand the immediate closure of these proceedings and respect for democratic legality, workers' rights and freedom of association.
the problem of unemployment, the scourge of precarious and low-paid work and the drama of late wages is growing in the north of portugal and is threatening more and more workers. two examples i bring to you: the media reported that today 51 portuguese construction workers from the marco de canavezes area went to protest at a company in galicia, spain, which has not paid them two months' wages and holiday allowance, and these workers continue to receive no unemployment allowance either. meanwhile, quimonda, a semiconductor company in vila do conde, portugal, is increasingly concerned about the future of its 2,000 employees, as its german parent company is announcing job cuts, although it is not known which companies are affected. it is therefore imperative that these problems be tackled urgently and that the community measures recently adopted do not ignore the plight of workers and their families.
i think that an agreement with the council on this directive could have been discussed before the second reading by parliament. the fact is that, despite the efforts of the french presidency, the council has not given it any mandate to negotiate with parliament. i want to make it clear that i am prepared to review the positions adopted at first reading, but i can only do so in a responsible way within a framework of compromise, which presupposes a dialogue between the two institutions. my aim remains to reach an agreement with the council. it was not possible before the first reading, but i am confident that it can be done in the spirit of conciliation. the two most politically sensitive issues in this directive are the so-called 'guarding time' and the 'opt-out clause'. as regards the 'guarding time', i do not see any reason why the court's decisions should not be complied with. there is a solution to this problem - which i am sure will be adopted in conciliation - which solves the problems of several member states and which is accepted by the whole european medical community, which is unanimously represented today in the demonstration in front of parliament by 400 doctors representing more than 2 million doctors from all over europe. as for the opt-out, for me and in my opinion, it is an issue that has nothing to do with flexibility in the labour market. flexibility, in my view, is fully discussed through annualization of the reference period. the key point here is whether or not we want european workers to be able to work more than 48 hours a week on average per year, that is, monday to saturday, 8 hours a day, and whether this is consistent with the statements we all make here, for example, about reconciling family and working life. i would remind everyone that the legal basis of this directive is the safety and health of workers and i cannot help but thank the many colleagues in the epp for all the support they have given me in this process.
the central objective of this council proposal is to devalue work, increase exploitation and make it possible to increase profits for employers, to increase profits for economic and financial groups by means of an average weekly working time of 60 or 65 hours and to reduce wages by means of the concept of idle working time. it is one of the most visible aspects of capitalist exploitation and it calls into question everything that has been said about work-life balance. the proposal is a 100-year retreat in hard-fought rights for workers, who are people and not machines. we therefore call for the rejection of this shameful position of the european council and we call on the members to vote in favour of the workers' protest in order to avoid further serious social tensions, further setbacks and a return to a kind of slavery in the 21st century. in a time of crisis and unemployment, what is needed is a gradual reduction in working hours without loss of pay, with a view to creating more jobs with rights, and respect for the dignity of those who work.
i regret that this time is being wasted in moving towards a more profound and significant improvement of this directive on the european works council, as was already envisaged in 2001 when the menrad report was adopted, in which i myself participated. we therefore insist on the submission and vote on certain amendments aimed at strengthening the right of workers' representatives to be informed and consulted in all cases, including also the right of veto, especially in the case of restructuring and attempts to relocate companies, particularly transnational ones, where workers' rights are not respected. it is good that these proposals can be adopted here so that there is in fact a strengthening of the european works council directive.
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is with particular pleasure that i stand before you today to present the work we have done together in this own-initiative report. for me and for all those who have collaborated in the development of this process, it is clear that we have done our job. i would like to thank all of them, in particular my fellow shadow rapporteurs from the various political groups who have worked hard to reach commitments for the future, the regional development staff who are always available, in particular miguel tell cremades and elisa daffarra, the pse staff, lila and petrus, and the european commission, which, always represented by the various directorates-general that such a comprehensive report covers, has closely and continuously followed the work and worked hard to ensure that it came to fruition. i would like to thank my office, and in particular joana benzinho, and all of you for the most harmonious and structured development of coastal regions and tourism in the european union. the 27 member states of the european union have a combined coastline of over 89 000 km. it has a variety of very particular characteristics which, depending on their location, are distinguished either by their cosmopolitanism, if we are talking about cities such as lisbon, copenhagen or stockholm, or by the difficulties of being peripheral or ultra-peripheral regions, with problems of connections to the large cities or with accelerated desertification contexts, such as the algarve, liguria, the canary islands or madeira. in one way or another, everyone is identified with the concept of coast and coastal zone and experiences the advantages and disadvantages associated with them on a daily basis. according to available data, by 2010, about 75% of humanity will live in coastal areas. based on the circuits and the relationships between them, we define these zones as the 50 kilometers in a straight line that go from the coastline to the inland zones. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of the environment, and i am sure that the commission will be able to support the proposals. this is where all these people come together in search of economic opportunities and synergies, and in many cases with the sole expectation that these will revolve around tourism. the need for a pragmatic and integrated view of the impact of tourism on coastal areas was therefore clearly in our minds and led us to take action. in the context of the current financial crisis, where the impact on the real economy is becoming increasingly insurmountable, tourism appears as a sector with enormous potential to be directly or indirectly affected in a brutal way. the regions whose development is overwhelmingly or totally dependent on tourism see their activity threatened and look to the future with suspicion, especially since tourism is not currently a competence of the european union. however, concerted action can and must be taken and the spirit of the lisbon treaty reflects this same tendency. however, to wait until the treaty enters into force to start acting is to wait for the stage when we will be crying over spilled milk. the present tourist activity and the fragile reality of the regions which depend on it require us to take urgent and effective action. the fact that these are areas structurally dependent on tourism as a source of employment, although often seasonal employment, and labour-intensive activity cannot be ignored in a context of pressure on urban areas and unemployment. that is why this report which we are presenting to you here and now, which was already of the greatest timeliness and urgency when the committee on regional development decided to promote it, now assumes that it must be seen as a priority for the european commission and the european council. the commission's response to the crisis in the steel sector is to give priority to the numerous initiatives which it incorporates, as well as those for which it expressly supports and which have already been communicated by other institutions, along with the measures taken in the commission's emergency plan, of which i would stress the review of the globalisation adjustment fund, in which the issues associated with this sector and the shock to which it is currently subject must obviously be covered. it is crucial to ensure the development of new segments of the economy of these coastal zones, ensuring their social and environmental sustainability and promoting the real integration of the different sectoral policies, such as the maritime sector, transport, energy, the cohesion instruments already in place, the new quality product policy that the cap review incorporates with the announcement of the health check report and the new tourism products in these coastal zones, taking into account their crucial contribution to the european economy. the implementation of an appropriate and holistic vision for this policy should be a reality in the european union in the near future. finally, mr president, only by clearly articulating these instruments and by taking swift and effective action involving all the partners involved in the field can we ensure that we have a sustainable and future-oriented coastal tourism sector in the european union.
in writing. - the cancellation of eur 4.5 billion for the structural and cohesion funds in the community budget for 2008 justifies our vote against. the 2007-2013 multiannual financial framework is not complied with from the outset, in particular as regards the use of financial resources for cohesion policy. the 'justifications' - such as the delay in adopting and implementing the programmes - do not explain why, in two consecutive years, these amounts are either not entered in the community budget or are subsequently cancelled. the commission is also proposing to increase the number of member states that have adopted the euro by a factor of two. and this in a year of crisis. if there are difficulties in implementing each member state's operational programmes, these should be overcome (including by increasing the community co-financing rates). what is unacceptable is that 'difficulties' are used to cancel amounts which should be used to support productive sectors and promote employment with rights in the 'cohesion' countries, which include portugal. on the other hand, funds are being accumulated which are in danger of not being used because of the application of the n+2 and n+3 rules and the difficulties of these being partly co-financed by the national budgets of these countries.
in writing. − tourism is an essential factor for the socioeconomic development of the eu's coastal regions. i therefore support the creation of specific instruments that can lead to a more integrated and sustainable development strategy, reducing the seasonal nature of tourism in these regions, as this is the only way to encourage economic competitiveness, respond to social needs (creation of more stable jobs and improvement of the quality of life), while paying particular attention to the preservation of natural and cultural resources and the promotion of more responsible tourism models. although tourism is not a community competence, it is important to avoid fragmented, sectoral and sometimes inconsistent action at european level. this should ensure a general and integrated approach in the context of the various related policies (e.g. cohesion, environment, maritime, social, etc.). i have no doubt that the structural funds make a great contribution to the development of coastal regions. it is a pity, however, that the real impact of these investments is not known because of the lack of information. it is also regrettable that the operational programmes for 2007-13 contain almost no specific reference to the case of coastal areas. i support the rapporteur's intention to undertake a review to change this situation.
in writing. − issues related to the sustainable development of coastal areas are of paramount importance for eu countries which, like portugal, have regions heavily dependent on some maritime activities. among these activities, coastal tourism is a key pillar in pursuing the current objectives of the european strategy to bring europe closer to the sea. in this sense, the eu should include coastal tourism in the list of its political priorities. despite their undoubted wealth, coastal regions in europe, and in particular in portugal, suffer from serious constraints dictated by a poor approach, planning and intervention by decision-making. the eu should develop a policy that specifically addresses tourism-related issues by integrating them into broader frameworks, including: european maritime policy, marine environment directive, strategy related to integrated coastal zone management, trans-european transport network and natura 2000 environmental policy, among others. this report incorporates these and other proposals which i consider to be fundamental to the development of tourism in the eu's coastal areas and therefore deserves my vote in favour.
in writing. - although we clearly disagree with some aspects of the report, we value the overall content of the report, including the inclusion of many of the proposals we have put forward and advocated, such as: 'stresses the need to safeguard the rights of workers in the sector by promoting quality jobs and their qualification, which implies, inter alia, adequate vocational training, the promotion of stable contractual ties and a level of fair and dignified remuneration, and the improvement of working conditions.' however, we regret that other proposals have been rejected which: - considered that 'the tourism sector should be a factor contributing to territorial cohesion, economic development and employment at regional level, and stressed the need for a transversal approach to the sector in community policies and funds, in particular by creating a specific community programme, complementing the action of the member states, to promote the sector and the synergies between the various economic and social actors involved'; - and recalling that 'coastal regions characterised by tourist activity were unfairly penalized by the so-called 'statistical effect' in the current financial framework 2007-2013, and therefore calls for the adoption of compensatory measures at community level targeted at these regions', such as the algarve.
in writing. - this report on the regional development aspects of the impact of tourism in coastal areas underlines that tourism is an essential factor for the socioeconomic development of these regions of the european union. this is a very important issue, given that the european union has more than 89000 km of coastline in its member states and that, on the other hand, islands, island member states and the outermost regions are highly dependent on the tourism sector. it is therefore essential that coastal member states devise specific strategies and integrated plans at national and regional level to mitigate the seasonal nature of tourism in coastal regions and to ensure more stable employment and a better quality of life for local communities. i voted in favour of this report, which stresses the need for an integrated approach to coastal tourism in the context of the european union's maritime cohesion, fisheries, environmental, transport, energy, social and health policies, in order to create synergies and avoid contradictory interventions.
in writing. - if we consider the importance for europe of the idea of a global strategy that exploits the potential of the sea, and if we consider the economic power that tourism has and can have for european economies, and if, to these considerations, we add the need to respond not only to the concern raised by the relocation of various economic activities, but also to the challenges posed by the current economic crisis, it is easy to understand the importance of a specific strategy for tourism in coastal areas, within the framework of the global strategies for tourism and the sea. in view of these considerations, both of which are reflected in two reports to which i was a party (rapporteur on the report on the future of sustainable tourism, shadow rapporteur on the report on the european maritime strategy), this report is welcome. however, we must recognize that it is not enough to have a strategy for tourism in coastal areas that brings together the greatest common denominator of the two global strategies mentioned. more generally, it is necessary to stimulate an economic environment that is conducive to entrepreneurship, that takes advantage of this enormous potential - of these enormous potentials - by exploiting it today and doing so in a way that makes this exploitation lasting and therefore sustainable and responsible.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the christa prets report on media literacy in a digital world because i felt it was urgent to tackle this problem. in this age of digital information, info-exclusion can become a new form of discrimination and inequality. i agree with the objectives set out in the report, in particular the promotion of the democratisation of broadband internet access, the fight to reduce the disparities in this area between the various member states, and the need to invest in education and training in this area. i also think that the trend towards concentration of companies in this sector must be monitored with some caution in order to avoid oligopolistic situations, which could compromise transparency and the pluralism of information.
in writing. - i support this proposal which aims to improve the functioning of the european judicial network in civil and commercial matters and i am pleased that an agreement at first reading has been reached. i have always encouraged the establishment of closer links between magistrates and the institutional mechanisms of european judicial cooperation in order to facilitate the monitoring by those professionals of the various stages of the process of building a judicial europe, thus contributing to the consolidation of the area of freedom, security and justice and to the creation of a european judicial culture. this network is made up of contact points (judges) who cooperate with each other in order to deal with any difficulties that may arise in the context of judicial cooperation between member states, covering all areas, i.e. civil law matters and commercial law matters. i believe that it should be opened up to allow the participation of the professional orders, while efforts should be made to strengthen information to the general public. these improvements will bring clear benefits for the mutual recognition of judgments, which is, in fact, the cornerstone of judicial cooperation.
in writing. the clear lack of political will on the part of the majority of the european parliament to deepen the current directive and improve the rights and role of the european works council was once again evident in the vote in plenary. all the proposals of our group have been rejected, including the proposal for a thorough and complete revision of this directive to be initiated no later than five years after the date of entry into force of the minor amendments now introduced. they only accepted that the commission should submit a report on the application of the provisions of this directive. and then you'll see. we know that the strengthening of workers' rights will depend on the development of the class struggle. unlike at other times, when the european parliament has already accepted in non-binding deliberations the principle of the right of veto of workers' representatives, as in my report on the role of women in industry, it has now refused to include it in the directive on the european works council, which is regrettable. hence our final abstention vote.
in writing. − 'simplifying the intra-community transfer of defence-related products' is not a neutral process. the strengthening of the internal market rules in an area which was hitherto the exclusive competence of the member states is also another step in the direction of federalism, strengthening the power of the great powers to the detriment of national sovereignty. in the context of a serious international economic crisis, the development of the military-industrial complex in the eu opens up new prospects for profits for the major economic groups and the strengthening of the eu's military intervention capacity in the framework of the cfsp. the aim is to secure dominance over markets, finite energy resources and other natural resources which are crucial to the capitalist mode of production, in a context of increased international competitiveness. the way forward should be quite different, namely in the effort to reduce nuclear and conventional arsenals worldwide, in the peaceful resolution of conflicts, in respect for international law and the sovereignty of countries. the path of humanity must be that of disarmament and not that of relaunching the arms race which this proposal for a directive seeks to promote. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the matthias groote report on the typeapproval of motor vehicles and engines, as i believe that the development of common rules limiting the emission of air pollutants from motor vehicles will make a significant contribution to the protection of the environment and also to the proper functioning of the single market in the european union. i agree with the rapporteur's proposal, which calls for more ambitious limit values for particulate emissions (beyond those proposed by the european commission) to ensure a high level of protection of human health and the environment, particularly with regard to climate change mitigation.
in writing. - i am in favour of harmonising the rules for the construction of heavy motor vehicles with regard to emissions of air pollutants, because i believe that this is the best way to avoid divergent requirements being applied by the member states and to ensure the protection of the environment. the general community system of motor vehicle typeapproval exists to ensure the functioning of the internal market, which, we must never forget, is an area without internal frontiers, where there is free movement of goods, people, services and capital. there is a need to update the standards, to make them more stringent, so that all member states can ensure the production of less polluting heavy-duty vehicles and have access to the information on the repair and maintenance of those heavy-duty vehicles in a standardised format. the eu has shown a strong willingness to take the lead in tackling climate change. this report is nothing more than a new lever to supplement the fight against environmental deterioration. the new reduction of limit values for harmful emissions of carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter is the main aspect of this regulation and will certainly improve air quality in europe.
in writing. − member states have shown that it has proved difficult to apply this article effectively. the main difficulties are an administrative burden disproportionate to the amounts involved and a significant risk factor in the implementation of the programmes. it is in this context that i voted in favour of this proposal to amend and simplify this article, which deals with two points: the exclusion of operations co-financed by the esf from the provisions of article 55 and the fixing of a threshold - eur 1 million - below which projects co-financed by the erdf or the cohesion fund would be excluded from the same provisions, both as regards the calculation of eligible expenditure and monitoring. the other provisions of article 55 shall not be amended.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mrs giusepe gargani on the conditions of employment of other servants of the european communities, as i believe that the proposal to create a new category of specific staff of the european parliament, covering parliamentary assistants working at one of the three places of work of the european parliament (brussels, strasbourg and luxembourg), will make it possible to clarify and improve the current situation of these assistants, while respecting the specific nature of the duties they perform. the new system for recruiting parliamentary assistants, which creates a single system where the employment relationship is now made by direct contract with the european parliament, is essential to ensure respect for the principles of equality, non-discrimination and transparency in recruitment, as well as legal security for these workers.
in writing. the decisions of the european council - apart from all the rhetoric and demagogy that always accompany them - lay bare the real objectives and policies of the eu. after having prevented the other peoples from expressing themselves in a referendum, they now impose a new referendum on the people who have rejected this draft treaty in a sovereign and democratic way. moreover, the irish people will be faced with a referendum on the same treaty, accompanied, for the time being, by a "political commitment" to be legally implemented when croatia joins in 2010 or 2011. the aim is to impose a qualitative leap forward on neoliberalism, federalism and militarism, in favour of the interests of big business and the great powers that this draft treaty represents. moreover, the same european council is moving towards a new stage of militarization of the eu and international relations, preparing the next nato summit (april 2009) and establishing the eu as its european pillar. as we have already stressed, such decisions highlight the undemocratic character of the eu, which is inseparable from its assertion as an imperialist bloc. the so-called 'european economic recovery plan' is the same policy, giving priority to the interests of the great powers and financial capital.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected. - mr president, despite the financial and economic crisis, the european union has not wavered in its commitments on climate, and the statements by the president-elect of the united states and the position taken in poznań by china, brazil, mexico, etc. prove that european environmental pioneering is beginning to bear fruit. this parliament has clearly added value to the commission's proposal and i thank the rapporteur, mrs doyle, for her openness to the suggestions of the econ committee. it has brought to this parliament common sense solutions to the problems of carbon leakage in industry, introduced quality criteria and a 50% limit on the use of offsetting and clean development mechanisms and sought to condition the freedom of states to use auction revenues by about 50%. there is still much to be done, i hope with the active participation of this parliament. in particular, we must set out in detail the criteria for classifying sectors liable to leak carbon, the consequences for the economy and for citizens of the increase in energy prices and, above all, we must use all the european diplomatic power to ensure that the environmental commitments of our main partners are serious, measurable and comparable to our own. sectoral agreements could be a key part of this process. for now, however, we are on the right track and i think we have done a good job.
on behalf of the pse group. i would first like to thank the rapporteur, mrs hassi, very warmly for her hard work and the determination with which she negotiated the compromise. i also thank the commission and the council for their efforts. a note on what the epp shadow rapporteur said: i admit he is uncomfortable in his own group but obviously the socialists cannot be the scapegoat. this was not, in fact, an easy process, but it was worth it, if there is an international agreement to the legal commitment of member states to reach 30% reduction in co2 emissions. parliament's proposals have also improved the original text. long-term targets have been included: 50% emission reduction by 2035 and 60-80% by 2050. the commission also noted the energy efficiency and quality of cdm projects and the intention to help third countries reduce emissions and adapt to climate change. a corrective action mechanism of 1.08 was also included to punish offenders more severely. it could be better, no doubt, but the worst of it would be no commitment. the energy-climate package is a dossier of the utmost importance for citizens, the environment and the economy. the agreement reached in the council is therefore to be welcomed. the european union has set a fantastic example, as senator john kerry acknowledged in pozsnan. with this agreement, the european union has sent a very positive signal to the other international partners, showing that it continues to lead the fight against climate change and that it expects the same effort from the other parties. i hope that the european parliament will approve this package tomorrow, as the socialists will do.
mr president, our colleague ari vatanen, who is a well-known champion of motor sport, often says that we all have to die someday, but he adds that this should not necessarily happen at the wheel of a car. since 2005, however, the number of road fatalities has not slowed as it should. the 2007 figures reflect this concern. it's these ups and downs that best demonstrate how much there is still to do. we are all aware that many of the offences committed in the territory of the member states, other than that of the driver's residence, are often followed by penalties which are not enforced. the draft directive we are discussing here sets out a well-designed electronic information exchange system which aims to facilitate the crossborder enforcement of road traffic fines, focusing on the four most serious offences in terms of human lives in europe. this system is self-justifying. it must, however, preserve the guarantees of citizens regarding the protection of their personal data. the european commission's assessment of the results of its implementation is therefore indispensable and should be carried out with the utmost rigor. there is also the problem of the different legal nature of the offences depending on the member state in which they are committed. in some cases, they are merely administrative offences, in others they are criminal in nature. in some cases, they are accompanied by ancillary sanctions, such as driving bans, while in others they are not. this is not the time to go into technical details, but it is the time to call for the best possible future implementation of the directive to be studied. the rapporteur, whom i congratulate, has already suggested ways of solving the problem, including the harmonization of fines and road traffic control equipment and practices. in our view, there are also doubts as to the effective right of appeal when the driver does not comply with the fine imposed. is that right duly guaranteed where the applicant has to resort to a court and to laws other than those of his state of residence? that is a question i leave to commissioner tajani. finally, it is important that citizens who drive are properly informed of their new duties and rights. only then will they see this initiative not so much as a repressive instrument but rather as a means of encouraging safer driving behaviour and more respect for the lives of others and their own lives.

in writing. − the use of renewable energy in transport is one of the most effective instruments for the eu to reduce its dependence on oil. we also know that controlling energy consumption in europe and the use of energy from renewable sources are important parts of the package of measures needed to combat climate change. i think the most important thing in this report is to maintain the binding final target of 20% renewable energy by 2020, including the minimum target of 10% renewable in transport. for portugal, the inclusion of wave energy in the renewable energy definition constitutes an opportunity to use our energy potential to achieve the objectives. the fact that the report includes an incentive for second generation biofuels not only gives credibility to the document, but also ensures the sustainability of the use of renewables for the transport sector. in order to achieve an energy model that supports renewable energies, i consider it essential that the document encourages mechanisms for strategic cooperation between member states. this report is fundamental in itself and as part of an agreement (climate-energy package). while ensuring the preservation of environmental integrity, the agreement will make it possible to achieve the 20/20/20 targets by 2020. the targets set for the member states are ambitious but achievable.
in writing. - this is a theme of the so-called 'climate-energy package'. it deals with the promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources, covering the following sectors: electricity, heating and cooling and transport. the aim is for the eu to increase the share of renewable energy in energy consumption to 20% by 2020, setting national overall targets for each member state and also setting a target of 10% renewable energy in the transport sector by that date. according to information provided, for portugal, the target for the share of energy from renewable sources in final energy consumption in 2020 is set at 31%, taking into account the starting point (in 2005 the share in portugal was already 20,5%) and the national potential in renewable energy. the 10% target for renewable energy in transport is, by contrast, set at the same level for all member states. the fact is that, although we voted in favour of it in the end, we have serious doubts about its implementation, since it is misleading to assume that we know the extent of the renewable resources that can be exploited or that we have the technology to do so. it would be preferable to set public and private investment amounts and to promote a general survey and mapping plan for the classification and quantification of renewable energy resources.
in writing. − while the concept and system of greenhouse gas emission allowances is justified by the need to prevent chemical changes in the atmosphere with potential climate impact (precautionary principle) and the scarcity of fossil fuel sources and lack of rationality in their consumption, there are aspects to be cautious about. the issue of emission allowances and the subsequent trading of emission allowances is questionable and should be opposed because its impact on the real economy is largely uncertain, because there is still a wide margin of doubt about diversified technical solutions, and because the fate of these technical solutions is also dependent on the evolution of the financial situation in the various sectors involved (air transport, automotive, thermoelectricity production, cement plants, heavy chemicals, petrochemicals, and increasingly other energy-intensive sectors). on the other hand, the expected beneficiaries will be a few high-tech industrial sectors and a few (few) financial operators. the irreversible reduction of fossil fuel consumption is necessitated by constraints on the availability of sources and the allocation to different sectors must be achieved more out of social urgency and economic rationality than out of financial influence and profit. hence our final vote of abstention.
in writing. − the report's main thrust is to strengthen, expand and improve beyond 2012 the functioning of the ets, one of the main instruments for achieving the eu's goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions. i agree with this report, mainly because auctions are key to achieving an efficient allocation and decisive for the environmental effectiveness of the eu ets; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the drafting of the new treaty on european union. the highlight of the agreement was the increase in free licences, which is not very positive from my point of view. however, it is important to bear in mind that emissions will be reduced each year.
in writing. - we agree on the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and on the establishment of a system to do so. but we have the greatest doubts about the proposed system, which, while claiming to be based on the 'principle of solidarity between member states and the need for sustainable economic growth', then insists that it is only the countries that pay the bill, through national budgets - and not the community budget - for the unequal conditions of development in which they find themselves. by allowing the transfer of emissions between member states, either through 'auctioning' or through 'market intermediaries', mechanisms are being put in place which will accentuate the differences in economic power between member states to the benefit of the great powers. on the other hand, they outsource a significant part of their efforts to third countries, increasing international pressure on the least developed countries to surrender part of their sovereignty in exchange for (pseudo) aid, opening their economies to investment by community firms. all these measures are aimed at pressing for an international agreement which, in the context of a serious economic crisis, will emphasize the capitalist vision of the environmental front.
in writing. − with a view to eu action on climate change in a future international agreement to replace the kyoto protocol, it is essential that the eu sends a clear signal to the world and commits to effectively reducing its greenhouse gas emissions. the commission's proposal to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 10% by 2020 compared to 2005 levels for non-ets sectors is therefore of paramount importance. the targets set for each member state, with gdp per capita as the main criterion, seem fair to me. the compromise reached between the european parliament and the council, although not the ideal compromise (for example, by allowing excessive use of flexibility mechanisms), seems to me to be overall balanced and i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. the so-called 'climate-energy package' also includes a proposal for a directive on carbon capture and storage. the purpose of geological storage is to provide an alternative to the release of co2 into the atmosphere by permanently containing it underground. the commission proposes that all new power stations should have the capacity to capture co2 from the moment they are built. this technology, although controversial, can help achieve negative emissions by complementing renewable energy. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat the spread of the virus and to ensure that the virus is contained in the body. although we have doubts about some amendments, which are technically controversial, we voted in favour of the european parliament's position. but we consider the position to be too restrictive, particularly as regards the autonomy of the states, in a field where scientific and technical knowledge is still very limited. we regret that the enormous r & d & d effort which still needs to be done is not given the necessary prominence, and that the proposed timetables will be excessively ambitious unless very generous public resources are voted in a few years.
in writing. − in mitigating climate change in the eu, ccs technology holds great promise, but should not be a reason for slackening and reducing efforts to make european electricity production cleaner. the davies report is very balanced and the compromise reached between the european parliament and the council fully meets the needs of the eu. the implementation of the 12 demonstration projects is of particular importance, the results of which will guide the eu in the medium term towards the most cost-effective and environmentally efficient introduction of this technology. finally, and in view of the many remaining doubts, in particular the uncertainty as to the existence of suitable storage sites in all member states, i consider it very positive that the issue of co2 exports to third countries can be reviewed (article 35a (2)) and that economic operators are not obliged to apply ccs technology (article 32).
in writing. - i voted in favour of the dorette corbey report on the control and reduction of greenhouse gas emissions from road transport and inland waterway transport, as i consider that improving air quality and reducing greenhouse gas emissions are two crucial aspects of tackling climate change and minimising health risks. i think that the adoption of this directive is very important, as it will contribute to the reduction of co2 in the transport sector, in particular by stimulating the development of clean technologies and by setting concrete requirements for carbon emissions from the production process.
in writing. − this report from the so-called 'climate-energy package' aims to improve air quality and contribute to the fight against climate change by reducing greenhouse gas emissions from fuels used in the transport sector. the directive has so far only regulated the quality of fuels. the proposed amendment also provides for mandatory reductions in greenhouse gases from fuels. in general, the rapporteur has done a good job with amendments which we consider to be positive, with a sound general sense and properly justified, aiming at maximum efficiency, equal conditions of competition, with ambitious but reasonable objectives. it is also important that the directive is technologically neutral, since it should not involve any additional incentives in favour of a particular fuel or technology. that is why we voted in favour.
in writing. - this report is very important because in the same document it is intended to improve air quality by reducing air pollution, in particular emissions of highly toxic and polluting substances, and secondly to contribute to the fight against climate change by reducing greenhouse gas emissions from fuels used in the transport sector. this is the first time that a reduction target is applied to a specific product (fuel) based on a life cycle analysis (extraction, production, transport, distribution and end use), which underlines the importance of this directive. i would like to endorse the agreement reached between parliament and the council and stress the fact that sustainability is guaranteed in the production and use of biofuels, which is fundamental to the viability of the directive. the fuel quality directive will become a key instrument in the fight against climate change.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the guido sacconi report on emission standards for new passenger cars. given that road transport accounts for 12% of total carbon dioxide emissions in the european union, i believe that this regulation, while not part of the 'energy-climate package', is key to the eu meeting its 20% greenhouse gas emission reduction target by 2020. i congratulate the rapporteur on the decisive role he has played in the negotiations with the council and the european commission, which have resulted in a strong and balanced commitment to the benefit of the car industry, the consumer and, above all, the protection of the environment. it is therefore an ambitious but flexible model, since it seeks to meet the objectives of reducing pollutant emissions while allowing for gradual adaptation by companies in the automotive sector.
in writing. − road transport is the second largest source of greenhouse gas emissions in the eu and, above all, a sector where emissions continue to rise. the considerable progress made in automobile technology has not been sufficient to counteract the effects of increased transport demand and vehicle size. the proposal for a regulation is in line with the spirit and objectives of the eu, namely to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by at least 20% by 2020. the fact that the proposal provides for a division of labour, since each manufacturer will be assigned a precise objective to be met, is, in my view, exemplary. the penalties for manufacturers who do not meet their targets are also, in my view, fundamental. the agreement reached is, from the community's point of view, a positive one. in order to achieve the objectives which the european union has set itself in combating climate change, this regulation will certainly make a contribution.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the so-called 'energy-climate package' which includes the doyle, hassi, turmes and davies reports, because i consider that the agreement concluded between the european parliament, the council and the european commission is a balanced agreement which reconciles the protection of the environment with the legitimate interests of industry. it was important to reach an agreement at first reading, in time for the european union to present a credible proposal at the copenhagen conference in 2009 with a view to reaching an international agreement, and to continue to lead the fight against climate change.
in writing. − the reports that address the different issues of the 'climate package' provide a global approach. considering that the global increase in energy consumption will continue and that the most co2-emitting energies are the most expensive, it is easy to understand that the adoption of lower co2-emitting energies is both an environmental and an economic necessity. for this reason, it is a priority to invest in technologies that reduce energy consumption and in technological solutions that reduce emissions that will always exist. the adaptation of industries producing goods that emit more co2 and which can and should be encouraged, rather than penalized, to produce more technologically advanced goods is needed, including through public procurement rules. similarly, industries that emit a lot of co2 during their production activity need to benefit from support for research and innovation in order to be more competitive, and not from rules that penalize the production process making it unviable in europe. finally, it is noted that the need to reduce energy dependence by diversifying sources and suppliers is essential and should be exploited to stimulate energy with lower co2 emissions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of rejecting the council's position on the grounds that it does not respect the legitimate rights of workers. the european parliament's position was clear and explicit in rejecting the possibility of 65 hours a week.
in writing. - the defeat of the european council in the european parliament today is an important victory for the workers' struggle, since it has not succeeded in getting its inadmissible proposals to amend the working time directive, which call into question the gains of more than a hundred years of hard labour struggles, to pass. the cases in which they sought to extend the average working day to 60 and 65 hours a week, the creation of the concept of 'inactive working time', which would not be considered as working time, and the attack on the trade union movement are noteworthy. all of this was rejected. this is also a defeat for the ps/socrates government, which had abstained on the council's position. after today's vote in the european parliament, the council's proposal cannot enter into force. but he can open new negotiations with the ep. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. so despite the important victory achieved, the war against the council proposal and some of the reformist positions that have shown themselves to be willing to accept something in future negotiations is not over. we shall remain firm in our rejection of the proposal and call for vigilance on the part of the workers and their trade union organizations.
in writing. - balancing the right to work and rest with the needs of competitiveness and even economic viability puts us in front of the obligation to choose what we prefer. for our part, priority is given to the maintenance and promotion of employment. jobs depend on the viability of companies. for this reason, there must be sensitivity and understanding of the need to adapt labour rules to economic reality. but reality is not a sufficient criterion. over time, we have sought and claimed the success of the capitalist model, which has managed to produce more, better and offer better living conditions. those purposes stand. for this reason, just as we favour a compromise to defend the economy, we can never accept that this compromise be obtained at the expense of the essential progress achieved. there is one point, however, which is important to stress. looking at the debate in the council, it is not unremarkable that the countries which expressed the most reservations about the solution found are some of those with the worst economic performance. we have little use for rules to protect workers if there is less and less work and if we are thereby encouraging emigration to the countries of the 'opting out', whether european or non-european.
in writing. − a very ambitious target was set in 2001 to halve the number of road deaths by 2010. although the start was good, progress was slowing down and was finally nil last year (with some 43 000 fatalities still recorded on the roads of the 27 member states). it is therefore urgent to encourage the pursuit of this objective and to create a new approach to european road safety policy. the proposal we are considering is limited to the four offences which cause the highest number of accidents and deaths on the road (75%) and which are common to all member states: speeding, drunk driving, not wearing a seatbelt and disregarding a traffic light. so far, there has been a general feeling of impunity, since in the vast majority of cases any sanctions have had no effect. in a europe without internal frontiers, this is unacceptable, because we cannot encourage unequal treatment between citizens who are residents and those who are not. the law should be applied equally to all citizens! at the same time, it is essential to increase road safety in order to reduce the number of deaths on european roads.
in writing. the proposal for a directive aims to facilitate the enforcement of penalties against offenders for speeding, drunk driving, failure to wear a seatbelt or disregarding a red light (the four most serious offences in terms of loss of life at eu level) in a member state in which they are not resident. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the safety of road users is not compromised. certainly measures should be implemented to combat 'impunity' for offences committed in the territory of a country other than the country of residence of the driver. however, we believe that these objectives will not necessarily be achieved by excessive harmonization and increased safety measures at european union level (installation of monitoring and surveillance equipment on motorways, secondary roads and urban roads, creation of community electronic data transfer networks where the guarantee of adequate protection of personal data is doubtful), since it is through prevention (based on the concrete - and differentiated - reality in each country) that road safety will be promoted and the number of accidents reduced. that is why we abstained.
madam president, the sakharov prize awarded by this parliament to hu jia, on behalf of all defenders of the people in china and tibet, puts human rights at the centre of eu-china relations, regardless of the wish of rulers in europe or beijing. as other colleagues have said, the eu cannot promote the rule of law and human rights worldwide if it is not consistent in upholding them in europe and in europe’s external relations. regrettably, the 2008 annual report on human rights demonstrates that european governments and institutions persist in hiding the truth about european connivance with the abhorrent practices of the bush administration in subtracting from justice and in subcontracting torture for thousands of men, and even children, detained for years in guantánamo and in secret prisons. shamefully, reference to this in the chapter about eu troika and us consultations in human rights is limited to eu concern about ‘certain practices and policies of the us in the framework of the fight against terrorism’. this speaks volumes about double standards, hypocrisy and cover-up. until europeans assume their responsibilities and cooperate with president-elect obama to expose the truth, close guantánamo and the secret prisons, and compensate victims, europe will not regain moral authority, political credibility or efficiency in promoting human rights.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, europe is used to looking at human rights in all four corners of the world - and it is right - and that is why we are celebrating the 20th anniversary of the sakharov prize today. it does well, but it is not enough, and this is the main merit of the catania report, it is that it looks at the state of the implementation of fundamental rights in our own country. it is a political programme for the commission and the council, for today and for the years to come, because the respect of fundamental rights is the basis of the authority with which we speak about them. i'll give you an example of a concrete issue that's important. it is unacceptable that several governments are currently refusing to take in guantanamo detainees without a proven fault. my government, on the contrary, has decided to take them in, and i welcome that, but it has said that it would do so to help the american administration, and that is the problem with this argument. it's also to help washington that several governments have accepted the illegal flights. we should accept prisoners without guilt if and when they request it, not to help a state solve the problem it created.
the tampere and hague programmes, which we are discussing today with the question from mr deprez, are aimed at implementing an area of freedom, security and justice by strengthening measures to guarantee freedom, security and justice, which are essential to the process of european integration, through the indispensable cooperation between the member states and between them and the union's bodies. but our union will only truly exist when, alongside the market and economic cooperation, a common area of freedom, security and justice is achieved and when european citizens feel equally free, with their fundamental rights guaranteed, and when justice is equal for all. the development of cooperation in this area is therefore very important. but the treaty of lisbon will be decisive, since its rules in this area give autonomy and powers to the european parliament and the national parliaments.
the new multiannual programme for the area of freedom, security and justice is due to be adopted in 2009. the balance sheet of the last ten years is positive, but we must avoid the recurring temptation to give priority to the security aspect to the detriment of freedom and justice. for example, in the area of judicial cooperation, the application of the principle of mutual recognition brings enormous benefits to all those who move in this area, but it should have a corresponding effect in the adequate protection of the procedural rights and guarantees of individuals throughout the union, which has not yet happened. several information systems have been set up to enhance security, but the framework decision on third pillar data protection has still not been adopted, as mrs roure knows very well. the promotion and effective protection of fundamental rights is the basis of our democracy and must be an ever-present objective in all european policies. fundamental rights are interdependent and constitute an indivisible whole and it is in this spirit that they are enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights. that is why the amendment of the treaty of lisbon is essential if our charter is to have binding legal force. the catania report identifies a number of priorities, ranging from social rights to data protection and the protection of minority rights, among others. but at a time when we are living through a general economic crisis, i think it is important to pay particular attention to cases of extreme poverty and social exclusion which are in themselves a violation of fundamental rights. i therefore consider it essential that both the social dimension and the protection of fundamental rights be integrated into all union policies, while at the same time we must ensure systematic and rigorous monitoring of the compatibility of legislative proposals with respect for these rights.
i really appreciate your opinions. i'd like to hear your opinion on the following: the economic and monetary organization of the union will, in my view, only be complete with the common area of freedom, security and justice, that is, we need common laws that are the same for everyone and that the courts apply the laws in the same way in the union area. we are far from having a common area of freedom, security and, above all, justice. what i ask is this: if, for some reason, which we would not like to have, the treaty of lisbon does not enter into force, do you think that there is a danger to the process of european construction, and in particular to economic and monetary union?

mr president, mr vice-president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, i would first like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr javier moreno sánchez, on his excellent work, and also my colleague, mr simon busuttil, who, on behalf of the epp, has been appointed as shadow rapporteur. an area without internal borders cannot function without a sharing of responsibilities and solidarity in the management of external borders. this is essential if we are to tackle migration in a comprehensive and harmonised way, combat illegal immigration and implement integrated border management, using common human and material resources. border surveillance is not, however, limited to unauthorized border crossings. it also covers other aspects of the fight against crime, such as the prevention of terrorism, trafficking in human beings, drug smuggling and arms trafficking, thus contributing to the strengthening of internal security. i have no doubt that frontex can play a key role in this integrated border strategy of the union. after the substantial increase in its budget, which has always been demanded by this parliament and supported by commissioner barrot, i think the next step should be to review its mandate in order to close the legal loopholes in respect of rescue operations at sea, cooperation in return operations or even the possibility for third countries to make use of its equipment, which has already been mentioned by president barrot. i therefore agree with an expansion of frontex's role, albeit gradually and in accordance with concrete needs. i also recognise the importance of optimising the use of all security instruments and devices, in particular by extending their current coverage, creating synergies and strengthening cooperation with european agencies such as europol and other international organisations.
the commission's vice-president - madam president, i would like to thank mr susta for his report on the impact of counterfeiting on international trade and, of course, the committee on the internal market and consumer protection. these questions of counterfeiting and piracy deserve - as mrs korhola has just shown - our full attention and our full commitment. the commission is fully committed to promoting a high level of protection of intellectual property and its respect in third countries. in line with europe's role in the world and the commission's strategy to enforce intellectual property rights, we cooperate with partners who share our concerns. this is the case with the united states, japan, the g8 or the oecd countries. we want the most modern, innovative and quality-oriented european industrial sectors, identified as one of our main assets in terms of global competitiveness, not to be abused or even looted by third countries. the involvement of the european parliament in this matter is welcome. - thank you. - thank you. the commission has followed the drafting of mr susta's report, and i thank him for taking a very ambitious and constructive position. we take note of the proposals concerning work with china, the use of wto dispute settlement, our generalised system of preferences and the need to help our small and mediumsized enterprises more. however, in several areas the final version of the report backs down from the initial approach. the report also adopts a more reserved, more defensive tone, particularly with regard to acta, the anti-counterfeiting trade agreement. acta aims to tackle large-scale illegal activities and protect innovators in the european union. and acta is not intended to restrict civil liberties or put pressure on consumers. as the commission has repeatedly stated to the european parliament, acta will not go further than the current eu regime for the enforcement of intellectual property rights. the current regime respects fundamental rights, civil liberties, including the protection of personal data. the application of criminal sanctions will have to be negotiated by the presidency of the european union on behalf of the member states. as regards the questions put by the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, i would point out that since the high-level conference held last may with members of the european parliament, the commission has been considering the most appropriate means of supporting the member states, the judicial and police authorities, businesses and consumers in their fight against these criminals. it is true that these complex problems refer to different areas and fall within the remit of several directorates-general of the commission. we need to strengthen cooperation. at the beginning of this year - and this is important - a unit specialising in the enforcement of industrial and intellectual property rights was set up. i insist on this point. in addition, a solid knowledge base is needed to develop a sustainable strategy to combat counterfeiting and piracy. but here we have a problem: it is the production of statistics. we would need statistics to give us a precise idea of the extent and scale of the problem. the oecd has highlighted this in its report 'the economic impact of counterfeiting and piracy'. we must therefore ensure that accurate and complete information can be collected. companies have access to essential data, but some of this data is considered sensitive. it should be noted that the only statistics which member states are obliged to provide are those concerning customs seizures. similarly, it is difficult to obtain information on the number of people who have been harmed by counterfeit products. even if systems such as the community rapid alert system for consumer goods other than food (rapex) provide elements, they will not be complete. the rapex system was designed to prevent accidents caused by dangerous products. it is true that counterfeit products could fall into this category. the main advantage of rapex is that information on dangerous consumer products detected in one member state can be quickly transmitted to other member states and the commission to prevent other consumers from buying them. however, as rapex covers all dangerous consumer products, it is not necessarily the most appropriate instrument to collect information on harm caused by counterfeit products. the european accident database, which is fed by systematic monitoring of personal injuries, collects data on accidents and personal injuries reported by hospital emergency services. however, the information provided on the origin of the personal injury is sometimes too general and the level of detail is not sufficient to establish whether the damage is due to a counterfeit product. in addition, the disparity in the methods used by the member states to record the causes of accidents makes comparison and the production of statistics difficult and imprecise. it is therefore clear that we must promote the creation of rapid exchange networks through national contact points. this approach would strengthen coordination and information sharing between administrative bodies, judicial and police authorities and the economic sectors concerned throughout the european union. in this respect, the observatory could be very useful. the commission is currently examining the most appropriate practical possibilities for implementing it. in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, it is the responsibility of the member states to ensure that all products placed on the market are safe and that market surveillance is carried out effectively, but that market surveillance has not been carried out with the same rigor in all member states in recent years. the commission therefore proposed a regulation on accreditation and market surveillance, which was adopted by the council in june 2008. this regulation establishes a common framework for market surveillance. it concerns the system set up by the general product safety directive but it completes it. it lays down common requirements for market surveillance, which all member states are required to comply with. the regulation introduces a mechanism for cooperation between authorities, both at national and crossborder level. this mechanism should allow useful information to be disseminated in an efficient manner, for example to alert the arrival of dangerous goods at one of the points of entry. last july, the commission adopted a communication on a strategy for industrial property rights in europe. we therefore want to put in place an integrated strategy including non-legislative measures to strengthen the application of these provisions. this strategy will develop a new customs action plan to combat counterfeiting and piracy, to develop new approaches to improve information collection, to promote general awareness campaigns and to increase the effectiveness of cooperation networks at all levels. the council expressed its strong support for this approach. on 25 september 2008, it adopted a comprehensive european plan to combat counterfeiting and piracy. this resolution, which sets out this comprehensive european plan to combat counterfeiting and piracy, is a major political signal. this is proof that the member states attach considerable importance to the respect of intellectual property rights. in this context, the commission met the directors-general of customs of the member states at a high-level seminar held in paris on 25 and 26 november 2008. the seminar helped to define the main lines of a new customs plan to combat counterfeiting for the years 2009 to 2012. the commission will draw up this customs plan to combat counterfeiting under the forthcoming czech presidency. the commission attaches great importance to the protection and effective enforcement of intellectual property rights in third markets. it has established structured dialogues on ipr issues with its main trading partners, such as china. the commission has proposed to introduce detailed provisions on intellectual property rights, with a particular focus on enforcement in bilateral and regional trade agreements. as far as consumer awareness and warning of the increasing risks is concerned, the commission of course considers this to be a major problem. the collection and analysis of robust data is fundamental to support our work, enabling us to develop effective policies and strategies. quality information will enable us to inform and educate consumers without creating distrust and concern for sensitive product lines such as pharmaceuticals or foodstuffs. member states have an important role to play in this respect by ensuring that information is exchanged. i would like to conclude by apologizing, madam president, for being a little long. we want to support member states to be able to contribute more effectively to promoting innovation, protecting consumer health and safety, and we need a comprehensive approach. the commission is therefore concentrating its efforts on the establishment of a mechanism to develop knowledge and cooperation between member states, consumers and businesses. you see, mr. susta, your report is timely. we are now at the heart of a subject which has always been of particular concern to me personally, namely counterfeiting. we cannot defend a europe of innovation if we do not fight counterfeiting effectively. i therefore thank the european parliament for its sensitivity to this major problem. i thank you for your attention and now, madam president, i shall listen carefully to the speeches of the members.
madam president, the european parliament's resolution of 13 december 2007 on the textile sector pointed out that half of the european customs cases concerning counterfeiting concern textiles and clothing. the same resolution underlined the need to apply binding rules on the labelling of textiles imported from third countries, and called on the council to approve the pending proposal for a regulation on the indication 'made in' as a way of increasing consumer protection and supporting european industry. the truth is that a proposal from the european commission in this regard, although insufficient, has been making headway since 2005. so the question we are asking is: when will the european union establish rules for indicating the origin of imports or of products manufactured in the different countries within it?
madam president, mr vice-president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, the phenomenon of counterfeiting is a dangerous attack on the most legitimate socioeconomic interests in the european union, it undermines the competitiveness of companies, it undermines employment, it puts consumers' safety and health at risk and it seriously harms the member states and the european union itself. so it must be vigorously fought. the european union, by virtue of the transparency and openness of its market, its position as the world's second largest importer of goods and services and the nature of its economic specialisation in high value-added products, is particularly exposed to the dangers of counterfeiting. the negative effects of the crisis are felt throughout the economic fabric, but they are particularly acute in small and mediumsized enterprises, which are naturally less prepared to face such a serious threat. the fight against this particularly dangerous crime requires increased cooperation, both within the european union and in external relations with other countries or regional groups also facing this problem. at the internal level, the measures to be taken should focus on two areas: the progressive harmonization of legislation between the various member states, especially in the criminal field, and the strengthening of cooperation in the customs field. given the special situation of small and mediumsized enterprises, it is necessary to set up a technical assistance service for these enterprises, because they are less prepared to deal with such issues. only then will they be able to defend their rights. at the broader international level, ongoing initiatives, both in the field of bilateral agreements and in the wider field of multilateral regulation of international trade, should be pursued, thus contributing to strengthening the role that the world trade organisation, through its dispute settlement body, can and should play in this area. counterfeiting calls into question some of the foundations of our model of economic and social organisation. it calls into question investment in research and innovation, devalues intelligence and the skill effort, favours organised crime and clearly undermines the rule of law. it is therefore an absolute imperative for all member states of the european union to combat it.

in writing. the eu has decided to set up a new facility for rapid response to food price rises in developing countries (the 'food facility') with a budget of €1 billion for three years. initially, it was proposed to finance the food facility by using the margin of heading 2 (agriculture) of the multiannual financial framework, then by revising the ceiling of heading 4 (external policy) of the mff, and finally it was defined that it would be financed through the flexibility instrument, the reserve for emergency aid and a reallocation under heading 4 of the stability instrument. the amendment to the interinstitutional agreement aims to increase the funds available in the emergency aid reserve for 2008 to eur 479 218 000 (current prices) to finance this initiative. we welcome the stated objectives of this initiative and reaffirm that it should not be reduced to a mere counterpart or condition for the eu to impose an agreement in the wto or economic partnership agreements with the acp countries, nor should it ignore the reduction in eu development aid, nor the huge sums of the relaunch of the arms race and the militarisation of international relations that it entails.
in writing. - this new amending budget proposal concerns the mobilisation of the solidarity fund (about eur 7.6 million, against a loss of eur 176 million) for cyprus following a period of severe drought. the commission notes, however, that 'in view of the identification of surplus appropriations under cohesion fund heading 13 04 02, no new payment appropriations will be needed to finance the eu solidarity fund payments to cyprus'. in other words, it is from cohesion policy that the money to deal with this natural disaster will come. the 'surplus allocations' in the cohesion fund are due (among many other reasons) to the delay in implementing programmes in the so-called 'cohesion' countries, so instead of applying a concept of 'solidarity' which could penalise the economically less developed countries, what should have been done was to take decisions to avoid the continued under-implementation of structural and cohesion policies. we also draw attention, as in the past, to the need to speed up the procedures for mobilising the solidarity fund; to ensure that regional disasters remain eligible; and to recognize, indeed, the specific nature of mediterranean natural disasters such as drought and fires.
in writing. − the increase in food prices in developing countries is a matter of the utmost importance and requires rapid action by the union to counterbalance the adverse effects on the most deprived populations. in this report, parliament therefore proposes to finance eur 420 million for a rapid response to the consequences of this situation. in particular, the flexibility instrument provided for in the 2006 interinstitutional agreement needs to be mobilised. through this instrument, europe has envisaged the possibility of mobilising a flexibility instrument to allow the financing of specifically identified expenditure which cannot be financed within the available ceilings of one or more headings of the multiannual financial framework. the situation under consideration is entirely in line with the institutional requirements and, without any doubt, with the foundations of the union's solidarity policy, and has therefore not raised any doubts for decision-makers in view of the seriousness of the situation. time is of the essence and our swift action and response could be the difference between an accident and a human tragedy with incalculable consequences for the future development of these populations.
in writing. − in the current financial period (2007 and 2008), the solidarity fund has been mobilised 9 times (germany: €166.9 million; united kingdom: €162.3 million; greece: €99 million; france: €17.1 million; hungary: €15 million; slovenia: €8.2 million and cyprus: €7.6 million), amounting to some €477.3 million against a maximum of €1 billion per year. beyond the obvious need for this support - and without going into the procedure for activation and (late) making available - there is the question of the origin of the financial means mobilised, particularly in the light of this draft amending budget. in other words, apart from the urgency of the support to be provided in the event of natural disasters, the origin of these financial means may be called into question, all the more so if they are 'subtracted' from cohesion policy and not, for example, from the funds devoted to the progressive militarisation of the eu. that is to say, we believe that cohesion policy should be safeguarded. finally, as we have done on other occasions, we stress the need to introduce changes in the solidarity fund in order to speed up the procedures for its mobilisation, ensuring that regional disasters remain eligible, and effectively recognising the specific nature of mediterranean natural disasters such as drought and fires.
