in writing. − while this report contains some important and correct recommendations in advocating greater economic and social support, complementary measures, the integration of migrants and minorities, in highlighting the importance of sport for education and training, in insisting on greater support for pre-primary education, teachers and pupils, particularly in primary and secondary education, it supports the european commission's proposals, including the lisbon strategy, and insists on the implementation of bologna, ignoring its practical consequences. the commission's communication on lifelong learning for knowledge, creativity and innovation not only accepts the picture of progress made and the areas where progress is still insufficient, but also proposes measures to change the situation in line with objectives which are not always the most correct, because they accept and insist on neoliberalism applied to education. it is thus a political declaration which can also be seen as a road map for the years ahead. hence our basic disagreement. we cannot accept that, for example, the modernisation of higher education should be complementary to the reforms in the bologna process and that private sector sponsorship should be increased, especially when public higher education is being stifled, as is the case in portugal.
in writing. the directive on the safety of toys represents a major step forward in ensuring the safety of our children. it was absolutely necessary to broaden the scope and clarify the legislation on such an important matter as this. aspects such as the holding of producers and importers to account and the judicious increase in prohibited substances are evidence of the strictness with which this matter has been dealt with. i would like to commend the rapporteur for having succeeded in establishing the rules to ensure the safety of children, taking into account the survival and balance of small and mediumsized enterprises in this sector. however, it is necessary to reflect on the increased responsibility of the member states that arises from this legislation. the aim of this directive - the safety of our children - requires that the member states meet their obligations, which are now being strengthened in terms of market surveillance. in view of the portuguese case and the successive failures of the responsible (state-sponsored) agency to monitor this matter, i urge the member states to take up their responsibilities properly. it is essential that the advances in safety introduced by this directive be matched by effective and responsible national enforcement action.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the marianne thyssen report on the safety of toys, as i believe that the compromise text adopted will make it possible to strengthen the safety requirements for toys by extending the responsibility of producers and importers in the marketing of products and increasing the obligations of market surveillance by the member states. i regret, however, the rejection of amendment no 142, which required that toys be assessed by a third party laboratory before being placed on the market in order to ensure that they were in conformity.
in writing. the aim of this proposal for a directive is to strengthen the safety requirements for toys, particularly as regards the use of chemical substances and the requirements relating to electrical properties. the new legislation also adapts the physical and mechanical properties to reduce the risk of suffocation. provisions are also made to strengthen state controls and to impose new obligations on manufacturers. the aim is to improve the existing directive, taking into account the new safety risks that may arise as a result of the development and marketing of new types of toys, possibly made with new materials. however, many doubts arose in the debate and vote on the proposals for this directive. the european commission guarantees were not available at the time of the vote, which caused a minor incident. on the other hand, some experts consider it serious to maintain requirements which do not completely eliminate the use of carcinogenic, mutagenic or toxic substances for reproduction (so-called cmr substances), although they establish new restrictions. there is also controversy about the limit values for metals, such as arsenic, cadmium, chromium, lead, mercury and tin, which are particularly toxic and should not be used in the components of toys to which children have access. that is why i am voting against our group.
in writing. the european parliament could not have marked international migration day in a worse way by approving a report praising the strengthening of the so-called 'frontex' and 'welcoming the adoption of the european pact on immigration and asylum by the european council'. like frontex, the inhumane 'return directive' is one of the central pillars of the eu's criminalising, security, exploitative and elitist immigration policy. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment. the ps members of the ep may well try to whitewash the behaviour of their party and government. the fact is that the council of the eu voted in favour of this shameful directive. the need now arises to combat it in the process of transposition in portugal, which requires denouncing the inhuman and human rights-violating nature of this directive and the mobilisation of all those who are fighting for the defence of the human dignity of immigrants. the cfp will continue to be at the forefront of this fight, pushing for the rejection of the shameful content of this directive and for the ratification of the un international convention on the protection of the rights of all migrant workers and members of their families.
in writing. the growing relevance of intellectual property law reflects an inescapable paradigm: the modern economy values and protects the knowledge on which it is based. industries, regardless of their sector, rely heavily on the holding of exclusive rights to exploit a specific know-how. counterfeiting is often condemned because the damage it causes to legitimate industry has obvious implications for employment, research and development. its effects are worrying in my country. moreover, the issues of counterfeiting today outweigh the economic damage. the harmfulness of counterfeiting has new frontiers - where once there were imitations of tailor's clothes, now there are harmful counterfeits of medicines and food products. the unwarned consumer does not question the risk he is taking. it is essential to fight against counterfeiting. that is why we call for stronger sanctions, coordination and cooperation between the competent authorities and the harmonisation of the legal principles applied in the partner jurisdictions. in addition to creating effective mechanisms to deal with potential conflicts and litigation, we need something like the anti-counterfeiting trade agreement, a multilateral international agreement under discussion, with the legal innovation needed to adapt effective enforcement and repression practices.
in writing. - the resolution adopted by the european parliament incorporates concerns and proposals which we share, although we disagree with some of its points. the fight against counterfeiting should undoubtedly be a priority. however, although the resolution considers that 'iprs, including geographical indications and designations of origin, are not always effectively protected by the european union's trading partners', it should be stressed that the eu itself is not setting an example, as a proposal for a regulation on 'made in' is currently blocked in the council and the council has not adopted any other measure aimed at applying binding rules on the indication of the origin of products to imports from third countries. we will continue to work towards community action to encourage each country to take and implement measures to combat counterfeiting of trade marks and smuggling, and specific checks at customs to identify products accompanied by false declarations of origin or which violate the rules on the protection of trade marks. each country should implement measures to defend itself against aggressive exports by systematically using control and surveillance of imported goods, with the use of safeguard clauses where necessary.
in writing. − the european area of justice has been developing (either through the mutual recognition of judicial decisions or through the creation of a culture of judicial cooperation between the competent authorities) in order to accompany the free movement of citizens within the european area. it is estimated that some 10 million people are involved in crossborder litigation in europe, with all the problems that underlie it such as language issues, distance, different legal systems, etc. the use of information and communication technologies in the administration of justice ultimately offers new solutions, improves the functioning of justice (better accessibility and efficiency), contributes to the streamlining of procedures and reduces costs. the proposed e-justice strategy has as its primary objective to enhance the effectiveness of justice across europe for the benefit of citizens. however, the potential scope of e-justice can be very wide, and the scope of its action needs to be clearly defined so as not to jeopardise the effectiveness and credibility of eu action. any developments should be made gradually and in line with the progress of the european judicial area and technological developments. i support the call on the commission to prepare a european action plan and to create a european e-justice portal.
in writing. - since it is impossible to comment on the (intentional) amalgamation of this report, we will focus on what we consider to be its main objective: whitewashing the interference of the eu's great powers in third countries, under the concept of the 'responsibility to protect'. the report, stressing the sovereignty of states, then considers that 'however, ... in cases where governments prove incapable of or refuse to guarantee such protection, the responsibility to take appropriate measures becomes a collective responsibility at the level of the entire international community', and these should 'have a preventive as well as a reactive character and imply the use of coercive military force', stating that the latter will be used 'only as a last resort', language not betraying the intention. and, in the same vein, there can be no doubt, it "calls" for "the principle of non-intervention to yield to the international responsibility to protect", considering that "the restoration of peace and state-building are processed in two phases: the stabilization phase in which the emphasis is placed on security, law and order and the provision of basic services; and the second phase of state-building which focuses on governance and the institutions that will implement it". and so we have the be-a-ba of the booklet that opens the door to meddling and colonialism.
the european parliament, like other countries which are taking the path of affirming and defending their sovereignty and national independence, that is, the right to decide their own present and future, and which are promoting a project of emancipation and social progress and solidarity with the peoples of the world, is once again engaging in an unacceptable and despicable act of interference, this time in relation to nicaragua. this debate and this resolution are only intended to give blatant support to those who are fuelling and promoting a process of interference and attempts to destabilize a democratic and sovereign state such as nicaragua. instead of distorting reality and facts and legitimately giving conspiratorial lessons on democracy to nicaragua, the european parliament should have denounced the anti-democratic operation of the european union to impose a proposal for a european treaty which has already been rejected, in profound disregard of the democratic and sovereign decision expressed by the french, dutch and irish peoples. instead of interfering in what only the nicaraguan people can decide, the european parliament should have rejected the inhumane return directive, which violates the human rights of immigrants, many of them from latin america, and denounced the european union's complicity in the criminal flights of the cia. instead of following the united states' manoeuvres of interference, the european parliament should denounce the unacceptable blackmail of the european union towards nicaragua and demand that the commitments it has made to that country be respected. what really bothers the promoters of this initiative is that nicaragua is determined to improve the living conditions of its people in food, health, education, supporting the most disadvantaged population. the best indication of this manoeuvre of interference by the european parliament is the real recognition and solidarity of the peoples of latin america with nicaragua. so, once again, stop pretending that you can lecture the world.
madam president, we are concluding a debate of the utmost importance which, as has already been said here, is a debate we should have had a long time ago. russia is essential to us in every way, but above all as a country where human rights must be respected. these human rights necessarily include the denial of xenophobia and homophobia, and i would appeal to all colleagues to make explicit reference to these two enormous scourges in russia, which are rightly considered as such in the resolution being proposed, and not to accept withdrawing them.
